# السابع: السجود وأقله مباشرة بعض جبهته مصلاه فإن سجد على متصل به جاز إن

لم يتحرك بحركته ولا يجب وضع يديه وركبتيه وقدميه في الأظهر.
# قلت: الأظهر وجوبه والله أعلم ويجب أن يطمئن وينال مسجده ثقل رأسه وأن لا

يهوى لغيره فلو سقط لوجهه وجب العود إلى الاعتدال وأن ترتفع أسافله على

أعاليه في الأصح وأكمله يكبر لهويه بلا رفع ويضع ركبتيه ثم يديه ثم جبهته

وأنفه ويقول: سبحان
# 
# ربي الأعلى ثلاثا ويزيد المنفرد اللهم لك سجدت وبك آمنت ولك أسلمت سجد

وجهي للذي خلقه وصوره وشق سمعه وبصره تبارك الله أحسن الخالقين  ويضع يديه

حذو منكبيه وينشر أصابعه مضمومة للقبلة ويفرق ركبتيه ويرفع بطنه عن فخذيه

ومرفقيه عن جنبيه في ركوعه وسجوده وتضم المرأة والخنثى.
# الثامن: الجلوس بين سجدتيه مطمئنا ويجب أن لا يقصد برفعه غيره وأن لا

يطوله ولا لاعتدال وأكمله يكبر ويجلس مفترشا واضعا يديه قريبا من ركبتيه

وينشر أصابعه قائلا رب اغفر لي وارحمني واجبرني وارفعني وارزقني واهدني

وعافني ثم يسجد الثانية كالأولى والمشهور من جلسة خفيفة بعد السجدة الثانية

في كل ركعة يقوم عنها.
# التاسع والعاشر والحادي عشر: التشهد وقعوده والصلاة على النبي صلى الله

عليه وسلم فالتشهد وقعوده إن عقبهما سلام ركنان وإلا فسنتان وكيف قعد جاز

ويسن في الأول افتراش فيجلس على كعب يسراه وينصب يمناه ويضع أطراف أصابعه

للقبلة وفي الآخر التورك وهو كالافتراش لكن يخرج يسراه من جهة يمينه ويلصق

وركه بالأرض والأصح يفترش المسبوق والساهي ويضع فيهما يسراه على طرف ركبتيه

منشورة الأصابع بلا ضم.
# قلت: الأصح الضم والله أعلم ويقبض من يمناه الخنصر والبنصر وكذا الوسطى

في الأظهر ويرسل المسبحة ويرفعها عند قوله إلا الله ولا يحركها والأظهر ضم

الإبهام
# 
# إليها كعاقد ثلاثة وخمسين والصلاة على النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم فرض في

التشهد الأخير والأظهر سنها في الأول ولا تسن على الآل في الأول على الصحيح

وتسن في الآخرة وقيل: تجب وأكمل التشهد مشهور وأقله التحيات لله سلام عليك

أيها النبي ورحمة الله وبركاته سلام علينا وعلى عباد الله الصالحين أشهد أن

لا إله إلا الله وأشهد أن محمدا رسول الله وقيل: يحذف وبركاته والصالحين

ويقول: وأن محمدا رسوله.
# قلت: الأصح وأن محمدا رسول الله وثبت في صحيح مسلم والله أعلم وأقل

الصلاة على النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم وآله اللهم صل على محمد وآله والزيادة

إلى حميد مجيد سنة في الآخر وكذا الدعاء بعده ومأثوره أفضل ومنه اللهم اغفر

لي ما قدمت وما أخرت الخ ويسن أن لا يزيد على قدر التشهد والصلاة على النبي

صلى الله عليه وسلم ومن  عجز عنهما ترجم ويترجم للدعاء والذكر المندوب

العاجز لا القادر في الأصح.
# الثاني عشر: السلام وأقله السلام عليكم والأصح جواز سلام عليكم قلت:

الأصح المنصوص لا يجزئه والله أعلم وأنه لا تجب نية الخروج وأكمله السلام

عليكم ورحمة الله مرتين يمينا وشمالا ملتفتا في الأولى حتى يرى خده الأيمن

وفي الثانية الأيسر ناويا السلام على من عن يمينه ويساره من ملائكة وإنس

وجن وينوي الإمام السلام على المقتدين وهم الرد عليه.
# الثالث عشر: ترتيب الأركان كما ذكرنا فإن تركه عمدا بأن سجد قبل ركوعه

بطلت صلاته وإن سها فما بعد المتروك لغو فإن تذكر قبل بلوغ مثله فعله وإلا

تمت به ركعته
# 
# وتدارك الباقي فلو تيقن في آخر صلاته ترك سجدة من الأخيرة سجدها وأعاد

تشهده أو من غيرها لزمه ركعة وكذا إن شك فيهما وإن علم في قيام ثانية ترك

سجدة فإن كان جلس بعد سجدته سجد وقيل: إن جلس بنية الاستراحة لم يكفه وإلا

فليجلس مطمئنا ثم يسجد قيل: يسجد فقط وإن علم في آخر رباعية ترك سجدتين أو

ثلاث جهل موضعها وجب ركعتان أو أربع فسجدة ثم ركعتان أو خمس أو ست فثلاث أو

سبع فسجدة ثم ثلاث.
# قلت: يسن إدامة نظره إلى موضع سجوده وقيل: يكره تغميض عينيه وعندي لا

يكره إن لم يخف ضررا والخشوع وتدبر القرآن والذكر ودخول الصلاة بنشاط وفرغ

قلب وجعل يديه تحت صدره آخذا بيمينه يساره والدعاء في سجوده وإن يعتمد في

قيامه من السجود والقعود على يديه وتطويل قراءة الأولى على الثاينة في

الأصح والذكر بعدها وأن ينتقل للنفل من موضع فرضه وأفضله إلى بيته وإذا صلى

وراءهم نساء مكثوا حتى ينصرفن وأن ينصرف في جهة حاجته وإلا فيمينه وتنقضي

القدوة بسلام الإمام فللمأموم أن يشتغل بدعاء ونحوه ثم يسلم ولو اقتصر

إمامه على تسليمة سلم ثنتين. والله أعلم.
#

| باب شروط الصلاة
# خمسة
# معرفة الوقت والاستقبال وستر العورة وعورة الرجل ما بين سرته وركبته وكذا

الأمة في الأصح والحرة ما  سوى الوجه والكفين وشرطه ما منع إدراك لون
# 
# البشرة ولو بطين وماء كدر والأصح وجوب التطين على فاقد الثوب ويجب ستر

أعلاه وجوانبه لا أسفله فلو رؤيت عورته من جيبه في ركوع أو غيره لم يكف

فليزره أو يشد وسطه وله ستر بعضها بيده في الأصح فإن وجد كان في سوأتيه
chapters.anchors:
- Root: س-ج-د (s-j-d)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To prostrate, to place the forehead upon the ground in humble submission; the act of lowering oneself in worship.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Sujūd is the physical manifestation of servitude (ʿubūdiyyah) before Allah, the highest form of bodily humility in prayer.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal (ḥaqīqah) — physical prostration; metaphorical (majāz) — complete submission of the soul.
- Root: ج-ل-س (j-l-s)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To sit, to assume a seated posture; jalsah in prayer denotes the prescribed sitting between prostrations.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): The seated position in prayer signifies composed stillness (ṭumaʾnīnah) and attentiveness before the Divine.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal — physical sitting; metaphorical — steadfastness in devotion.
- Root: ش-ه-د (sh-h-d)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To bear witness, to testify; tashahhud is the verbal testimony of faith in the prayer.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): The testimony of tawḥīd and prophethood, the verbal seal of one's servitude.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal — legal testimony; metaphorical — the soul's affirmation of divine unity.
- Root: س-ل-م (s-l-m)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Peace, safety, salutation; taslīm is the concluding salutation of prayer.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): The salutation of peace as the exit from the sacred state of prayer, invoking divine safety upon angels and fellow beings.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal — greeting of peace; metaphorical — the soul's release from ritual consecration.
- Sībawayh Rule: Conditional Clauses (al-Sharṭ wa al-Jawāb) — The text employs conditional constructions (e.g., "if he prostrated upon something connected to him, it is permissible if it does not move with his movement") requiring precise parsing of protasis and apodosis to determine legal rulings.
chapters.translation:
I say: The seventh [pillar] is the prostration (sujūd), and its minimum is that one directly place part of his forehead upon his place of prayer. If he prostrates upon something connected to him, it is permissible provided it does not move with his movement. It is not obligatory to place his hands, knees, and feet [upon the ground] in the more apparent (al-aẓhar) opinion.

I say: The more apparent (al-aẓhar) opinion is that it is obligatory, and Allah knows best. It is obligatory to be tranquil (ṭumaʾnīnah), and that the weight of his head reach his place of prostration, and that he not intend something else by his descent. If he falls upon his face, he must return to the upright position, and that his lower parts be raised above his upper parts in the most correct (al-aṣaḥḥ) opinion. Its most complete form is that he say the takbīr for his descent without raising [his hands], and place his knees, then his hands, then his forehead and nose, and say: "Glory be to my Lord, the Most High" (subḥāna rabbī al-aʿlā) three times. The one praying alone adds: "O Allah, to You I have prostrated, in You I have believed, and to You I have submitted. My face has prostrated to the One who created it and fashioned it, and opened its hearing and sight. Blessed is Allah, the Best of Creators." He places his hands level with his shoulders, spreads his fingers, joined together, toward the qiblah, and separates his knees, and raises his belly from his thighs and his elbows from his sides in his bowing (rukūʿ) and prostration. The woman and the hermaphrodite draw themselves together [in a compact posture].

The eighth [pillar] is the sitting between the two prostrations with tranquility (ṭumaʾnīnah). It is obligatory that he not intend by his rising anything other than [the prayer], and that he not prolong it, nor [prolong] the upright position. Its most complete form is that he say the takbīr and sit in the iftirāsh posture, placing his hands near his knees, spreading his fingers, saying: "My Lord, forgive me, have mercy upon me, restore me, raise me, provide for me, guide me, and grant me well-being." Then he prostrates the second [prostration] like the first. The well-known (al-mashhūr) [opinion] is that there is a brief sitting after the second prostration in every unit (rakʿah) from which he rises.

The ninth, tenth, and eleventh [pillars]: the testification (tashahhud), its sitting, and the blessing upon the Prophet ﷺ. The testification and its sitting — if the salutation (salām) follows them, they are pillars (arkān); otherwise, they are Sunnah. However he sits, it is permissible. It is Sunnah in the first [sitting] to adopt the iftirāsh posture, so he sits upon his left foot and erects his right [foot], placing the tips of his toes toward the qiblah. In the last [sitting], [he adopts] the tawarruk posture, which is like the iftirāsh except that he brings out his left [foot] from his right side and presses his buttock to the ground. The more correct (al-aṣaḥḥ) opinion is that the one who is preceded [in prayer] (al-masbūq) and the one who errs adopt the iftirāsh. In both [sittings], he places his left hand upon the edge of his left knee, with fingers spread without joining.

I say: The more correct (al-aṣaḥḥ) opinion is to join [the fingers], and Allah knows best. He clenches from his right hand the little finger and the ring finger, and likewise the middle finger in the more apparent (al-aẓhar) opinion, and releases the index finger, raising it when he says "except Allah" (illā Allāh), and does not move it. The more apparent (al-aẓhar) opinion is to join the thumb to it, like one who is contracting fifty-three. The blessing upon the Prophet ﷺ is obligatory (farḍ) in the final testification, and the more apparent (al-aẓhar) opinion is that it is Sunnah in the first. It is not Sunnah to [bless] the family (āl) in the first [testification] according to the sound (al-ṣaḥīḥ) opinion, and it is Sunnah in the last; and it was said: it is obligatory. The most complete testification is the well-known (mashhūr) one, and its minimum is: "The greetings are for Allah. Peace be upon you, O Prophet, and the mercy of Allah and His blessings. Peace be upon us and upon the righteous servants of Allah. I bear witness that there is no god but Allah, and I bear witness that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah." It was said: one may omit "and His blessings" and "the righteous," and say: "and that Muhammad is His Messenger."

I say: The more correct (al-aṣaḥḥ) opinion is "and that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah," and this is established in Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim, and Allah knows best. The minimum of the blessing upon the Prophet ﷺ and his family is: "O Allah, bless Muhammad and the family of Muhammad" (Allāhumma ṣalli ʿalā Muḥammad wa ʿalā āli Muḥammad). Adding "the Praiseworthy, the Glorious" (ḥamīd majīd) is Sunnah in the last [testification], as is the supplication (duʿāʾ) after it, and the transmitted (maʾthūr) supplication is superior. Among it is: "O Allah, forgive me what I have done before and what I have deferred," etc. It is Sunnah that he not exceed the measure of the testification and the blessing upon the Prophet ﷺ. Whoever is unable to perform them may substitute with translation (tarjamah). One may translate the recommended supplication and remembrance if unable — not the one who is able, in the more correct (al-aṣaḥḥ) opinion.

The twelfth [pillar] is the salutation (salām). Its minimum is "Peace be upon you" (al-salāmu ʿalaykum). The more correct (al-aṣaḥḥ) opinion is that "Peace be upon you" (salāmun ʿalaykum) is permissible. I say: The more correct (al-aṣaḥḥ) opinion, according to the explicit text (al-manṣūṣ), is that it does not suffice, and Allah knows best. It is not obligatory to intend the exit [from prayer]. Its most complete form is "Peace be upon you and the mercy of Allah" twice, to the right and to the left, turning in the first until his right cheek is seen, and in the second until his left cheek [is seen], intending by the salutation those on his right and left from among the angels, humans, and jinn. The imam intends the salutation upon the followers, and they are obligated to respond to him.

The thirteenth [pillar] is the order (tartīb) of the pillars as we have mentioned. If one deliberately omits it, such as prostrating before bowing, his prayer is invalidated. If he errs, then whatever came after the omitted [pillar] is void. If he remembers before reaching its equivalent [in the subsequent unit], he performs it; otherwise, his unit (rakʿah) is completed by it, and he makes up the remainder. If he is certain at the end of his prayer that he omitted a prostration from the last [unit], he prostrates it and repeats his testification; or if from another [unit], a full unit is incumbent upon him. Likewise, if he doubts concerning them. If he knows during a second standing that he omitted a prostration — if he had sat after his prostration, he prostrates; it was said: if he sat with the intention of rest (istirāḥah), it does not suffice him; otherwise, let him sit with tranquility, then prostrate. It was said: he prostrates only. If he knows at the end of a four-unit prayer that he omitted two or three prostrations without knowing their location, then two or four units are obligatory; if [he omitted] a prostration then two units; or five or six, then three; or seven, then a prostration then three.

I say: It is Sunnah to continuously direct one's gaze to the place of his prostration. It was said: it is disliked (makrūh) to close one's eyes, but in my view it is not disliked if one does not fear harm. [It is Sunnah to observe] humility (khushūʿ), reflection upon the Qurʾān and remembrance, entering the prayer with vigor and an empty heart, placing his hands beneath his chest, taking his left with his right, supplication in his prostration, and that he lean upon his hands when rising from prostration and sitting, and the prolongation of the recitation of the first [unit] over the second in the more correct (al-aṣaḥḥ) opinion, and the remembrance after it, and that he move to the voluntary prayer from the place of his obligatory prayer — and the best is in his house. When women pray behind them, they remain until the men depart. And that he depart in the direction of his need, otherwise to his right. The following (iqtidāʾ) is terminated by the salutation of the imam, so the follower may occupy himself with supplication and the like, then give the salutation. If his imam limits himself to one salutation, he gives two. And Allah knows best.

| Chapter on the Conditions of Prayer

There are five [conditions]: knowledge of the time, facing the qiblah, covering the nakedness (ʿawrah). The nakedness of the man is what is between his navel and his knee, and likewise the female slave in the more correct (al-aṣaḥḥ) opinion. The free woman [must cover] everything except the face and the two hands. Its condition is that it prevent the perception of the color of the skin, even with mud or turbid water. The more correct (al-aṣaḥḥ) opinion is that it is obligatory to apply mud for the one who lacks clothing. It is obligatory to cover its upper part and its sides, not its lower part. If his nakedness is seen through his pocket during bowing or otherwise, it does not suffice, so he must button it or tighten his waist. He may cover part of it with his hand in the more correct (al-aṣaḥḥ) opinion. If he finds [clothing] while he is in his two private parts [i.e., during the act], [he must cover himself].

chapters.title_en: Section 8 — On Matters Nullifying Prayer, Uncleanliness, and Prostration for Forgetfulness (Sajdah al-Sahw)
chapters.arabic_text:
تعين لهما أو إحداهما فقبله وقيل: دبره وقيل: يتخير وطهارة الحدث فإن سبقه

بطلت وفي القديم يبني ويجربان في كل مناقض عرض بلا تقصير وتعذر دفعه في

الحال فإن أمكن بأن كشفته ريح فستر في الحال لم تبطل وإن قصر بأن فرغت مدة

خف فيها بطلت وطهارة النجس في الثوب والبدن والمكان ولو اشتبه طاهر ونجس

اجتهد ولو نجس بعض ثوب أو بدن وجهل وجب غسل كله فلو ظن طرفا لم يكف غسله

على الصحيح ولو غسل نصف نجس ثم باقيه فالأصح أنه إن غسل مع باقيه مجاوره

طهر كله وإلا فغير المتنصف ولا تصح صلاة ملاق بعض لباسه نجاسة وإن لم يتحرك

بحركته ولا قابض طرف شيء على نجس إن تحرك وكذا إن لم يتحرك في الأصح فلو

جعله تحت رجله صحت مطلقا ولا يضر نجس يحاذي صدره في الركوع والسجود على

الصحيح ولو وصل عظمه بنجس لفقد الطاهر فمعذور وإلا وجب نزعه إن لم يخف ضررا

ظاهرا قيل: وإن خاف فإن مات لم ينزع على الصحيح ويعفى عن محل استجماره ولو

حمل مستجمر أبطلت في الأصح وطين الشارع المتيقن نجاسته يعفى عنه عما يتعذر

الاحتراز منه غالبا ويختلف بالوقت وموضعه من الثوب والبدن وعن قليل دم

البراغيث وونيم الذباب والأصح لا يعفي عن كثيره ولا قليل انتشر بعرق وتعرف

الكثرة بالعادة.
# قلت: الأصح عند المحققين العفو مطلقا والله أعلم ودم البثرات كالبراغيث

وقيل: إن عصره فلاو الدماميل والقروح وموضع الفصد والحجامة قيل: كالبثرات
# 
# والأصح إن كان مثله يدوم غالبا فكالإستحاضة وإلا فكدم الأجنبي فلا يعفى

وقيل: يعفى عن قليله.
# قلت: الأصح أنها كالبثرات والأظهر العفو عن قليل  دم الأجنبي والله أعلم

والقيح والصديد كالدم وكذا ماء القروح والمتنفط الذي له ريح كذا بلا ريح في

الأظهر.
# قلت: المذهب طهارته والله أعلم ولو صلى بنجس لم يعلمه وجب القضاء في

الجديد وإن على ثم نسي وجب القضاء على المذهب.

# فصل
# تبطل بالنطق بحرفين أو حرف مفهم وكذا مدة بعد حرف في الأصح والأصح أن

التنحنح والضحك والبكاء والأنين والنفخ إن ظهر به حرفان بطلت وإلا فلا

ويعذر في يسير الكلام إن سبق لسانه أو نسي الصلاة أو جهل تحريمه إن قرب

عهده بالإسلام لا كثيره في الأصح وفي التنحنح ونحوه للغلبة وتعذر القراءة

لا الجهر في الأصح ولو أكره على الكلام بطلت في الأظهر ولو نطق بنظم القرآن

بقصد التفهيم كيا يحيى خذ الكتاب إن قصد معه قراءة لم تبطل وإلا بطلت ولا

تبطل بالذكر والدعاء إلا أن يخاطب كقوله لعطاس يرحمك الله ولو سكت طويلا

بلا غرض لم تبطل في الأصح ويسن لمن نابه شيء كتنبيه إمامه وإذنه لداخل

وإنذاره أعمى أن يسبح وتصفق المرأة بضرب اليمين على ظهر اليسار ولو فعل في

صلاته غيرها إن كان من جنسها بطلت إلا أن ينسى وإلا فتبطل بكثيره لا قليله

والكثرة بالعرف فالخطوتان أو الضربتان قليل والثلاث كثير إن توالت وتبطل

بالوثبة الفاحشة لا الحركات الخفيفة المتوالية كتحريك أصابعه في سبحة أو حك

في الأصح وسهو الفعل الكثير كعمده في الأصح وتبطل بقليل الأكل قلت: إلا أن

يكون ناسيا أو جاهلا تحريمه والله أعلم فلو كان بفمه سكرة فبلغ ذوبها بطلت

في الأصح ويسن للمصلي إلى جدار أو
# 
# سارية أو عصا مغروزة أو بسط مصلى أو خط قبالته دفع المار والصحيح تحريم

المرور حينئذ قلت: يكره الالتفات إلا لحاجة ورفع بصره إلى السماء وكف شعره

أو ثوبه ووضع يده على فمه بلا حاجة والقيام على رجل والصلاة حاقنا أو حاقبا

أو بحضرة طعام يتوق إليه وأن يبصق قبل وجهه أو عن يمينه ووضع يده على

خاصرته والمبالغة في خفض  الرأس في ركوعه والصلاة في الحمام والطريق

والمزبلة والكنيسة وعطن الإبل والمقبرة الطاهرة. والله أعلم.
#

| باب سجود السهو
# سنة عند ترك مأمور به أو فعل منهي عنه فالأول: إن كان ركنا وجب تداركه

وقد يشرع السجود لزيادة حصلت بتدارك ركن كما سبق في الترتيب أو بعضا وهو

القنوت أو قيامه أو التشهد الأول أو قعوده وكذا الصلاة على النبي صلى الله

عليه وسلم فيه في الأظهر سجد وقيل: إن ترك عمدا فلا.
# قلت: وكذا الصلاة على الآل حيث سنناها والله أعلم ولا تجبر سائر السنن

والثاني: إن لم يبطل عمده كالالتفات والخطوتين لم يسجد لسهوه وإلا سجد إن

لم تبطل بسهوه ككلام كثير في الأصح وتطويل الركن القصير يبطل عمده في الأصح

فيسجد لسهوه فالاعتدال قصير وكذا الجلوس بين السجدتين في الأصح ولو نقل

ركنا قوليا كفاتحة في ركوع أو تشهد لم تبطل بعمده في الأصح ويسجد لسهوه في

الأصح وعلى هذا تستثنى هذه الصورة من قولنا ما لا يبطل عمده لا سجود لسهوه

ولو نسي التشهد الأول فذكره بعد
# 
# انتصابه لم يعد له فإن عاد عالما بتحريمه بطلت أو ناسيا فلا ويسجد للسهو

أو جاهلا فكذا في الأصح وللمأموم العود لمتابعة إمامه في الأصح.
# قلت: الأصح وجوبه والله أعلم ولو تذكر قبل انتصابه عاد للتشهد ويسجد إن

كان صار إلى القيام أقرب ولو نهض عمدا فعاد بطلت إن كان إلى القيام أقرب

ولو نسي قنوتا فذكره في سجوده لم يعد له أو قبله عاد ويسجد للسهو إن بلغ حد
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ع-ف-و (ʿafw)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Erasure, pardon, remission; that which is excused or overlooked.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Legal dispensation (rukhṣah) whereby a ruling is lifted due to exigency (ḍarūrah) or hardship (mashaqqah).
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal sense is obliteration of a trace; here metaphorical for juridical non-accountability.
- Root: س-ه-و (sahw)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Forgetfulness, inadvertence, lapse of attention.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Mental absence from an intended act; in fiqh, a cause for compensatory prostration.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal is negligence; technical usage denotes an unintentional deviation in prayer.
- Root: ب-ط-ل (buṭlān)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To become void, null, invalid.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Invalidation of an act of worship due to violation of its conditions or integrals.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal is corruption; here juridical nullification of prayer.
- Sībawayh Rule: Conditional clauses with فاء (fā' al-sababiyyah) — the apodosis is linked to the protasis by causality, governing legal consequences (e.g., "if he is preceded... then it is nullified").
chapters.translation:
I say: If it is determined for both of them or for one of them, then he accepts it. And it was said: he prays after it (i.e., after the time of uncertainty). And it was said: he may choose. And regarding the purification from ritual impurity (ḥadath): if it (i.e., the prayer) is preceded by its occurrence, it is nullified. And in the old (qadīm) school, he builds upon it. And both are excused in every nullifying occurrence that arises without negligence and whose repulsion is impossible at the moment. But if it is possible — such as when wind uncovers him and he covers himself immediately — it does not nullify. And if he is negligent — such as when the duration of concealment is prolonged — it nullifies. And regarding purification from filth (najas) on the garment, body, and place: if pure and impure are confused, he exerts his judgment (ijtihād). And if part of a garment or body is impure but its location is unknown, washing all of it is obligatory. If he merely supposes a particular side, washing that side is not sufficient according to the soundest (al-aṣaḥḥ) opinion. And if he washes half of the impure area, then the remainder, the soundest view is: if he washed the adjacent part along with the remainder, all becomes pure; otherwise, the unwashed half remains impure. And prayer is not valid for one who carries some impurity on his garment even if it does not move with his movement. Nor for one who holds the edge of something upon which there is impurity, if it moves; and likewise if it does not move, according to the soundest view. But if he places it under his foot, prayer is valid absolutely. And impurity that faces his chest during bowing (rukūʿ) and prostration (sujūd) does not harm, according to the soundest view. And if his bone is connected to impurity due to the absence of pure (bone), he is excused; otherwise, removal is obligatory if he does not fear manifest harm. It was said: even if he fears, and if he dies, it is not removed, according to the soundest view. And the place of istinjā' (cleansing with stones) is excused. And if one carrying (a stone used for istinjā') prays, it is nullified, according to the soundest view. And the mud of the road whose impurity is certain is excused to the extent that avoidance is generally impossible; and this varies by time and by its location on the garment or body. And regarding the small amount of flea blood and fly residue: the soundest view is that a large amount is not excused, nor a small amount that spreads due to sweat. And the determination of "large" is by custom.

I say: The soundest view among the verifying scholars is absolute pardon (ʿafw), and Allah knows best. And the blood of pimples is like flea blood. And it was said: if it is squeezed, then no. And the blood of abscesses, sores, the place of phlebotomy (faṣd), and cupping (ḥijāmah): it was said it is like pimples. And the soundest view is: if its like persists generally, then it is like chronic uterine bleeding (istīḥāḍah); otherwise, it is like the blood of a stranger (i.e., foreign blood), so it is not excused. And it was said: a small amount is excused.

I say: The soundest view is that it is like pimples, and the more apparent view is pardon for a small amount of a stranger's blood, and Allah knows best. And pus and sanies are like blood. Likewise, the water of sores and of a blister that has an odor — and likewise without odor, according to the more apparent view.

I say: The school (madhhab) is that it is pure, and Allah knows best. And if one prays with impurity he did not know of, making up (qaḍā') is obligatory in the new (jadīd) view. And if he knew but forgot, making up is obligatory according to the school.

CHAPTER: [On What Nullifies Prayer]

Prayer is nullified by uttering two letters or one letter that conveys meaning. Likewise, a prolonged (madd) after a letter, according to the soundest view. And the soundest view is that clearing the throat, laughing, weeping, groaning, and blowing — if two letters become apparent thereby, it nullifies; otherwise, it does not. And one is excused for a small amount of speech if his tongue slipped, or he forgot the prayer, or he was ignorant of its prohibition while his conversion to Islam was recent — not for a large amount, according to the soundest view. And regarding clearing the throat and the like, one is excused if it overcomes him and recitation becomes difficult — but not for loud (deliberate) clearing, according to the soundest view. And if one is coerced into speaking, it nullifies, according to the more apparent view. And if he utters Quranic verse as speech intending to convey meaning — like {«يَا يَحْيَىٰ خُذِ الْكِتَابَ»} (O Yahya, take the Scripture) — if he intends with it recitation, it does not nullify; otherwise, it nullifies. And it does not nullify by dhikr (remembrance) or supplication (duʿā'), unless he addresses someone, such as saying to a sneezer, "May Allah have mercy on you." And if he remains silent for a long time without purpose, it does not nullify, according to the soundest view. And it is Sunnah for one whom something befalls — such as alerting his imam, granting permission to an entrant, or warning a blind man — to say "Subḥān Allāh" (glorification). And a woman claps by striking the right palm on the back of the left. And if one performs an extraneous act in his prayer: if it is of the same genus (jins) as prayer, it nullifies — unless he forgets. Otherwise, it nullifies by a large amount, not a small one. And "large" is determined by custom: two steps or two strikes are small, and three are large if consecutive. And it nullifies by an excessive leap, but not by light consecutive movements, such as moving his fingers in a rosary or scratching, according to the soundest view. And forgetfulness in a large act is like intentionality, according to the soundest view. And it nullifies by a small amount of eating.

I say: Unless he is forgetful or ignorant of its prohibition, and Allah knows best. And if there is a sugar piece in his mouth and its melting reaches (his throat), it nullifies, according to the soundest view. And it is Sunnah for one praying toward a wall, or a pillar, or a planted staff, or a spread prayer mat, or a line drawn in front of him, to repel a passerby. And the soundest view is that passing (in front of a praying person) is prohibited at that time.

I say: It is disliked (makrūh) to turn one's face (in prayer) except for need; and to raise one's gaze to the sky; and to smooth one's hair or garment; and to place one's hand on one's mouth without need; and to stand on one leg; and to pray while needing to urinate or defecate, or in the presence of food one craves; and to spit in front of one's face or to one's right; and to place one's hand on one's flank; and to exaggerate in lowering the head during rukūʿ; and to pray in a bathhouse, a road, a dunghill, a church, a camel resting place, or a pure cemetery. And Allah knows best.

CHAPTER: On the Prostration of Forgetfulness (Sajdah al-Sahw)

It is Sunnah upon omitting a commanded act or committing a prohibited act. As for the first: if it is an integral (rukn), it must be made up. And prostration may be prescribed for an increase that occurs due to making up an integral, as previously mentioned in the section on order (tartīb). Or for a part (of the prayer) — namely, the qunūt, or its standing, or the first tashahhud, or its sitting. Likewise, sending blessings upon the Prophet ﷺ therein (in the first tashahhud), according to the more apparent view — he prostrates. And it was said: if it is omitted intentionally, then no.

I say: Likewise, blessings upon the family (āl) where we deem it Sunnah, and Allah knows best. And the rest of the Sunnahs are not compensated (by prostration). As for the second (prohibited acts): if its intentional commission does not nullify — like turning the face or two steps — he does not prostrate for its forgetfulness. Otherwise, he prostrates — provided its forgetfulness does not nullify, such as much speech, according to the soundest view. And prolonging a short integral nullifies intentionally, according to the soundest view, so he prostrates for its forgetfulness. Thus, the standing upright (iʿtidāl) is short, and likewise the sitting between the two prostrations, according to the soundest view. And if one moves a verbal integral — such as the Fātiḥah — into rukūʿ or tashahhud, it does not nullify intentionally, according to the soundest view, and he prostrates for its forgetfulness, according to the soundest view. And on this basis, this case is excepted from our statement: "What does not nullify intentionally has no prostration for its forgetfulness." And if one forgets the first tashahhud and remembers after fully standing, he does not return to it. If he returns while knowing its prohibition, it nullifies; or if forgetful, then no, and he prostrates for forgetfulness; or if ignorant, likewise, according to the soundest view. And for the follower (ma'mūm), returning is permissible to follow his imam, according to the soundest view.

I say: The soundest view is that it is obligatory, and Allah knows best. And if he remembers before fully standing, he returns to the tashahhud, and he prostrates if he had become closer to standing. And if he rises intentionally and returns, it nullifies if he had become closer to standing. And if one forgets the qunūt and remembers during his prostration, he does not return to it; or if before it, he returns and prostrates for forgetfulness if he had reached the limit (of standing).

chapters.title_en: Section 9 — On Forgetfulness in Prayer (Sahw) and Supererogatory Prayers
chapters.arabic_text:
الراكع ولو شك في ترك بعض سجد أو ارتكاب نهي فلا ولو سها وشك هل سجد فيسجد

ولو شك أصلى ثلاثا أم أربعا أتى بركعة وسجد والأصح أنه يسجد وإن زال شكه

قبل سلامه وكذا حكم ما يصليه مترددا واحتمل كونه زائدا ولا يسجد لما يجب

بكل حال إذا زال شكه مثاله شك في الثالثة: أثالثة هي أم رابعة فتذكر فيها

لم يسجد أو في الرابعة: سجد ولو شك بعد  السلام في ترك فرض لم يؤثر على

المشهور وسهوه حال قدوته يحمله إمامه فلو ظن سلامه فسلم فبان خلافه سلم معه

ولا سجود ولو ذكر في تشهده ترك ركن غير النية والتكبير قام بعد سلام إمامه

إلى ركعته ولا يسجد وسهوه بعد سلامه لا يحمله فلو سلم المسبوق بسلام إمامه

بنى وسجد ويلحقه سهو إمامه فإن سجد لزمه متابعته وإلا فيسجد على النص ولو

اقتدى مسبوق بمن سها بعد اقتدائه وكذا قبله في الأصح فالصحيح أنه يسجد معه

ثم في آخر صلاته فإن لم يسجد الإمام سجد آخر صلاة نفسه على النص وسجود

السهو وإن كثر سجدتان كسجود الصلاة والجديد أن محله بين تشهده وسلامه فإن

سلم عمدا فات في الأصح أو سهوا وطال الفصل فات في الجديد وإلا فلا على النص

وإذا سجد صار عائدا إلى الصلاة في الأصح ولو سها إمام الجمعة وسجدوا فبان

فوتها أتموا ظهرا وسجدوا ولو ظن سهوا فسجد فبان عدمه سجد في الأصح.
#

| باب تسن سجدات التلاوة
# وهن في الجديد أربع عشرة منها سجدتا الحج لا ص بل هي سجدة شكر تستحب في

غير الصلاة وتحرم فيها على الأصح وتسن للقارىء والمستمع وتتأكد بسجود

القارىء.
# قلت: وتسن للسامع والله أعلم وإن قرأ في الصلاة سجد الإمام والمنفرد

لقراءته فقط والمأموم لسجدة إمامه فإن سجد إمامه فتخلف أو انعكس بطلت صلاته

ومن سجد خارج الصلاة نوى وكبر للإحرام رافعا يديه ثم للهوى بلا رفع وسجد

كسجدة الصلاة ورفع مكبرا وسلم وتكبيرة الإحرام شرط على الصحيح وكذا السلام

في الأظهر وتشترط شروط الصلاة ومن سجد فيها كبر للهوى وللرفع ولا يرفع

يديه.
# قلت: ولا يجلس للاستراحة والله أعلم ويقول سجد وجهي للذي خلقه وصوره وشق

سمعه وبصره بحوله وقوته ولو كرر آية في مجلسين سجد لكل وكذا المجلس في

الأصح وركعة كمجلس وركعتان كمجلسين فإن لم يسجد وطال ال فصل لم يسجد وسجدة

الشكر لا تدخل الصلاة وتسن لهجوم نعمة أو اندفاع نقمة أو رؤية مبتلى  أو عاص

ويظهرها للعاصي لا للمبتلي وهي كسجدة التلاوة والأصح جوازهما على الراحلة

للمسافر فإن سجد تلاوة صاة جاز عليها قطعا.
# 
# الصبح وركعتان قبل الظهر وكذا بعدها وبعد المغرب والعشاء وقيل: لا راتب

للعشاء وقيل: أربع قبل الظهر وقيل: وأربع بعدها وقيل: وأربع قبل العصر

والجميع سنة وإنما الخلاف في الراتب المؤكد وركعتان خفيفتان قبل المغرب.
# قلت: هما سنة على الصحيح ففي صحيح البخاري الأمر بهما وبعد الجمعة أربع

وقبلها ما قبل الظهر والله أعلم ومنه الوتر وأقله ركعة وأكثره إحدى عشرة

وقيل: ثلاث عشرة ولمن زاد على ركعة الفصل وهو أفضل والوصل بتشهد أو تشهدين

في الآخرتين ووقته بين صلاة العشاء وطلوع الفجر وقيل: شرط الإيثار بركعة

سبق نفل بعد العشاء ويسن جعله آخر صلاة الليل فإن أوتر ثم تهجد لم يعده

وقيل: يشفعه بركعة ثم يعيده ويندب القنوت آخر وتره في النصف الثاني من

رمضان وقال كل سنة وهو كقنوت الصبح ويقول قبله اللهم إنا نستعينك ونستغفرك

إلى آخره.
# قلت: الأصح بعده أن الجماعة تندب في الوتر عقب التراويح جماعة والله أعلم

ومنه الضحى وأقلها ركعتان وأكثرها ثنتا عشرة وتحية المسجد ركعتان وتحصل

بفرض أو نفل آخر لا بركعة على الصحيح.
# قلت: وكذا الجنازة وسجدة التلاوة والشكر وتتكر بتكرر الدخول على قرب في

الأصح والله أعلم ويدخل وقت الرواتب قبل الفرض بدخول وقت الفرض وبعده بفعله

ويخرج النوعان بخروج وقت الفرض ولو فات النفل المؤقت ندب قضاؤه في الأظهر

وقسم يسن جماعة كالعيد والكسوف والاستسقاء وهو أفضل مما لا يسن جماعة لكن

الأصح تفضيل الراتبة على التراويح وأن الجماعة تسن في التراويح ولا حصر

للنفل المطلق فإن أحرم بأكثر من ركعة فله التشهد في كل ركعتين وفي كل ركعة.
# 
# قلت: الصحيح منعه في كل ركعة والله أعلم وإذا نوى عددا فله أن يزيد وينقص

بشرط تغيير النية قبلهما وإلا فتبطل فلو نوى ركعتين فقام إلى ثالثة سهوا

فالأصح أنه يقعد ثم يقوم للزيادة إن شاء.
# قلت: نفل الليل  أفضل وأوسطه أفضل ثم آخره وأن يسلم من كل ركعتين ويسن

التهجد ويكره قيام كل الليل دائما وتخصيص ليلة الجمعة بقيام وترك تهجد

اعتاده. والله أعلم.
#

| باب صلاة النفل
# قسمان قسم لا يسن جماعة فمنه الرواتب مع الفرائض وهي ركعتان قبل
#

| كتاب صلاة الجماعة

| مدخل

chapters.anchors:
- Root: س-ه-و (s-h-w)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Forgetfulness, inadvertence, neglect arising from a lapse of attention; the state of being unmindful of an act while performing it.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In ritual law, sahw denotes an unintentional omission or excess in prayer that necessitates prostration (sujūd al-sahw) as a compensatory act, distinct from deliberate error.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal (ḥaqīqah) refers to mental absence; metaphorical (majāz) extends to any ritual irregularity requiring correction.
- Root: س-ج-د (s-j-d)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To prostrate, humble oneself; the physical act of placing the forehead on the ground in worship.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Sujūd is the culminating posture of prayer symbolizing absolute servitude (ʿubūdiyyah) and proximity to the Divine.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal prostration in prayer; metaphorically, submission of the soul.
- Root: ن-ف-ل (n-f-l)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Supererogatory, voluntary act; an increase beyond the obligatory.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Nafal denotes voluntary worship that supplements obligatory rites, enhancing the believer’s rank.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal surplus; in jurisprudence, a recommended prayer beyond the farḍ.
- Sībawayh Rule: Conditional and Exceptive Clauses (al-sharṭ wa al-istithnāʾ) — The text employs repeated conditional particles (law, in) and exceptions (illā) to delineate juristic rulings; parsing requires identifying the protasis and apodosis to preserve legal precision.
chapters.translation:
I say: Know that the one bowing, even if he doubts whether he omitted some prostration or committed a prohibited act, there is no [obligation to prostrate]. And if he forgets and doubts whether he prostrated, he must prostrate. And if he doubts whether he prayed three or four [rakʿahs], he performs an additional rakʿah and prostrates. The soundest (al-aṣaḥḥ) view is that he prostrates even if his doubt is removed before his salutation. Likewise is the ruling for what he prays while uncertain, and it is possible that it is an excess. And he does not prostrate for what is obligatory in all cases when his doubt is removed. Example: he doubts in the third [rakʿah]: is it the third or fourth, then he recalls therein that he did not prostrate, or in the fourth: he prostrates. And if he doubts after the salutation regarding an omitted obligatory act, it does not affect [his prayer] according to the well-known (al-mashhūr) view. His forgetfulness while following an imam is borne by his imam. So if he thinks the imam has saluted and he salutes, then it becomes clear otherwise, he salutes with him, and there is no prostration. And if he recalls in his tashahhud the omission of a pillar other than the intention (niyyah) and the takbīr [of consecration], he stands after his imam’s salutation to complete his rakʿah, and he does not prostrate. His forgetfulness after his imam’s salutation is not borne [by the imam]. So if a latecomer (masbūq) salutes with his imam’s salutation, he builds [upon what he has completed] and prostrates. The forgetfulness of his imam attaches to him; if [the imam] prostrates, he must follow him; otherwise, he prostrates according to the text (al-naṣṣ). And if a latecomer follows one who forgot after his following [began], and likewise before it according to the soundest view, the correct view is that he prostrates with him, then at the end of his own prayer. If the imam does not prostrate, he prostrates at the end of his own prayer according to the text. The prostration of forgetfulness, however numerous, is two prostrations like the prostrations of prayer. The new view (al-jadīd) is that its place is between his tashahhud and his salutation. If he salutes deliberately, it is missed according to the soundest view; or forgetfully and the interval is prolonged, it is missed according to the new view; otherwise not, according to the text. And when he prostrates, he becomes as one returning to the prayer according to the soundest view. And if the imam of the Friday prayer forgets and they prostrate, then it becomes clear that the Friday [prayer] was missed, they complete it as ẓuhr and prostrate. And if he thinks he forgot and prostrates, then it becomes clear there was no forgetfulness, he prostrates according to the soundest view.

Then follows the chapter on the recommended prostrations of recitation (sujūd al-tilāwah). They are, according to the new view, fourteen. Among them are the two prostrations in Sūrat al-Ḥajj — no, rather it is a prostration of thankfulness (sajdat shukr) recommended outside prayer and forbidden within it according to the soundest view. It is recommended for the reciter and the listener, and it is emphasized by the reciter’s prostration. I say: It is recommended for the hearer, and God knows best. If he recites in prayer, the imam and the one praying alone prostrate for their own recitation only, and the follower for his imam’s prostration. If his imam prostrates and he lags behind, or the reverse, his prayer is invalidated. And whoever prostrates outside prayer intends [the prostration], says the takbīr of consecration (takbīr al-iḥrām) while raising his hands, then [says takbīr] for bowing without raising, prostrates like the prostration of prayer, raises while saying takbīr, and salutes. The takbīr of consecration is a condition according to the correct view, and likewise the salutation according to the more apparent view. The conditions of prayer are required. And whoever prostrates within it says takbīr for bowing and for raising, and does not raise his hands. I say: He does not sit for rest, and God knows best. He says: “I have prostrated my face to Him who created it and fashioned it, and opened its hearing and sight by His might and power.” If he repeats a verse in two gatherings, he prostrates for each; likewise for one gathering according to the soundest view. One rakʿah is like one gathering, and two rakʿahs like two gatherings. If he does not prostrate and the interval is prolonged, he does not prostrate. The prostration of thankfulness does not enter the prayer, and it is recommended upon the advent of a blessing, the repulsion of a calamity, or seeing an afflicted person or a sinner. It is shown to the sinner, not to the afflicted. It is like the prostration of recitation. The soundest view is that both are permissible on a mount for the traveler; if he prostrates for recitation as a prayer, it is permissible upon it definitively.

Then [the chapter on] the morning [prayer] and two rakʿahs before ẓuhr, and likewise after it, and after maghrib and ʿishāʾ. It is said: there is no regular [sunnah] for ʿishāʾ. It is said: four before ẓuhr, and it is said: four after it, and it is said: four before ʿaṣr. All are sunnah; the disagreement is only regarding the emphasized regular [sunnah]. And two light rakʿahs before maghrib. I say: They are sunnah according to the correct view, for in Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī there is the command for them. After Friday [prayer], four, and before it, what is before ẓuhr. God knows best. Among them is the witr; its minimum is one rakʿah, and its maximum is eleven, and it is said: thirteen. For one who exceeds one rakʿah, separation [between pairs] is permissible and preferable, and joining with one tashahhud or two in the last two. Its time is between the ʿishāʾ prayer and the dawn’s rising. It is said: the condition of preferring one rakʿah is the precedence of a voluntary prayer after ʿishāʾ. It is recommended to make it the last of the night prayer. If he performs witr then prays the night vigil (tahajjud), he does not repeat it; and it is said: he makes it even with one rakʿah, then repeats it. The qunūt is recommended at the end of his witr in the second half of Ramaḍān, and it is said: every year, and it is like the qunūt of the morning prayer. He says before it: “O God, we seek Your aid and Your forgiveness” to its end. I say: The soundest view is that the congregation is recommended in witr following the tarāwīḥ in congregation, and God knows best. Among them is the ḍuḥā [prayer]; its minimum is two rakʿahs and its maximum is twelve. The greeting of the mosque (taḥiyyat al-masjid) is two rakʿahs, and it is fulfilled by an obligatory or another voluntary prayer, not by one rakʿah according to the correct view. I say: Likewise the funeral prayer and the prostration of recitation and thankfulness. It is repeated with the repetition of entry, even if close in time, according to the soundest view, and God knows best. The time of the regular [sunnah] prayers enters before the obligatory prayer with the entry of the obligatory prayer’s time, and after it by performing it, and both types exit with the exit of the obligatory prayer’s time. If a time-bound voluntary prayer is missed, it is recommended to make it up according to the more apparent view. A category is recommended in congregation, like the two ʿĪds, the eclipse prayer, and the rain prayer, and it is superior to what is not recommended in congregation. But the soundest view is the preference of the regular [sunnah] over the tarāwīḥ, and that the congregation is recommended in tarāwīḥ. There is no limit for the absolute voluntary prayer. If one consecrates with more than one rakʿah, he may perform the tashahhud in every two rakʿahs and in every rakʿah. I say: The correct view is its prohibition in every rakʿah, and God knows best. And if he intends a number, he may increase or decrease, provided he changes his intention before both; otherwise it is invalidated. So if he intends two rakʿahs and stands for a third forgetfully, the soundest view is that he sits, then stands for the increase if he wishes. I say: The voluntary night prayer is superior, and its middle is most superior, then its end, and that he salutes from every two rakʿahs. The tahajjud is recommended, and it is disliked to stand the entire night perpetually, and to single out Friday night for standing, and to abandon a habitual tahajjud. God knows best.

Then the chapter on the voluntary prayer (ṣalāt al-nafl). It is of two categories: a category for which congregation is not recommended, and from it are the regular [sunnah] prayers with the obligatory ones, which are two rakʿahs before [the morning prayer]...

chapters.arabic_text:
# كتاب صلاة الجماعة
# هي في الفرائض غير الجمعة سنة مؤكدة وقيل: فرض كفاية للرجال فتجب بحيث

يظهر الشعار في القرية فإن امتنعوا كلهم قوتلوا ولا يتأكد الندب للنساء

تأكده للرجال في الأصح.
# قلت: الأصح المنصوص أنها فرض كفاية وقيل: عين والله أعلم وفي المسجد لغير

المرأة أفضل وما كثر جمعه أفضل إلا لبدعة إمامه أو بعطل مسجد قريب لغيبته

وإدراك تكبيرة الإحرام فضيلة وإنما تحصل بالإستغال بالتحريم عقب تحرم إمامه

وقيل: بإدراك بعض القيام وقيل: بأول ركوع والصحيح إدراك الجماعة ما لم يسلم

وليخفف الإمام مع فعل الأبعاض والهيآت إلا أن يرضى بتطويله محصورون ويكره

التطويل ليلحق آخرون ولو أحسن في الركوع أو التشهد الأخير بداخل لم يكره

انتظاره في الأظهر إن لم يبالغ فيه ولم يفرق بين الداخلين.
# قلت: المذهب استحباب انتظاره والله أعلم ولا ينتظر في غبرهما ويسن للمصلي

وحده وكذا جماعة في الأصح عادتها مع جماعة يدركها وفرضه الأولى في الجديد

والأصح أنه ينوي بالثانية الفرض ولا رخصة في تركها وإن قلنا سنة إلا بعذر

عام كمطر أو ريح عاصف بالليل وكذا وحل شديد على الصحيح أو خاص كمرض وحر

وبرد شديدين وجوع وعطش ظاهرين ومدافعة حدث وخوف ظالم على نفس أو مال

وملازمة غريم معسر
# 
# أو عقوبة يرجى تركها إن تغيب أياما وعرى وتأهب لسفر مع رفقة ترحل وأكل ذي

ريح كريه وحضور قريب محتضر أو مريض بلا متعهد أو يأنس به.

# فصل
# لا يصح اقتداؤه بمن يعلم بطلان صلاته أو يعتقده كمجتهدين اختلفا في

القبلة أو إناءين فإن تعدد الطاهر والأصح الصحة ما لم يتعين إناء الإمام

للنجاسة فإن ظن طهارة إناء غيره اقتدى به قطعا فلو اشتبه خمسة فيها  نجس على

خمسة فظن كل طهارة إناء فتوضأ به وأم كل في صلاة ففي الأصح يعيدون العشاء

إلا إمامها فيعيد المغرب ولو اقتدى شافعي بحنفي مس فرجه أو افتصد فالأصح

الصحة في الفصد دون المس اعتبار أبنية المقتدي ولا تصح قدوة بمقتد ولا بمن

تلزمه إعادة كمقيم تيمم ولا قارىء بأمي في الجديد وهو من يخل بحرف أو

تشديدة من الفاتحة ومنه أرت يدغم في غير موضعه وألثغ يبدل حرفا بحرف وتصح

بمثله وتكره بالتمتام والفأفاء واللاحن فإن غير معنى كأنعمت بضم أو كسر

أبطل صلاة من أمكنه التعلم فإن عجز لسانه أو لم يمض زمن إمكان تعلمه فإن

كان في الفاتحة فكأمي وإلا فتصح صلاته والقدوة به ولا تصح قدوة رجل ولا

خنثى بامرأة ولا خنثى ولا تصح للمتوضيء بالمتيمم وبماسح الخف وللقائم

بالقاعد والمضطجع وللكامل بالصبي والعبد والأعمى والبصير سواء على النص

والأصح صحة قدوة السليم بالسلس
# 
# والطاهر بالمستحاضة غير المتحيرة ولو بان أمامه امرأة أو كافرا معلنا

قيل: أو مخفيا وجبت الإعادة لا جنبا وإذا نجاسة خفية.
# قلت: الأصح النصوص هو قول الجمهور أن مخفي الكفر هنا كمعلنه والله أعلم

والأمي كالمرأة في الأصح ولو اقتدى بخنثى فبان رجلا لم يسقط القضاء في

الأظهر والعدل أولى من الفاسق والأصح أن الأفقه أولى من الأقرإ والأورع

ويقدم الأفقه والأقرأ على الأسن النسيب والجديد تقديم الأسن على النسب فإن

استويا فبنظافة الثوب والبدن وحسن الصوت وطيب الصنعة ونحوها ومستحق المنفعة

بملك ونحوه أولى فإن لم يكن أهلا فله التقديم ويقدم على عبده الساكن لا

مكاتبه في ملكه والأصح تقديم المكتري على المكري والمعير على المستعير

والوالي في محل ولايته أولى من الأفقه والمالك.
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ج-م-ع (j-m-ʿ)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Gathering, uniting, bringing together; jamāʿah denotes a collective assembly bound by a common purpose.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In legal-theological usage, the congregational body whose cohesion fulfills the communal obligation of collective worship.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal (ḥaqīqah) for physical assembly; metaphorical (majāz) for the legal validity of prayer performed in unison.
- Root: ش-ع-ر (sh-ʿ-r)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Perception, marking, ritual sign; shiʿār is the visible emblem of religious identity.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): The outward manifestation of Islamic practice that distinguishes the community from others.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal for sensory awareness; transferred to the public display of devotional rites.
- Sībawayh Rule: Conditional Clause (al-Sharṭ wa al-Jawāb) — The protasis (inʿimāʿuhum) governs the apodosis (qūtilū), with the conditional particle "fa" omitted for concision, indicating legal consequence.
chapters.translation:
I say: Know that the Book of Congregational Prayer — it is, in the obligatory prayers other than Friday, a confirmed sunnah (sunnah muʾakkadah); and it was said: a communal obligation (farḍ kifāyah) for men, such that it becomes incumbent when the public emblem (shiʿār) is manifested in the village. If they all refuse, they are fought. The recommendation is not affirmed for women with the same emphasis as for men, according to the soundest opinion (al-aṣaḥḥ).

I say: The soundest transmitted opinion (al-manṣūṣ) is that it is a communal obligation (farḍ kifāyah); and it was said: an individual obligation (farḍ ʿayn). And Allah knows best. Prayer in the mosque is superior for other than a woman; and the more numerous the congregation, the more excellent — except due to the innovation (bidʿah) of its imam, or the disabling of a nearby mosque by his absence. Attaining the opening takbīr (takbīrat al-iḥrām) is a virtue; it is only achieved by commencing the consecration immediately following the imam's consecration. And it was said: by attaining part of the standing; and it was said: by the first bowing (rukūʿ). The correct view (al-ṣaḥīḥ) is that the congregation is attained as long as he has not saluted. The imam should shorten [the prayer] while performing the essential parts (abʿāḍ) and the postures (hayʾāt), unless those [following] are limited and consent to his prolongation. It is disliked (makrūh) to prolong so that others may join. If one excels in the rukūʿ or the final tashahhud while another enters, it is not disliked to wait for him, according to the most apparent view (al-aẓhar), provided he does not overdo it and does not separate between those entering.

I say: The school (al-madhhab) holds it commendable (mustaḥabb) to wait for him. And Allah knows best. He is not waited for in other than these two [positions]. It is sunnah for one praying alone — and likewise a congregation, according to the soundest opinion — to repeat [the prayer] in congregation when he finds one, and his obligatory [prayer] is the first, according to the new view (al-jadīd). The soundest opinion is that he intends by the second the obligatory [prayer]. There is no concession (rukhaṣ) to abandon it, even if we say it is sunnah, except for a general excuse — like rain or a violent wind at night, and likewise severe mud, according to the correct view — or a specific one: like illness, intense heat or cold, manifest hunger and thirst, the urge to relieve oneself (madāfaʿat ḥadath), fear of a tyrant over life or property, the companionship of an insolvent debtor, or a punishment whose abandonment is hoped for if one absents himself for days, nakedness, preparation for a journey with companions who depart, eating something with a foul odor, the presence of a near relative in the throes of death or ill without a caretaker, or one whose company brings solace.

Chapter (Faṣl):
It is not valid to follow (iqtidāʾ) one whose prayer one knows to be invalid, or believes to be so — like two mujtahids who differ over the direction of the qiblah, or over two vessels [one pure, one impure] when the pure one is multiple. The soundest opinion is validity, as long as the imam's vessel is not specifically determined to be impure. If one supposes the purity of another's vessel, he follows him definitively. If five vessels are confused, one of which contains impurity, among five people, and each supposes the purity of a vessel, performs ablution with it, and leads [a prayer], then according to the soundest opinion they repeat the ʿishāʾ prayer, except its imam — he repeats the maghrib. If a Shāfiʿī follows a Ḥanafī who touched his genitals or was cupped (iftaṣada), the soundest opinion is validity in the case of cupping, not in the case of touching — considering the [juridical] principles of the follower (iʿtibār abniyat al-muqtadī). It is not valid to follow one who is himself following [another], nor one who must repeat [his prayer] — like a resident who performed tayammum. Nor does a proficient reciter follow an illiterate one (ummī), according to the new view — he being one who errs in a letter or a doubled consonant (tashdīd) of the Fātiḥah. From this [category] is the one with a lisp (artaʾ) who assimilates [a letter] in other than its proper place, and the one with a speech defect (althagh) who substitutes one letter for another. It is valid to follow one like him; it is disliked to follow the stammerer (tamtām), the falterer (faʾfāʾ), and the one who errs in grammar (lāḥin). If he changes the meaning — like "anʿamta" with a ḍammah or kasrah [on the nūn] — he invalidates the prayer of one who could have learned [correctly]. If his tongue is incapable, or the time for possible learning has not elapsed: if [the error] is in the Fātiḥah, he is like the ummī; otherwise, his prayer is valid, and following him is valid. It is not valid for a man or a hermaphrodite (khunthā) to follow a woman, nor a hermaphrodite [to follow a woman]. It is not valid for one who performed ablution with water to follow one who performed tayammum, nor one who wiped over leather socks (māsih al-khuff). It is valid for the standing to follow the sitting and the reclining, and for the complete [in purity] to follow the boy, the slave, the blind, and the sighted — equally, according to the text (al-naṣṣ). The soundest opinion is the validity of the sound [in purity] following the one with chronic incontinence (sals), and the pure following the woman with prolonged uterine bleeding (mustaḥāḍah) other than the perplexed one (mutḥayyirah). If it becomes apparent that the imam was a woman or an open disbeliever (kāfir muʿlin) — and it was said: or a concealed one — repetition is obligatory; not so for the one in major impurity (junub), nor when there is hidden impurity.

I say: The soundest of the transmitted texts is the position of the majority (al-jumhūr): that the concealed disbeliever here is like the open one. And Allah knows best. The ummī is like the woman, according to the soundest opinion. If one follows a hermaphrodite and it becomes apparent he is a man, the make-up (qadāʾ) is not dropped, according to the most apparent view. The just (ʿadl) is more worthy than the sinner (fāsiq); and the soundest opinion is that the more jurisprudent (afqah) is more worthy than the better reciter (aqraʾ) and the more scrupulous (awraʿ). The more jurisprudent and the better reciter are given precedence over the older and the one of noble lineage (nasīb). The new view gives precedence to the older over the lineage. If they are equal, then [preference is] by cleanliness of garment and body, beauty of voice, excellence of craft, and the like. The one entitled to the benefit [of the property] by ownership or the like is more worthy; if he is not qualified, he may delegate [another]. He is given precedence over his resident slave — not his mukātab [slave contracted for manumission] — in his property. The soundest opinion is that the tenant is given precedence over the landlord, and the borrower over the lender. The governor (wālī) in his jurisdiction is more worthy than the more jurisprudent and the owner.

chapters.arabic_text:
# فصل
# لا يتقدم على إمامه في الموقف فإن تقدم بطلت في الجديد ولا تضر مساواته

ويندب تخلفه قليلا والإعتبار بالعقب ويستديرون في المسجد الحرام حول الكعبة

ولا يضر كونهم أقرب إلى الكعبة في غير جهة الإمام في الأصح وكذا لو وقفا في

الكعبة واختلف جهتاهما ويقف  الذكر عن يمينه فإن حضر آخر أحرم عن يساره ثم

يتقدم الإمام أو يتأخران وهو أفضل ولو حضر رجلان أو رجل وصب صفا خلفه وكذا

امرأة أو نسوة ويقف خلفه الرجال ثم الصبيان ثم النساء وتقف إمامتهن وسطهن

ويكره وقوف المأموم فردا بل يدخل الصف إن وجد سعة وإلا فليجر شخصا بعد

الإحرام وليساعده المجرور ويشترط علمه بانتقالات
# 
# الإمام بأن يراه أو بعض صف أو يسمعه أو مبلغا وإذا جمعهما مسجد صح

الإقتداء وإن بعدت المسافة وحالت أبنية ولو كانا بفضاء شرط أن لا يزيد ما

بينهما على ثلاثمائة ذراع تقريبا وقيل: تحديدا فإن تلاحق شخصان أو صفان

اعتبرت المسافة بين الأخير والأول وسواء الفضاء المملوك والوقف والمبعض ولا

يضر الشارع المطروق والنهر المحوج إلى سباحة على الصحيح فإن كانا في بناءين

كصحن وصفة أو بيت فطريقان أصحهما إن كان بناء المأموم يمينا أو شمالا وجب

اتصال صف من أحد البناءين بالآخر ولا تضر فرجه لاتسع واقفا في الأصح وإن

كان خلف بناء الإمام فالصحيح صحة القدوة بشرط أن لا يكون بين الصفين أكثر

من ثلاثة أذرع والطريق الثاني لا يشترط إلا القرب كالفضاء إن لم يكن حائل

أو حال باب نافذ فإن حال ما يمنع المرور لا الرؤية فوجهان أو جدار بطلت

باتفاق الطريقين.
# قلت: الطريق الثاني أصح والله أعلم وإذا صح اقتداؤه في بناء آخر صح

اقتداء من خلفه وإن حال جدار بينه وبين الإمام ولو وقف في علو وإمامه في

أسفل أو عكسه شرط محاذاة بعض بدنه بعض بدنه ولو وقف في موات وإمامه في مسجد

فإن لم يحل شيء فالشرط التقارب معتبرا من آخر المسجد وقيل: من آخر صف وإن

حال جدار أو باب مغلق منع وكذا الباب المردود والشباك في الأصح.
# قلت: يكره ارتفاع المأموم على إمامه وعكسه إلا لحاجة فيستحب ولا يقوم حتى

يفرغ المؤذن من الإقامة ولا يبتدىء نفلا بعد شروعه فيها فإن كان فيها أئمة

إن لم يخش فوت الجماعة. والله أعلم.

# فصل
# شرط القدوة أن ينوي المأموم مع التكبير الإقتداء أو الجماعة والجمعة

كغيرها على الصحيح فلو ترك هذه النية وتابع في الأفعال بطلت صلاته على

الصحيح ولا يجب تعيين
# 
# الإمام فإن عينه وأخطأ بطلت صلاته ولا يشترط للإمام نية الإمامة وتستحب

فلو أخطأ في تعيين تابعه لم يضر وتصح قدوة المؤدي بالقاضي والمفترض

بالمتنفل وفي الظهر بالعصر وبالعكوس وكذا الظهر بالصبح والمغرب وهو

كالمسبوق ولا تضر متابعة الإمام في القنوت والجلوس الآخر في المغرب وله

فراقه إذا اشتغل بهما ويجوز الصبح خلف الظهر في الأظهر فإذا قام للثالثة

فإن شاء فارقه وسلم وإن شاء انتظره ليسلم معه.
# قلت: انتظاره أفضل والله أعلم وإن أمكنه القنوت في الثانية قنت وإلا تركه

وله فراقه ليقنت فإن اختلف فعلهما كمكتوبة وكسوف أو جنازة لم يصح على

الصحيح.

# فصل
# تجب متابعة الإمام في أفعال الصلاة بأن يتأخر ابتداء فعله عن ابتدائه

ويتقدم على فراغه منه فإن قارنه لم يضر إلا تكبيرة إحرام وإن تخلف بركن بأن

فرغ الإمام منه وهو فيما قبله لم تبطل في الأصح أو بركنين بأن فرغ منهما

وهو فيما قبلهما فإن لم يكن عذر بطلت وإن كان بأن أسرع قراءته وركع قبل

إتمام المأموم الفاتحة فقيل: يتبعه وتسقط البقية والصحيح يتمها ويسعى خلفه

ما لم يسبق بأكثر من ثلاثة أركان مقصودة وهي الطويلة فإن سبق بأكثر فقيل:

يفارقه والأصح يتبعه فيما هو فيه ثم يتدارك بعد سلام الإمام ولو لم يتم

الفاتحة لشغله بدعاء الافتتاح فمعذور هذا كله في الموافق فأما مسبوق ركع

الإمام في فاتحته فالأصح أنه إن لم يشتغل بالافتتاح والتعوذ ترك قراءته

وركع وهو مدرك للركعة وإلا لزمه قراءة بقدره ولا يشتغل المسبوق بسنة بعد

التحرم بل بالفاتحة إلا أن يعلم إدراكها ولو علم المأموم في ركوعه أنه ترك

الفاتحة أو شك لم يعد إليها بل يصلي ركعة بعد سلام الإمام
# 
# فلو علم أو شك وقد ركع الإمام ولم يركع هو قرأها وهو متخلف بعذر وقيل:

يركع  ويتدارك بعد سلام الإمام ولو سبق إمامه بالتحرم لم تنعقد أو بالفاتحة

أو التشهد لم يضره ويجزئه وقيل: يجب إعادته ولو تقدم بفعل كركوع وسجود إن

كان بركنين بطلت وإلا فلا وقيل: تبطل بركن.
