- Root: س-و-ي (s-w-y)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Equality, levelness; two things being alike in measure or value.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Equivalence in legal standing — here, two owners whose shares are equal in zakatability.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal equality of portions; metaphorical extension to legal parity in obligation.
- Sībawayh Rule: Conditional Clause (al-Sharṭ wa al-Jawāb) — "إن اختار الغانمون تملكها" governs the apodosis "ومضى بعده حول," requiring the condition to be fulfilled before the ruling applies.
chapters.translation:
I say: Two [owners] are equal [in this ruling]. And [regarding] the spoils [taken] before division — if the combatants choose to take possession of them, and a full year (ḥawl) elapses thereafter, then [zakat is due]. And the whole [of such property] is a zakatable category (ṣinf zakawī), provided the share of each person reaches the niṣāb, or the total reaches it in a place where the rule of mixing (khilṭah) is established — then its zakat is obligatory. Otherwise, it is not obligatory.

And if a man gives as dowry (ṣadāq) a niṣāb of pasturing livestock (sā'imah), specifically designated, then its zakat becomes incumbent upon her when a full year elapses from the time of the dowering.

And if a man leases a house for four years for eighty dīnārs and receives the payment in advance, the more apparent (al-aẓhar) [view] is that he is not obliged to pay out except the zakat of what has become settled [as earned]. Thus, at the completion of the first year, he pays zakat on twenty; at the completion of the second, zakat on twenty for one year and twenty for two years; at the completion of the third, zakat on forty for one year and twenty for three years; and at the completion of the fourth, zakat on sixty for one year and twenty for four. The second [opinion] holds that he pays at the completion of the first year the zakat of the full eighty.

# Chapter
# Zakat becomes obligatory immediately (ʿalā al-fawr) when one has the capacity [to pay] — that is, when the wealth and the [eligible] categories are present. He may personally discharge the zakat of hidden wealth (al-māl al-bāṭin), and likewise of visible wealth (al-ẓāhir) according to the new [view] (al-jadīd). He may appoint an agent (tawkīl), and he may remit it to the ruler (imām). The more apparent [view] is that remitting to the ruler is superior — unless the ruler is unjust. Intention (niyyah) is obligatory, so he must intend: "This is the obligatory zakat of my wealth," or "the obligatory alms of my wealth," or similar. It is not sufficient to say "this is my obligatory [due]" — and likewise for alms, according to the soundest [view]. It is not required to specify the particular wealth [in the intention]; but if he does specify it, it does not fall upon another [portion]. The guardian (walī) is obliged to form the intention when he pays zakat on behalf of a minor or an insane person.

# And the intention of the principal suffices when remitting to the agent, according to the soundest [view]. Yet it is preferable that the agent also intend at the time of distribution. And if he pays to the sultan, the intention at his [the sultan's] end suffices; if he [the sultan] does not intend, it is still valid (yujzi') according to the correct [view], even if the sultan does intend. The soundest [view] is that the sultan is obliged to intend when he takes zakat from one who refuses [to pay], and that his intention suffices.

# Chapter
# It is not valid to advance zakat before one owns the niṣāb, but it is permissible [to advance it] before the [completion of the] year. It is not permissible to advance it for two years, according to the soundest [view]. He may advance the fiṭrah [zakat of breaking the fast] from the beginning of Ramaḍān; the correct [view] is that it is prohibited before that. It is not permissible to pay the zakat of dates before their ripening becomes apparent (budū ṣalāḥ), nor of grain before it hardens; it is permissible after both. A condition for the validity of the advanced zakat is that the owner remains eligible for the obligation until the end of the year, and that the recipient remains entitled [to receive it] at the end of the year. It is said: if [the recipient] ceases to be entitled during the year, it does not suffice him [the payer]. His [the recipient's] becoming wealthy [later] does not harm [the validity]. And if the advanced payment does not fall as zakat, [the payer] may reclaim it — if he had stipulated reclamation upon the occurrence of an impediment. The soundest [view] is that if he merely said "this is my advanced zakat," he may reclaim it; and that if he did not mention advancement and did not inform the recipient, he may not reclaim it. And if the two dispute over the basis of reclamation, the recipient is believed with his oath. Once reclamation is established and the advanced [property] is destroyed, its guarantee (ḍamān) is obligatory. The soundest [view] is that its value is assessed on the day of receipt; that if he finds it diminished, there is no compensation for the defect (arsh); and that he does not reclaim a detached increase. Delaying zakat after capacity [to pay] obligates guarantee if the wealth is destroyed. If it is destroyed before capacity, then no [guarantee]. If part of it is destroyed, the more apparent [view] is that he pays the proportionate share of what remains. And if he destroys it after the year but before capacity, zakat is not dropped; it attaches to the wealth as a claim of co-ownership (shirkah) — and in one saying, as a lien (rahn), and in another saying, as a debt upon the dhimmah. If he sells it before paying the zakat, the more apparent [view] is that the sale is void to the extent of the zakat's share and valid for the remainder.

# | The Book of Fasting (Kitāb al-Ṣiyām)

# | Introduction
# ...

# The Book of Fasting
# Fasting of Ramaḍān becomes obligatory by completing Shaʿbān as thirty [days] or by sighting the crescent [of Ramaḍān]. The sighting is established by a single just [witness] (ʿadl) — and in one saying, by two just witnesses. The condition of the single [witness] is the attribute of probity (ʿadālah), according to the soundest [view]; not a slave nor a woman [is accepted]. If we fast on [the testimony of] a single just witness and do not sight the crescent after thirty [days], we break the fast, according to the soundest [view], even if the sky is clear. And if the crescent is sighted in one town, its ruling binds the nearby town but not the distant one, according to the soundest [view]; the distance [that separates them] is the distance permitting shortening of prayer (masāfat al-qaṣr). And it is said: [the criterion] is the difference of rising-places (ikhtilāf al-maṭāliʿ).

I say: This latter is the soundest — and God knows best. And if [the sighting] is not binding upon the other town, then whoever travels from the town of sighting to [that other town] — the soundest [view] is that he conforms to them in fasting at the end [of the month]. And whoever travels from the other town to the town of sighting, and [the latter] celebrates the ʿĪd, he celebrates with them and makes up one day [later]. And whoever begins the day [thinking it is] ʿĪd, and then his ship sails to a distant town whose inhabitants are fasting — the soundest [view] is that he refrains (yumsik) for the remainder of the day.

# Chapter
# Intention is a condition for fasting. For the obligatory [fast], it is required that it be made during the night (tabyīt). The correct [view] is that it is not required [to be made] in the latter half of the night; that eating and intercourse after it do not harm; and that it need not be renewed when one sleeps and then wakes. The supererogatory (nafl) fast is valid with an intention made before noon (zawāl) — and likewise after it, in one saying. The correct [view] is that the condition of fasting — [namely, being in a state of fasting] — must be present from the beginning of the day.

# Specification (taʿyīn) is obligatory in the obligatory [fast], and its completeness in Ramaḍān is that one intend: "I intend to fast tomorrow as the performance (adā') of the obligatory fast of Ramaḍān of this year, for God most high." Regarding performance (adā'), obligation (furūḍiyyah), and attribution to God most high, there is the same disagreement mentioned in the Book of Prayer. The correct [view] is that specifying the year is not required. And if one intends on the night of the thirtieth of Shaʿbān to fast the morrow as Ramaḍān if it should be from it, and it turns out to be from it, it does not fall [as valid] for him — unless he believed it to be from it on the basis of the word of one he trusts, whether a slave, a woman, or discerning boys. And if one intends on the night of the thirtieth of Ramaḍān to fast the morrow if it should be from Ramaḍān, it suffices him if it is from it. And if the [months] are confused for him, he fasts a month by his best judgment (ijtihād); if it coincides with what follows Ramaḍān, it suffices him, and it counts as a make-up (qaḍā'), according to the soundest [view]. If [the month] falls short and Ramaḍān was complete, he must [fast] another day. And if he errs by advancing [too early] and then reaches Ramaḍān, he must fast it [again]; otherwise, the new [view] holds that make-up is obligatory. And if a menstruating woman intends to fast the morrow before her blood ceases, and then it ceases at night, it is valid if the greater part of menstruation has been completed for her during the night — and likewise the extent of her usual habit (al-ʿādah), according to the soundest [view].

chapters.title_en: The Conditions of Fasting: Abstention, Valid States, and Obligations
chapters.arabic_text:
# فصل
# شرط الصوم الإمساك عن الجماع والاستقاءة والصحيح انه لو تيقن أنه لم يرجع

شيء إلى جوفه بطل وإن غلبه القيء فلا بأس وكذا لو اقتلع نخامة ولفظها في

الأصح فلو نزلت من دماغه وحصلت في حد الظاهر من الفم فليقطعها من مجراها

وليمجها فإن تركها مع القدرة فوصلت الجوف أفطر في الأصح وعن وصول العين إلى

ما يسمى جوفا وقيل: يشترط مع هذا أن يكون فيه قوة تحيل الغذاء أو الدواء

فعلى الوجهين باطن الدماغ والبطن والأمعاء والمثانة مفطر بالاستعاط أو

الأكل أو الحقنة أو الوصول من جائفة أو مأمومة ونحوهما والتقطير في باطن

الأذن وإلا حليل مفطر في الأصح وشرط الواصل كونه من منفذ مفتوح فلا يضر

وصول الدهن بتشرب المسام ولا الاكتحال وإن وجد طعمه بحلقه وكونه بقصد فلو

وصل جوفه ذباب أو بعوضة أو غبار الطريق أو غربلة الدقيق لم يفطر ولا يفطر

ببلع ريقه من معدنه فلو  خرج عن الفم ثم رده وابتلعه أو بل خيطا بريقه ورده

إلى فمه وعليه رطوبة تنفصل أو ابتلع ريقه مخلوطا بغيره أو متنجسا أفطر ولو

جمع ريقه فابتلعه لم يفطر في الأصح ولو سبق ماء المضمضة أو الاستنشاق إلى

جوفه فالمذهب أنه إن بالغ
# 
# أفطر وإلا فلا ولو بقي طعام بين أسنانه فجرى به ريقه لم يفطر إن عجر عن

تمييزه ومجه ولو أوجر مكرها لم يفطر وإن أكره حتى أكل أفطر في الأظهر.
# قلت: الأظهر لا يفطر والله أعلم وإن أكل ناسيا لم يفطر إلا أن يكثر في

الأصح قلت: الأصح لا يفطر والله أعلم والجماع كالأكل على المذهب وعن

الاستمناء فيفطر به وكذا خروج المنى بلمس وقبلة ومضاجعة لا فكر ونظر بشهوة

وتكره القبلة لمن حركت شهوته والأولى لغيره تركها.
# قلت: هي كراهة تحريم في الأصح والله أعلم ولا يفطر بالقصد والحجامة

والاحتياط أن لا يأكل آخر النهار إلا بيقين ويحل بالاجتهاد في الأصح ويجوز

إذا ظن بقاء الليل.
# قلت: وكذا لو شك والله أعلم ولو أكل باجتهاد أولا أو آخر أو بان الغلط

بطل صومه أو بلا ظن ولم يبن الحال صح إن وقع في أوله وبطل في آخره ولو طلع

الفجر وفي فمه طعام فلفظه صح صومه وكذا لو كان مجامعا فنزع في الحال فإن

مكث بطل.

# فصل
# شرط الصوم الإسلام والعقل والنقاء عن الحيض والنفاس جميع النهار ولا يضر

النوم المستغرق على الصحيح والأظهر أن الإغماء لا يضر إذا أفاق لحظة من

نهار ولا يصح صوم العيد وكذا التشريق في الجديد ولا يحل التطوع يوم الشك

بلا سبب فلو صامه لم يصح في الأصح وله صومه عن القضاء والنذر وكذا لو وافق

عادة تطوعه وهو يوم الثلاثين من شعبان إذا تحدث الناس برؤيته أو شهد بها

صبيان أو عبيد أو فسقة وليس إطباق العيم بشك ويسن تعجيل الفطر على تمر وإلا

فماء وتأخير السحور ما لم يقع في شك وليصن لسانه عن الكذب والغيبة ونفسه  عن

الشهوات ويستحب أن يغتسل عن الجنابة قبل الفجر وأن يحترز
# 
# عن الحجامة والقبلة وذوق الطعام والعلك وأن يقول عند فطره اللهم لك صمت

وعلى رزقك أفطرت وأن يكثر الصدقة وتلاوة القرآن في رمضان وأن يعتكف لا سيما

في العشر الأواخر منه.

# فصل
# شرط وجوب صوم رمضان العقل والبلوغ وإطاقته ويؤمر به الصبي لسبع إذا أطاق

ويباح تركه للمريض إذا وجد به ضررا شديدا وللمسافر سفرا طويلا مباحا ولو

أصبح صائما فمرض أفطر وإن سافر فلا ولو أصبح المسافر والمريض صائمين ثم

أراد الفطر جاز فلو أقام وشفى حرم الفطر على الصحيح وإذا أفطر المسافر

والمريض قضيا وكذا الحائض والمفطر بلا عذر وتارك النية ويجب قضاء ما فات

بالإغماء والردة دون الكفر الأصلي والصبا والجنون وإذا بلغ بالنهار صائما

وجب إتمامه بلا قضاء ولو بلغ فيه مفطرا أو أفاق أو أسلم فلا قضاء في الأصح

ولا يلزمهم إمساك بقية النهار في الأصح ويلزم من تعدى بالفطر أو نسي النية

لا مسافرا ومريضا زال عذرهما بعد الفطر ولو زال قبل أن يأكلا ولم ينويا

ليلا فكذا في المذهب والأظهر أنه يلزم من أكل يوم الشك ثم ثبت كونه من

رمضان وإمساك بقية اليوم من خواص رمضان بخلاف النذر والقضاء.
chapters.anchors:
- Root: أ-م-س-ك (amsaka)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To hold back, restrain, or withhold; physical retention of the self from an action.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In fasting (ṣawm), it denotes the deliberate cessation from appetitive acts as an act of devotional obedience (ʿibādah).
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal (ḥaqīqah) in the sense of physical restraint; metaphorical (majāz) when applied to the tongue or inner faculties.
- Sībawayh Rule: Conditional Clause (al-Sharṭ) — The particle 'law' introduces a hypothetical protasis whose apodosis is governed by the established legal ruling (ḥukm), requiring precise parsing of the conditional sequence.
chapters.translation:
I say: The condition of fasting is abstention from sexual intercourse and from deliberate vomiting. The sound opinion (al-ṣaḥīḥ) is that if one is certain that nothing returned to his interior (jawf), [his fast is not broken]; but if vomiting overcame him involuntarily, there is no harm. Likewise, if one dislodges phlegm from his chest and expels it, [this does not break the fast] according to the most correct view (al-aṣaḥḥ). If it descends from his brain and reaches the apparent limit of the mouth, let him sever it from its passage and spit it out; if he leaves it while able [to expel it] and it reaches the interior, he breaks his fast according to the most correct view. [The ruling] concerns the reaching of a substance into what is termed an 'interior' (jawf). And it is said: it is additionally required that [the cavity] contain a power that transforms food or medicine. On both views, the interior of the brain, the belly, the intestines, and the bladder are rendered fast-breaking by snuffing [medicine], eating, enema, or by [a substance] reaching [the body] through a penetrating wound (jāʾifah) or a skull wound (maʾmūmah) and the like. Instilling [medicine] into the inner ear, and [similarly] the urethra (iḥlīl), breaks the fast according to the most correct view. A condition of the reaching substance is that it enter through an open passage (manfadh maftūḥ); thus, oil penetrating through the pores does not harm, nor does kohl [applied to the eyes] even if one finds its taste in his throat. And [a further condition] is that it be deliberate; if a fly, mosquito, road dust, or sifted flour enters his interior, he does not break his fast. Nor does he break his fast by swallowing his own saliva from its source. But if it exits the mouth and he returns it and swallows it, or he moistens a thread with his saliva and returns it to his mouth while it has separable moisture, or he swallows his saliva mixed with something else or with impurity, he breaks his fast. If he gathers his saliva and swallows it, he does not break his fast according to the most correct view. If water from rinsing the mouth (maḍmaḍah) or snuffing (istinshāq) precedes [unintentionally] into his interior, the school’s position (al-madhhab) is that if he exaggerated [in the rinsing], he breaks his fast; otherwise, he does not. If food remains between his teeth and his saliva flows over it, he does not break his fast if he is unable to distinguish it and spit it out. If one is forced to drink against his will, he does not break his fast; but if he is coerced until he eats, he breaks his fast according to the most apparent view (al-aẓhar).
I say: The most apparent view is that he does not break his fast, and God knows best. If one eats forgetfully, he does not break his fast, unless [the forgetful eating] is excessive, according to the most correct view.
I say: The most correct view is that he does not break his fast, and God knows best. Sexual intercourse is like eating according to the school. Regarding masturbation (istimnāʾ), [the school holds] that it breaks the fast; likewise, the emission of semen by touching, kissing, or lying together—but not by thought or lustful looking. Kissing is disliked (makrūh) for one whose desire is stirred, and for another it is preferable to avoid it.
I say: It is a disliked-of-prohibition (karāhah taḥrīm) according to the most correct view, and God knows best. He does not break his fast by [mere] intention or by cupping (ḥijāmah). Prudence dictates that one not eat at the end of the day except with certainty; but it is permissible [to eat] based on ijtihād (legal estimation) according to the most correct view, and it is permitted when one supposes the night remains.
I say: Likewise, if he doubts, and God knows best. If one eats based on ijtihād at the beginning or end [of the night], and then error becomes apparent, his fast is invalidated. If he eats without supposition and the matter is not clarified, his fast is valid if it occurred at the beginning [of the night] and invalid if at the end. If dawn breaks while food is in his mouth and he spits it out, his fast is valid. Likewise, if he was in intercourse and withdrew immediately, [his fast is valid]; but if he lingered, it is invalidated.

I say: The conditions of fasting are Islam, sanity, and purity from menstruation and postpartum bleeding for the entire day. Deep sleep does not harm [the fast] according to the sound opinion (al-ṣaḥīḥ). The most apparent view is that unconsciousness does not harm if one regains consciousness for a moment during the day. The fast of the Day of Fitr is not valid, nor is that of the Days of Tashrīq according to the new view (al-jadīd). Voluntary fasting on the Day of Doubt (yawm al-shakk) is not permissible without a cause; if one fasts it, it is not valid according to the most correct view. But he may fast it for a make-up (qaḍāʾ) or a vow (nadhr). Likewise, if it coincides with his habitual voluntary fast, and it is the thirtieth of Shaʿbān when people speak of sighting [the crescent] or boys, slaves, or sinners testify to it. The consensus of the masses is not [a cause of] doubt. It is recommended (sunna) to hasten the breaking of the fast with dates, or else with water, and to delay the pre-dawn meal (saḥūr) as long as it does not fall into doubt. Let him guard his tongue from lying and backbiting, and his soul from lusts. It is recommended that he perform the major ablution (ghusl) from janābah before dawn, and that he be cautious of cupping, kissing, tasting food, and chewing gum. Let him say at his breaking of the fast: 'O God, for You I fasted, and upon Your provision I break my fast.' Let him increase charity and recitation of the Quran in Ramadan, and let him perform iʿtikāf (seclusion), especially in the last ten nights thereof.

I say: The conditions for the obligation of fasting Ramadan are sanity, puberty, and ability. A boy is commanded to [fast] at seven years if he is able. It is permissible for the sick to omit fasting if he experiences severe harm, and for the traveler on a long, permissible journey. If one begins the day fasting and then becomes sick, he may break his fast; if he travels, [he may also break it]. If a traveler and a sick person begin the day fasting and then wish to break, it is permissible. But if the traveler settles [in a place] and the sick recovers, breaking becomes forbidden according to the sound opinion. When the traveler and the sick break their fast, they must make it up; likewise, the menstruating woman, the one who breaks without excuse, and the one who omits the intention. It is obligatory to make up what was missed due to unconsciousness and apostasy (riddah), but not due to original unbelief, childhood, or insanity. If one reaches puberty during the day while fasting, he must complete it without a make-up. If he reaches puberty during the day while not fasting, or an unbeliever embraces Islam, or an insane person recovers, there is no make-up according to the most correct view, nor are they required to abstain for the rest of the day according to the most correct view. It is incumbent upon one who transgresses by breaking his fast or forgets the intention—not being a traveler or sick whose excuse has ceased after breaking—[to abstain]. If the excuse ceases before they eat and they had not intended [the fast] the night before, the same applies in the school. The most apparent view is that it is incumbent upon one who eats on the Day of Doubt and then it is confirmed that it was from Ramadan [to abstain for the rest of the day]. Abstention for the rest of the day is a specific characteristic of Ramadan, unlike the vowed fast or the make-up fast.

chapters.title_en: Section 23 — Missed Fasts, Expiation, Voluntary Fasting, and Seclusion (Iʿtikāf)
chapters.arabic_text:
# فصل
# من فاته شيء من رمضان فمات قبل إمكان القضاء فلا تدارك له ولا إثم وإن

مات بعد التمكن لم يصم عنه وليه في الجديد بل يخرج من تركته لكل يوم مد

طعام وكذا النذر والكفارة.
# 
# قلت: القديم هنا أظهر والولي كل قريب على المختار ولو صام أجنبي بإذن

الولي صح لا مستقلا في الأصح ولو مات وعليه صلاة أو اعتكاف لم يفعل عنه ولا

فدية وفي الاعتكاف قول والله أعلم والأظهر وجوب المد على من أفطر للكبر

وأما الحامل والمرضع فإن أفطرتا خوفا على نفسهما وجب القضاء بلا فدية أو

على الولد لزمتهما الفدية في الأظهر والأصح أنه يلحق بالمرضع من أفطر

لإنقاذ مشرف على هلاك لا المتعدي بفطر رمضان بغير  جماع ومن أخر قضاء رمضان

مع إمكانه حتى دخل رمضان آخر لزمه مع القضاء لكل يوم مد والأصح تكرره بتكرر

السنين وإنه لو أخر القضاء مع إمكانه فمات أخرج من تركته لكل يوم مدان مد

للفوات ومد للتأخير ومصرف الفدية الفقراء والمساكين وله صرف إمداد إلى شخص

واحد وجنسها جنس الفطرة.

# فصل
# تجب الكفارة فإفساد صوم يوم من رمضان بجماع أثم به بسبب الصوم فلا كفارة

على ناس ولا مفسد غير رمضان أو بغير الجماع ولا مسافر جامع بنية الترخص

وكذا بغيرها في الأصح ولا على من ظن الليل فبان نهارا ولا على من جامع بعد

الأكل ناسيا وظن أنه أفطر به وإن كان الأصح بطلان صومه ولا من زنى ناسيا

ولا مسافر أفطر بالزنا مترخصا والكفارة على الزوج عنه وفي قول عنه وعنها

وفي قول عليها كفارة أخرى وتلزم من انفرد برؤية الهلال وجامع في يومه ومن

جامع في يومين لزمه كفارتان وحدوث السفر بعد الجماع لا يسقط الكفارة وكذا

المرض على المذهب ويجب معها قضاء يوم الإفساد على الصحيح وهي عتق رقبة

مؤمنة فإن لم يجد فصيام شهرين متتابعين فإن لم يستطع فإطعام
# 
# ستين مسكينا فلو عجز عن الجميع استقرت في ذمته في الأظهر فإذا قدر على

خصلة فعلها والأصح أن له العدول عن الصوم إلى الإطعام لشدة الغلمة وأنه لا

يجوز للفقير صرف كفارته إلى عياله.
# 

| باب صوم التطوع
# يسن صوم الاثنين والخميس وعرفة وعاشوراء وتاسوعاء وأيام البيض وستة من

شوال وتتابعها أفضل ويكره إفراد الجمعة وإفراد السبت وصوم الدهر غير العيد

والتشريق مكروه لمن خاف به ضررا أو فوت حق ومستحب لغيره ومن تلبس بصوم تطوع

أو صلاته فله قطعهما ولا قضاء ومن تلبس بقضاء حرم عليه قطعه إن كان على

الفور وهو صوم من تعدى بالفطر. وكذا إن لم يكن على الفور في الأصح بأن لم

يكن تعدى بالفطر.
# 

| كتاب الاعتكاف
# هو مستحب كل وقت وفي العشر الأواخر من رمضان أفضل لطلب ليلة القدر وميل 

الشافعي رحمه الله إلى أنها ليلة الحادي أو الثالث والعشرين وإنما يصح

الاعتكاف في المسجد والجامع أولى والجديد أنه لا يصح اعتكاف امرأة في مسجد

بيتها وهو المعتزل المهيأ للصلاة ولو عين المسجد الحرام في نذره الاعتكاف

تعين وكذا مسجد المدينة والأقصى في الأظهر ويقوم المسجد الحرام مقامهما ولا

عكس ويقوم مسجد المدينة مقام الأقصى ولا عكس والأصح أنه يشترط في الاعتكاف

لبث قدر يسمى عكوفا وقيل: يكفي مرور بلا لبث وقيل: يشترط مكث نحو يوم ويبطل

بالجماع وأظهر الأقوال أن المباشرة بشهوة كلمس وقبلة تبطله إن أنزل وإلا

فلا ولو جامع ناسيا فكجماع الصائم ولا يضر التطيب والتزين والفطر بل يصح

اعتكاف الليل وحده ولو نذر اعتكاف يوم هو فيه صائم لزمه ولو نذر أن يعتكف

صائما أو يصوم معتكفا لزماه والأصح وجوب جمعهما ويشترط نية الاعتكاف وينوي

في النذر الفرضية وإذا أطلق كفته نيته وإن طال مكثه لكن لو خرج وعاد احتاج

إلى الاستئناف ولو نوى مدة فخرج فيها وعاد فإن خرج لغير قضاء الحاجة لزمه

الاستئناف أولها فلا وقيل: إن طالت مدة خروجه استأنف وقيل: لا يستأنف مطلقا

ولو نذر مدة متتابعة فخرج لعذر لا يقطع التتابع لم يجب استئناف النية وقيل:

إن خرج لغير حاجة وغسل الجنابة وجب وشرط المعتكف الإسلام والعقل والنقاء عن

الحيض والجنابة ولو
# 
# ارتد المعتكف أو سكر بطل والمذهب بطلان ما مضى من اعتكافهما المتتابع ولو

طرأ جنون أو إغماء لم يبطل ما مضى إن لم يخرج ويحسب زمن الإغماء من

الاعتكاف دون الجنون أو الحيض وجب الخروج وكذا جنابة إن تعذر الغسل في

المسجد فلو أمكن جاز الخروج ولا يلزم ولا يحسب زمن الحيض ولا الجنابة.
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ف-و-ت (f-w-t)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Loss, passing by, escaping; something that elapses without being seized.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Temporal lapse of an obligatory act beyond its appointed time; irrecoverability in this world.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal for time passing; metaphorical for the loss of merit or obligation.
- Root: ك-ف-ر (k-f-r)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Covering, veiling, concealing; expiation as covering over sin.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Atonement (kaffārah) — an act that veils the offense before God.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal: covering; metaphorical: the prescribed penance that obscures the fault.
- Root: ع-ك-ف (ʿ-k-f)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To remain, stay, cleave to a place; devotion through lingering.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Ritual seclusion in a mosque for worship, a form of spiritual clinging.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal: physical lingering; metaphorical: the soul's adherence to divine service.
- Sībawayh Rule: Conditional and Exceptive Constructions (al-sharṭ wa al-istithnāʾ) — Governing the nuanced legal conditions (e.g., "if... then...", "except...") with precise apodosis and protasis.
chapters.translation:
I say: Know that whoever misses any part of Ramadan, then dies before the possibility of making it up (al-qadāʾ) becomes available — there is no making it up for him, nor is there any sin upon him. But if he dies after being able to make it up, his guardian (walī) does not fast on his behalf in the new opinion (al-jadīd); rather, from his estate there is given for each day a mudd of food. Likewise for a vow (al-nadhr) and an expiation (al-kaffārah).

I say: The old opinion (al-qadīm) here is more apparent (aẓhar). The guardian is any relative (qarīb) in the chosen view (al-mukhtār). And if a stranger fasts with the guardian's permission, it is valid — but not independently, in the most correct view (al-aṣaḥḥ). And if he dies owing prayers (ṣalāh) or seclusion (iʿtikāf), it is not done on his behalf, nor is there any ransom (fidyah) — though concerning seclusion there is a saying (qawl). And God knows best. The most apparent view (al-aẓhar) is the obligation of a mudd upon one who breaks the fast due to old age (al-kibar). As for the pregnant woman and the nursing mother — if they break the fast out of fear for themselves, the qadāʾ is obligatory without fidyah; but if out of fear for the child, the fidyah is incumbent upon them in the most apparent view. And the most correct view (al-aṣaḥḥ) is that one who breaks the fast to rescue a person on the brink of destruction is joined to the nursing mother — not the one who transgresses by breaking the fast of Ramadan without intercourse. And whoever delays the qadāʾ of Ramadan while able to do so until another Ramadan enters — there is incumbent upon him, along with the qadāʾ, a mudd for each day. And the most correct view is that it is repeated with the repetition of the years. And if he delays the qadāʾ while able, then dies, there is taken from his estate for each day two mudds: a mudd for the loss (al-fawāt) and a mudd for the delay (al-taʾkhīr). The channel for the fidyah is the poor (al-fuqarāʾ) and the destitute (al-masākīn). And he may give multiple mudds to a single person. Its kind (jins) is the kind of the alms of breaking the fast (fiṭrah).

I say: The expiation (al-kaffārah) is obligatory for corrupting the fast of a day of Ramadan by intercourse — sinning thereby because of the fast. Thus there is no expiation upon one who forgets, nor upon one who corrupts a fast other than Ramadan, nor by other than intercourse. Nor upon a traveler who has intercourse with the intention of availing the concession (al-tarakhkhuṣ). Likewise, in the most correct view, not upon one who does so without that intention. Nor upon one who thought it was night, then it became clear it was day. Nor upon one who has intercourse after eating out of forgetfulness, thinking he had thereby broken his fast — even though the most correct view is that his fast is invalidated. Nor upon one who commits fornication (zinā) forgetfully, nor upon a traveler who breaks his fast by fornication while availing the concession. The expiation is upon the husband on his own behalf; in one saying (qawl), on his behalf and hers; and in one saying, upon her another expiation. It is incumbent upon one who alone sights the crescent (al-hilāl) and has intercourse on that day. And whoever has intercourse on two days — two expiations are incumbent upon him. The occurrence of travel after intercourse does not drop the expiation; likewise illness, in the school (al-madhhab). Along with it, the qadāʾ of the corrupted day is obligatory in the sound view (al-ṣaḥīḥ). It is the freeing of a believing slave; if he finds none, then fasting two consecutive months; if he cannot, then feeding sixty poor persons. If he is incapable of all of these, it remains established as a debt upon him (mustaqirrah fī dhimmatihi) in the most apparent view; when he becomes able to do any one of them, he does it. And the most correct view is that he may shift from fasting to feeding due to intense sexual desire (shiddat al-ghulmah). And it is not permissible for the poor person to direct his expiation to his own dependents.

| Chapter on Voluntary Fasting (Ṣawm al-Taṭawwuʿ)

I say: Fasting Monday and Thursday, the Day of ʿArafah, ʿĀshūrāʾ, Tāsūʿāʾ, the white days (al-ayyām al-bīḍ), and six days of Shawwāl is Sunnah. Their consecutiveness is more virtuous. It is disliked (makrūh) to single out Friday, and to single out Saturday. Fasting perpetually (ṣawm al-dahr) — other than on the two ʿĪds and the days of al-Tashrīq — is disliked for one who fears harm thereby or the loss of a right, and it is recommended (mustaḥabb) for one other than that. Whoever enters upon a voluntary fast or a voluntary prayer — he may break both of them, and there is no qadāʾ upon him. But whoever enters upon a qadāʾ — it is forbidden for him to break it if it is immediate (ʿalā al-fawr), which is the fast of one who transgressed by breaking the fast. Likewise, in the most correct view, even if it is not immediate — namely, when one has not transgressed by breaking the fast.

| Book of Seclusion (Iʿtikāf)

I say: It is recommended (mustaḥabb) at all times, and in the last ten days of Ramadan it is more virtuous, in pursuit of the Night of Decree (laylat al-qadr). Al-Shāfiʿī — may God have mercy on him — inclined to the view that it is the twenty-first or the twenty-third night. Seclusion is only valid in a mosque; the congregational mosque (al-jāmiʿ) is more virtuous. The new opinion (al-jadīd) is that a woman's seclusion is not valid in the mosque of her house — that is, the secluded place prepared for prayer. If one specifies the Sacred Mosque (al-masjid al-ḥarām) in his vow of seclusion, it becomes determined (taʿayyana); likewise the Mosque of Medina and al-Aqṣā in the most apparent view. The Sacred Mosque stands in place of both of them, but not the reverse. The Mosque of Medina stands in place of al-Aqṣā, but not the reverse. The most correct view is that seclusion requires a lingering (lubth) of an amount that can be called "secluding" (ʿukūf). It was said: passing through without lingering suffices. And it was said: a stay of about a day is required. It is invalidated by intercourse. And the most manifest of the sayings is that intimate touching with desire — like touching and kissing — invalidates it if it leads to emission; otherwise not. If one has intercourse forgetfully, it is like the intercourse of the fasting person. Perfuming, adorning, and eating do not harm it. Rather, seclusion at night alone is valid. If one vows to seclude on a day in which he is fasting, it is incumbent upon him. If one vows to seclude while fasting, or to fast while secluding, both are incumbent upon him; and the most correct view is the obligation of combining them. The intention (niyyah) of seclusion is required; in a vow, one intends obligation (al-farḍiyyah). If he makes it absolute (muṭlaq), his intention suffices him, even if his stay is prolonged. But if he leaves and returns, he needs to recommence (al-istīʾnāf). If he intends a specified period and leaves during it, then returns — if he left for other than relieving a need, he must recommence from its beginning; so it is said. And it was said: if his period of leaving is prolonged, he recommences. And it was said: he does not recommence at all. If he vows a consecutive period and leaves for an excuse that does not break the consecutiveness, recommencing the intention is not obligatory. It was said: if he leaves for other than a need, and for the washing of major impurity (ghusl al-janābah), it is obligatory. The conditions of the one secluding are Islam, sanity, and purity from menstruation and major impurity. And if the one secluding apostatizes (irtadda) or becomes intoxicated, it is invalidated. The school holds the invalidation of what has passed of their consecutive seclusion. If madness (junūn) or unconsciousness (ighmāʾ) occurs, what has passed is not invalidated if he does not leave; and the time of unconsciousness is counted from the seclusion — unlike madness. Or menstruation — then leaving is obligatory. Likewise major impurity, if washing in the mosque is impossible; if it is possible, leaving is permissible but not obligatory. The time of menstruation is not counted, nor that of madness.

# فصل
# إذا نذر متتابعة لزمه والصحيح أنه لا يجب التتابع بلا شرط وأنه لو نذر

يوما لم يجز تفريق ساعاته وأنه لو عين مدة كأسبوع وتعرض للتتابع وفاته لزمه

التتابع في القضاء وإن لم يتعرض له لم يلزمه في القضاء وإذا ذكر التتابع

وشرط الخروج  لعارض صح الشرط في الأظهر والزمان المصروف إليه لا يجب تداركه

إن عين المدة كهذا الشهر وإلا فيجب وينقطع التتابع بالخروج بلا عذر ولا يضر

إخراج بعض الأعضاء ولا الخروج لقضاء الحاجة ولا يجب فعلها في غير داره ولا

يضر بعدها إلا أن يفحش فيضر في الأصح ولو عاد مريضا في طريقه لم يضر ما لم

يطل وقوفه أو يعدل عن طريقه ولا ينقطع التتابع بمرض يحوج إلى الخروج ولا

بحيض إن طالت مدة الاعتكاف فإن كانت بحيث تخلو عنه انقطع في الأظهر ولا

بخروج ناسيا على المذهب ولا بخروج مؤذن راتب إلى منارة منفصلة عن المسجد

للأذان في الأصح ويجب قضاء أوقات الخروج بالأعذار إلا وقت قضاء الحاجة.
# 

| كتاب الحج

| مدخل
# ...
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ت-ب-ع (t-b-ʿ)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Sequential following, one thing trailing another without gap.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Technical term for legal continuity (tawātur) in devotional acts, implying unbroken succession.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal (ḥaqīqah) for physical succession; metaphorical (majāz) for legal obligation of unbroken sequence.
- Root: ق-ض-ي (q-ḍ-y)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To fulfill, complete, or render a judgment; here, making up a missed obligation.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Judicial completion of a deficient act; in fiqh, compensatory performance.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal for settling a debt; metaphorical for religious reparation.
- Root: ع-ز-ل (ʿ-z-l)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Separation, withdrawal, or setting apart.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In iʿtikāf, temporary exit for a legitimate cause (ʿudhr), not a breach of devotion.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal physical departure; metaphorical for legal exemption.
- Sībawayh Rule: Conditional Clause (al-sharṭ wa al-jawāb) — The particle "law" (لو) introduces a hypothetical condition; the apodosis (jawāb) is governed by the protasis, requiring precise parsing of whether the condition (e.g., stipulating tawātur) alters the legal consequence.
chapters.translation:
I say: If one vows consecutive fasting, it is binding upon him. The soundest position (al-ṣaḥīḥ) is that consecutiveness is not obligatory without an explicit stipulation. And if he vows a single day, it is not permissible to disperse its hours. And if he specifies a period, such as a week, and stipulates consecutiveness, then if he misses it, consecutiveness becomes obligatory in the make-up (al-qaḍāʾ). But if he did not stipulate it, it is not obligatory in the make-up. And when he mentions consecutiveness and stipulates the condition of exiting for an incidental cause, the condition is valid in the stronger view (al-aẓhar). The time spent in such exit need not be compensated if he specified the period, like "this month"; otherwise, it must be compensated. Consecutiveness is broken by exiting without an excuse. It does not harm to exit some parts of the body, nor to exit for relieving oneself. It is not obligatory to do so outside his dwelling, nor does it harm after that, unless the exit becomes excessive, in which case it harms in the soundest view (al-aṣaḥḥ). And if a sick person returns along his path, it does not harm as long as his standing is not prolonged, nor does he deviate from his route. Consecutiveness is not broken by an illness that necessitates exiting, nor by menstruation if the period of iʿtikāf is long; but if the menstruation is such that the place becomes vacant of him, it is broken in the stronger view (al-aẓhar). Nor is it broken by an unintentional exit, according to the school’s position (al-madhhab). Nor by the exit of a regular muezzin to a minaret detached from the mosque for the call to prayer, in the soundest view (al-aṣaḥḥ). It is obligatory to make up the times of exits due to excuses, except for the time of relieving oneself.

chapters.arabic_text:
# كتاب الحج
# هو فرض وكذا العمرة في الأظهر وشرط صحته الإسلام فللوي أن يحرم عن الصبي

الذي لا يميز والمجنون وإنما تصح مباشرته من المسلم المميز وإنما يقع عن

حجة الإسلام بالمباشرة إذا باشره المكلف الحر فيجزىء حج الفقير دون الصبي

والعبد وشرط وجوبه الإسلام والتكليف والحرية والاستطاعة وهي نوعان أحدهما:

استطاعة مباشرة ولها شروط.
# أحدها: وجود الزاد وأوعيته ومؤنة ذهابه وإيابه وقيل: إن لم يكن له ببلده

أهل وعشيرة لم تشترط نفقة الإياب فلو كان يكتسب كل يوم ما يفي بزاده وسفره

طويل لم يكلف الحج وإن قصر وهو يكتسب في يوم كفاية أيام كلف.
# الثاني: وجود الراحلة لمن بينه وبين مكة مرحلتان فإن لحقته بالراحلة مشقة

شديدة اشترط وجود محمل واشترط شريك يجلس في الشق الآخر ومن بينه وبينها دون

مرحلتين وهو قوي على المشي يلزمه الحج فإن ضعف فكالبعيد ويشترط كون الزاد

والراحلة فاضلين عن دينه ومؤنة من عليه نفقتهم مدة ذهابه وإيابه والأصح

اشتراط كونه فاضلا عن مسكنه وعبد يحتاج إليه لخدمته وأنه يلزمه صرف مال

تجارته إليهما.
# الثالث: أمن الطريق فلو خاف على نفسه أو ماله سبعا أو عدوا أو رصديا ولا

طريق
# 
# سواه لم يجب الحج والأظهر وجوب ركوب البحر إن غلبت  السلامة وأنه يلزمه

أجرة البذرقة ويشترط وجود الماء والزاد في المواضع المعتاد حمله منها بثمن

المثل وهو القدر اللائق به في ذلك الزمان والمكان وعلف الدابة في كل مرحلة

وفي المرأة أن يخرج معها زوج أو محرم أو نسوة ثقات والأصح أنه لا يشترط

وجود محرم لإحداهن وأنه يلزمها أجرة المحرم إذا لم يخرج إلا بها.
# الرابع: أن يثبت على الراحلة بلا مشقة شديدة وعلى الأعمى الحج إن وجد

قائدا وهو كالمحرم في حق المرأة والمحجور عليه لسفه كغيره لكن لا يدفع

المال إليه بل يخرج معه الولي أو ينصب شخصا له.
# النوع الثاني: استطاعة تحصيله بغيره فمن مات وفي ذمته حج وجب الإحجاج عنه

من تركته والمعضوب العاجز عن الحج بنفسه إن وجد أجرة من يحج عنه بأجرة

المثل لزمه ويشترط كونها فاضلة عن الحاجات المذكورة فيمن حج بنفسه لكن لا

يشترط نفقة العيال ذهابا وإيابا ولو بذل ولده أو أجنبي مالا للأجرة لم يجب

قبوله في الأصح ولو بذل الولد الطاعة وجب قبوله وكذا الأجنبي في الأصح.
# 

| باب المواقيت
# وقت إحرام الحج شوال وذو القعدة وعشر ليال من ذي الحجة وفي ليلة النحر

وجه فلو أحرم به في غير وقته انعقد عمرة على الصحيح وجميع السنة وقت لإحرام

العمرة والميقات المكاني للحج في حق من بمكة نفس مكة وقيل: كل الحرم وأما

غيره فميقات
# 
# المتوجه من المدينة ذو الحليفة ومن الشام ومصر والمغرب الجحفة ومن تهامة

اليمن يلملم ومن نجد الحجاز قرن ومن المشرق ذات عرق والأفضل أن يحرم من أول

الميقات ويجوز من آخره ومن سلك طريقا لا ينتهي إلى ميقات فإن حاذى ميقاتا

أحرم من محاذاته أو ميقاتين فالأصح أنه يحرم من محاذاة أبعدهما وإن لم يحاذ

أحرم على مرحلتين من مكة ومن مسكنه بين مكة والميقات فميقاته مسكنه ومن بلغ

ميقاتا غيرت مريد نسكا ثم أراده فميقاته موضعه وإن بلغه مريدا لم تجز

مجاوزته بغير إحرام فإن فعل لزمه العود ليحرم منه إلا إذا ضاق  الوقت أو كان

الطريق مخوفا فإن لم يعد لزمه دام وإن أحرم ثم عاد فالأصح أنه إن عاد قبل

تلبسه بنسك سقط الدم وإلا فلا والأفضل أن يحرم من دويرة أهله وفي قول من

الميقات قلت: الميقات أظهر وهو الموافق للأحاديث الصحيحة والله أعلم وميقات

العمرة لمن هو خارج الحرم ميقات الحج ومن بالحرم يلزمه الخروج إلى أدنى

الحل ولو بخطوة فإن لم يخرج وأتى بأفعال العمرة أجزأته في الأظهر وعليه دم

فلو خرج إلى الحل بعد إحرامه سقط الدم على المذهب وأفضل بقاع الحل الجعرانة

ثم التنعيم ثم الحديبية.
# 

| باب الإحرام
# ينعقد معينا بأن ينوي حجا أو عمرة أو كليهما ومطلقا بأن لا يزيد على نفس

الإحرام والتعيين أفضل وفي قول الإطلاق فإن أحرم مطلقا في أشهر الحج صرفه

بالنية إلى ما شاء من النسكين أو إليهما ثم اشتغل بالأعمال وإن أطلق في غير

أشهره فالأصح انعقاده عمرة فلا يصرفه إلى الحج في أشهره وله أن يحرم كإحرام

زيد فإن لم يكن زيد محرما انعقد إحرامه مطلقا وقيل: إن علم عدم إحرام زيد

لم ينعقد وإن كان زيد محرما انعقد إحرامه
# 
# كإحرامه فإن تعذر معرفة إحرامه بموته جعل نفسه قارنا وعمل أعمال النسكين.
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ح-ج-ج (ḥ-j-j)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To repair to a place repeatedly; the pilgrimage to the Sacred House as a ritual of visitation (al-qaṣd).
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): The intended journey to the Kaʿbah for the performance of its rites; a divinely ordained act of worship (ʿibādah) with fixed conditions.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal (ḥaqīqah) for physical journeying; metaphorical (majāz) for the soul's intent toward God.
- Sībawayh Rule: Conditional Clause Sequencing (al-Sharṭ wa al-Jawāb) — The protasis (sharṭ) governs the apodosis (jawāb) in legal stipulations, as in "if he fears... then pilgrimage is not obligatory."
chapters.translation:
I say: The Book of Pilgrimage (al-Ḥajj). It is an obligation (farḍ), and likewise ʿUmrah is obligatory in the more apparent position (al-aẓhar). The condition of its validity is Islam. Thus, it is permissible for a guardian (walī) to assume the state of iḥrām on behalf of a young child who lacks discernment (tamyīz) and on behalf of the insane. Its direct performance (mubāsharah) is only valid from a Muslim who possesses discernment. It is only reckoned as the Pilgrimage of Islam (ḥijjat al-Islām) by direct performance when the legally responsible (mukallaf), free person performs it. Thus, the pilgrimage of the poor person suffices, but not that of the young child or the slave.

The conditions of its obligation are: Islam, legal responsibility (taklīf), freedom, and capacity (istiṭāʿah). Capacity is of two types. The first: direct capacity (istiṭāʿah mubāsharah), which has conditions.

One of them: The existence of provisions (zād) and their containers, and the expense of his going and returning. It was said: If he has no family and kin in his own land, the expense of return (nafaqat al-iyāb) is not stipulated. Thus, if he could earn each day what suffices for his provisions, but his journey is long, he is not obligated to perform the pilgrimage. But if it is short, and he earns in one day what suffices for the days [of travel], he is obligated.

The second: The existence of a mount (rāḥilah) for one whose distance from Mecca is two stages (marḥalatān). If severe hardship afflicts him on the mount, then the existence of a litter (maḥmil) is stipulated, and a companion is stipulated who sits in the other side [of the litter]. One whose distance from it is less than two stages and who is strong enough to walk — pilgrimage is incumbent upon him. If he is weak, then he is like the distant one. It is also stipulated that the provisions and the mount be surplus (fāḍilayn) over his debt and over the maintenance of those whose support is incumbent upon him for the duration of his going and returning. The more correct position (al-aṣaḥḥ) is the stipulation that it be surplus over his dwelling and over a slave he needs for his service, and that he is obligated to divert the capital of his trade to these two [purposes].

The third: Safety of the road. Thus, if he fears for himself or his wealth — [due to] a predatory beast, an enemy, or a highway robber — and there is no other road, pilgrimage is not obligatory. The more apparent position (al-aẓhar) is the obligation of sea travel if safety predominates, and that he is obligated to pay the fee of the armed escort (ujrat al-badharqah). The existence of water and provisions is stipulated in the places from which it is customary to carry them, at a fair price (thaman al-mithl) — that is, the amount befitting him in that time and place — and the fodder of the mount at every stage. Regarding the woman: her husband, a male relative within prohibited degrees (maḥram), or trustworthy women must accompany her. The more correct position (al-aṣaḥḥ) is that the existence of a maḥram is not stipulated for one of them [i.e., a group of women], and that she is obligated to pay the hire of the maḥram if he will not go out except with her.

The fourth: That he be able to remain firmly on the mount without severe hardship. Upon the blind person, pilgrimage is obligatory if he finds a guide (qāʾid), who is like the maḥram in the case of the woman. The one placed under legal restriction (maḥjūr ʿalayh) due to foolishness (safah) is like others [in obligation], but the wealth is not handed to him; rather, the guardian (walī) goes out with him or appoints a person for him.

The second type: Capacity to procure it through another (istiṭāʿat taḥṣīlihi bi-ghayrihi). Thus, whoever dies while pilgrimage is incumbent upon his liability (dhimmah), it is obligatory to have someone perform the pilgrimage on his behalf from his estate (tarkah). The incapacitated person (maʿḍūb) who is unable to perform pilgrimage himself — if he finds someone to perform it for him at a fair wage (ujrat al-mithl), it is incumbent upon him. It is stipulated that [the wage] be surplus over the needs mentioned for one who performs pilgrimage himself, but the maintenance of dependents for the going and returning is not stipulated. If his son or a stranger offers wealth for the wage, acceptance is not obligatory in the more correct position (al-aṣaḥḥ). If the son offers obedience [i.e., to go in his stead], acceptance is obligatory; likewise the stranger, in the more correct position.

| Chapter on the Fixed Times (al-Mawāqīt)

The time for the iḥrām of pilgrimage is Shawwāl, Dhū al-Qaʿdah, and ten nights of Dhū al-Ḥijjah. Regarding the night of sacrifice (laylat al-naḥr), there is a position [of validity]. If one assumes iḥrām for it outside its time, it is contracted as ʿUmrah according to the sound position (al-ṣaḥīḥ). The entire year is a time for the iḥrām of ʿUmrah. The spatial mīqāt for pilgrimage in the case of one who is in Mecca is Mecca itself; it was said: the entire Sacred Precinct (al-ḥaram). As for other than him, the mīqāt of one proceeding from Medina is Dhū al-Ḥulayfah; from Syria, Egypt, and the Maghrib, al-Juḥfah; from the Tihāmah of Yemen, Yalamlam; from the Najd of the Ḥijāz, Qarn; from the East, Dhāt ʿIrq. It is preferable to assume iḥrām from the beginning of the mīqāt, and it is permissible from its end. Whoever takes a road that does not terminate at a mīqāt — if he aligns (ḥādhā) with a mīqāt, he assumes iḥrām from the point of alignment; or with two mīqāts, then the more correct position (al-aṣaḥḥ) is that he assumes iḥrām from the alignment of the farther of the two. If he does not align with any, he assumes iḥrām at two stages from Mecca. One whose residence is between Mecca and the mīqāt — his mīqāt is his residence. Whoever reaches a mīqāt not intending a rite (nusuk), then later intends it — his mīqāt is his location. If he reaches it intending [the rite], it is not permissible to pass it without iḥrām. If he does so, he is obligated to return to assume iḥrām from it, unless the time is constricted or the road is fearsome. If he does not return, a blood-offering (dam) is incumbent upon him. If he assumes iḥrām and then returns, the more correct position (al-aṣaḥḥ) is that if he returns before engaging in any rite, the blood-offering is dropped; otherwise not. It is preferable to assume iḥrām from the dwelling of his family, and in one position, from the mīqāt. I say: The mīqāt is the more apparent (aẓhar), and it is what accords with the authentic hadiths. And God knows best. The mīqāt of ʿUmrah for one who is outside the Sacred Precinct is the mīqāt of pilgrimage. One who is within the Sacred Precinct is obligated to go out to the nearest point of the profane land (adnā al-ḥill), even by one step. If he does not go out and performs the acts of ʿUmrah, it suffices him in the more apparent position (al-aẓhar), and a blood-offering is incumbent upon him. If he goes out to the profane land after his iḥrām, the blood-offering is dropped according to the school (al-madhhab). The most virtuous places of the profane land are al-Jiʿrānah, then al-Tanʿīm, then al-Ḥudaybiyyah.

| Chapter on Iḥrām

It is contracted as specified (muʿayyan) by intending pilgrimage, ʿUmrah, or both; and as absolute (muṭlaq) by not adding anything beyond the iḥrām itself. Specification is preferable, and in one position, absoluteness [is preferable]. If one assumes absolute iḥrām in the months of pilgrimage, he may direct it by intention to whichever of the two rites he wishes, or to both, then occupy himself with the acts. If he assumes it absolute outside these months, the more correct position (al-aṣaḥḥ) is that it is contracted as ʿUmrah, so he may not direct it to pilgrimage in its months. He may assume iḥrām like the iḥrām of Zayd (ka-iḥrām Zayd). If Zayd was not in a state of iḥrām, his iḥrām is contracted as absolute; and it was said: If he knew that Zayd was not in iḥrām, it is not contracted. If Zayd was in iḥrām, his iḥrām is contracted like his iḥrām. If knowing his iḥrām becomes impossible due to his death, he makes himself a qārin (one performing both rites together) and performs the acts of both rites.

chapters.arabic_text:
# فصل
# المحرم ينوي ويلبي فإن لبى بلا نية لم ينعقد إحرامه وإن نوى ولم يلب

انعقد على الصحيح ويسن الغسل للإحرام فإن عجز تيمم ولدخول مكة وللوقوف

بعرفة وبمزدلفة غداة النحر وفي أيام التشريق للرمي وأن يطيب بدنه للإحرام

وكذا ثوبه في الأصح ولا بأس باستدامته بعد الإحرام ولا بطيب له جرم لكن لو

نزع ثوبه المطيب ثم لبسه لزمه الفدية في الأصح وأن تخضب المرأة للإحرام

يديها ويتجرد الرجل لإحرامه عن مخيط الثياب ويلبس إزارا ورداء أبيضين

ونعلين ويصلي ركعتين ثم الأفضل أن يحرم إذا انبعثت به راحلته أو توجه

لطريقه ماشيا وفي قول يحرم عقب الصلاة ويستحب إكثار التلبية ورفع صوته بها

في دوام إحرامه وخاصة عند تغاير الأحول كركوب ونزول وصعود وهبوط واختلاط 

رفقة ولا تستحب في طواف القدوم وفي القديم تستحب فيه بلا جهر ولفظها لبيك

اللهم لبيك لبيك لا شريك لك لبيك إن الحمد والنعمة لك والملك لا شريك لك

وإذا رأى ما يعجبه قال لبيك إن العيش عيش الآخرة وإذا فرغ من تلبيته صلى

على النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم وسأل الله تعالى الجنة ورضوانه واستعاذ به من

النار.
# 

| باب دخول مكة
# الأفضل دخولها قبل الوقوف وأن يغتسل داخلها من طريق المدينة بذي طوى

ويدخلها من مر ثنية كداء ويقول إذا أبصر البيت اللهم زد هذا البيت تشريفا

وتعظيما وتكريما ومهامة،
# 
# وزد من شرفه وعظمه ممن حجه أو اعتمره تشريفا وتكريما وتعظيما وبرا اللهم

أنت السلام ومنك
# السلام فحينا ربنا بالسلام ثم يدخل المسجد من باب بني شيبة ويبتدىء بطواف

القدوم ويختص طواف القدوم بحاج دخل مكة قبل الوقوف ومن قصد مكة لا لنسك

استحب له أن يحرم بحج أو عمرة وفي قول يجب إلا أن يتكرر دخوله كحطاب وصياد.

# فصل
# للطواف بأنواعه واجبات وسنن أما الواجبات: فيشترط ستر العورة وطهارة

الحدث والنجس فلو أحدث فيه توضأ وبنى وفي قول يستأنف وأن يجعل البيت عن

يساره مبتدئا بالحجر الأسود محاذيا له في مروره بجميع بدنه فلو بدأ بغير

الحجر لم يحسب فإذا انتهى إليه ابتدأ منه ولو مشى على الشاذروان أو مس

الجدرا في موازاته أو دخل من إحدى فتحتي الحجر وخرج من الأخرى لم تصح طوفته

وفي مسألة المس وجه وأن يطوف سبعا داخل المسجد.
# وأما السنن: فأن يطوف ماشيا ويستلم الحجر أول طوافه ويقبله ويضع جبهته

عليه فإن عجز استلم فإن عجز أشار بيده ويراعي ذلك في كل طوفة ولا يقبل

الركنين الشاميين ولا يستلمهما ويستلم اليماني ولا يقبله وأن يقول أول

طوافه بسم الله والله أكبر اللهم إيمانا بك وتصديقا بكتابك ووفاء بعهدك

واتباعا لسنة نبيك محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم وليقل قبالة الباب اللهم إن

البيت بيتك والحرم حرمك والأمن أمنك وهذا مقام العائذ بك من  النار وبين

اليمانيين اللهم آتنا في الدنيا حسنة وفي الآخرة حسنة وقنا عذاب النار

وليدع بما شاء
# 
# ومأثور الدعاء أفضل من القراءة وهي أفضل من غير مأثوره وأن يرمل في

الأشواط الثلاثة الأولى بأن يسرع مشيه مقاربا خطاه ويمشي في الباقي ويختص

الرمل بطواف يعقبه سعي وفي قول بطواف القدوم وليقل فيه اللهم اجعله حجا

مبرورا وذنبا مغفورا وسعيا مشكورا وأن يضطبع في جميع كل طواف يرمل فيه وكذا

في السعي على الصحيح وهو جعل وسط ردائه تحت منكبه الأيمن وطرفيه على الأيسر

ولا ترمل المرأة ولا تضطبع وأن يقرب من البيت فلو فات الرمل بالقرب لزحمة

فالرمل مع بعد أولى إلا أن يخاف صدم النساء فالقرب بلا رمل أولى وأن يوالي

طوافه ويصلي بعده ركعتين خلف المقام يقرأ في الأولى قل يا أيها الكافرون

وفي الثانية الإخلاص ويجهر ليلا وفي قول تجب الموالاة والصلاة ولو حمل

الحلال محرما وطاف به حسب للمحمول وكذا لو حمله محرم قد طاف عن نفسه وإلا

فالأصح أنه إن قصده للمحمول فله وإن قصده لنفسه أولهما فللحامل فقط.

# فصل
# يستلم الحجر بعد الطواف وصلاته ثم يخرج من باب الصف للسعي وشرطه أن يبدأ

بالصفا وأن يسعى سبعا ذهابه من الصفا إلى المروة مرة وعوده منها إليه أخرى

وأن يسعى بعد طواف ركن أو قدوم بحيث لا يتخلل بينهما الوقوف بعرفة ومن سعى

بعد قدوم لم يعده ويستحب أن يرقى على الصفا والمروة قدر قامة فإذا رقى قال:

الله أكبر الله أكبر الله أكبر
# 
# ولله الحمد الله أكبر على ما هدانا والحمد لله على ما أولانا لا إله إلا

الله وحده لا شريك له له الملك وله الحمد يحي ويميت بيده الخير وهو على كل

شيء قدير ثم يدعو بما شاء دينا ودنيا.
# قلت: ويعيد الذكر والدعاء ثانيا وثالثا، والله أعلم. وأن يمشي أول المسعى

وآخره ويدعو في الوسط وموضع النوعين معروف.

  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In devotional law (ʿibādāt), niyyah is the discriminative factor (mumayyizah) that elevates a physical act into an act of worship, orienting it toward the Divine.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Used literally (ḥaqīqah) as the heart's determination; metaphorically (majāz) it may denote the act's legal identity.
- Root: ل-ب-ي (l-b-y)

  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Theological nuance: the pilgrim's response (ijābah) to God's command to Abraham to proclaim the Hajj, affirming divine unity and sovereignty.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal: "I am present, I am obedient"; metaphorical: the soul's steadfastness in the state of iḥrām.

chapters.translation:
I say: Know that the chapter on the rites of the one in iḥrām (al-muḥrim) comprises the following rulings.

**Chapter: On the Intention and Talbiyah of the Muhrim**

The one entering iḥrām must form the intention (niyyah) and utter the talbiyah. If he utters the talbiyah without an intention, his iḥrām does not contract. But if he forms the intention and does not utter the talbiyah, his iḥrām does contract — this is the sound opinion (al-ṣaḥīḥ). It is Sunnah to perform the major ablution (ghusl) for iḥrām; if he is unable due to lack of water, he performs dry ablution (tayammum). Ghusl is also Sunnah for entering Mecca, for standing at ʿArafah, for staying at Muzdalifah on the morning of the Day of Sacrifice, and during the Days of Tashrīq for the stoning (ramy). It is Sunnah for him to perfume his body for iḥrām, and likewise his garment — this is the sounder opinion (al-aṣaḥḥ). There is no harm in the perfume's fragrance persisting after he has entered iḥrām, nor in perfume that has no visible substance (jirm). However, if he removes his perfumed garment and then dons it again, a ransom (fidyah) becomes obligatory upon him — this is the sounder opinion. It is Sunnah for a woman to dye her hands with henna for iḥrām. A man, for his iḥrām, must divest himself of sewn garments (makhīṭ); he wears a waist-wrapper (izār) and a cloak (ridāʾ), both white, and sandals. He prays two rakʿahs. Then it is preferable (al-afḍal) that he enter iḥrām when his mount rises with him, or when he sets out on his path if walking. In one opinion (qawl), he enters iḥrām immediately after the prayer. It is recommended (yustaḥabb) to multiply the talbiyah and to raise his voice with it throughout the duration of his iḥrām, especially at times of changing circumstances (taghāyur al-aḥwāl) — such as mounting and dismounting, ascending and descending, and when caravans meet. It is not recommended during the Tawaf of Arrival (ṭawāf al-qudūm); in the old opinion (al-qadīm), it is recommended therein without raising the voice. Its wording is: {«Labbayka Allāhumma labbayk, labbayka lā sharīka laka labbayk, inna al-ḥamda wa'l-niʿmata laka wa'l-mulk, lā sharīka lak»} — "I am at Your service, O God, I am at Your service; I am at Your service, You have no partner, I am at Your service; truly all praise and grace are Yours, and the dominion — You have no partner." When he sees something that pleases him, he says: "Labbayk, indeed true life is the life of the Hereafter." When he finishes his talbiyah, he sends blessings upon the Prophet ﷺ, asks God Almighty for Paradise and His good pleasure, and seeks refuge with Him from the Fire.

**Chapter: On Entering Mecca**

It is preferable to enter Mecca before the Standing at ʿArafah. He should perform ghusl before entering it, at Dhī Ṭuwā, if coming by the road from Medina. He enters from the upper pass (thaniyyat kadāʾ). When he beholds the House, he says: "O God, increase this House in honor, veneration, and reverence, and increase in honor, veneration, reverence, and goodness those who perform the Hajj or ʿUmrah to it. O God, You are Peace, and from You is peace; so revive us, our Lord, with peace." Then he enters the Mosque from the gate of Banī Shaybah, and begins with the Tawaf of Arrival (ṭawāf al-qudūm). This Tawaf of Arrival is specific to a pilgrim who enters Mecca before the Standing. For one who enters Mecca with no intention of performing a rite (nusuk), it is recommended that he enter iḥrām for Hajj or ʿUmrah; in one opinion, it is obligatory — except for one whose entry is repeated, such as a woodcutter or a fisherman.

**Chapter: On the Obligations and Sunnahs of Tawaf**

The Tawaf, in all its types, has obligatory elements (wājibāt) and Sunnahs. As for the obligatory elements: it is required that the private parts be covered, and that one be pure from major and minor ritual impurity (ḥadath) and from physical impurity (najas). If he becomes impure during the Tawaf, he performs ablution and continues from where he left off; in one opinion, he must restart. He must keep the House on his left, beginning at the Black Stone, aligning his entire body with it as he passes. If he begins at a point other than the Black Stone, that circuit does not count; when he reaches it, he begins from it. If he walks upon the semi-circular wall (al-shādharwān), or touches the wall in its alignment, or enters through one of the two openings of the Hijr and exits through the other, his circuit is not valid — and in the matter of touching, there is a detailed discussion. He must complete seven circuits within the Mosque.

As for the Sunnahs: he should perform the Tawaf walking. He touches the Black Stone at the start of his Tawaf, kisses it, and places his forehead upon it. If he cannot, he touches it with his hand; if he cannot, he gestures toward it with his hand. He observes this in every circuit. He does not kiss the two Yamani corners, nor does he touch them; he touches the Yamani corner but does not kiss it. At the beginning of his Tawaf, he says: "In the name of God, and God is Greatest. O God, in faith in You, and affirmation of Your Book, and fulfillment of Your covenant, and following the Sunnah of Your Prophet Muhammad ﷺ." Facing the door, he says: "O God, truly this House is Your House, and this Sanctuary is Your Sanctuary, and this security is Your security, and this is the station of one seeking refuge with You from the Fire." Between the two Yamani corners, he says: {«Rabbanā ātinā fī al-dunyā ḥasanah wa fī al-ākhirati ḥasanah wa qinā ʿadhāba al-nār»} — "Our Lord, give us good in this world and good in the Hereafter, and protect us from the punishment of the Fire." And he supplicates with whatever he wishes. The transmitted supplications (maʾthūr) are better than recitation of the Quran, and recitation is better than non-transmitted supplications.

It is Sunnah to hasten (ramal) in the first three circuits — that is, to quicken his pace with short, close steps — and to walk normally in the remaining four. The ramal is specific to a Tawaf followed by a Saʿy; in one opinion, it is specific to the Tawaf of Arrival. During it, he says: "O God, make it an accepted Hajj, a forgiven sin, and a thanked striving." It is Sunnah to drape the cloak (iḍṭibāʿ) throughout every Tawaf in which he performs ramal, and likewise during the Saʿy — this is the sound opinion. This consists of placing the middle of his cloak under his right shoulder and its two ends over his left. A woman does not perform ramal nor iḍṭibāʿ. It is Sunnah to draw close to the House. If the ramal is missed due to closeness caused by crowding, then ramal from a distance takes precedence; however, if he fears colliding with women, then closeness without ramal takes precedence. It is Sunnah to maintain continuity (muwālāh) in his Tawaf, and to pray two rakʿahs after it behind the Station of Abraham (maqām Ibrāhīm), reciting in the first {«Qul yā ayyuhā al-kāfirūn»} and in the second {«al-Ikhlāṣ»}, and to recite aloud at night. In one opinion, the continuity and the prayer are obligatory. If a non-muḥrim carries a muḥrim and circumambulates with him, the circuit counts for the one carried. Likewise, if a muḥrim who has already performed the Tawaf for himself carries another, the circuit counts for the carried one. But if he intends it for himself, or for both — then, in the soundest opinion, it counts only for the carrier.

**Chapter: On the Saʿy**

After the Tawaf and its prayer, he touches the Black Stone, then exits through the gate of al-Ṣafā for the Saʿy. Its condition is that he begin at al-Ṣafā, and that he perform seven traversals — his going from al-Ṣafā to al-Marwah counts as one, and his return from al-Marwah to al-Ṣafā counts as another. It is also a condition that the Saʿy follow an obligatory Tawaf or a Tawaf of Arrival, such that the Standing at ʿArafah does not intervene between them. Whoever performs the Saʿy after the Tawaf of Arrival need not repeat it. It is recommended that he ascend upon al-Ṣafā and al-Marwah to the height of a man. When he ascends, he says: "God is Greatest, God is Greatest, God is Greatest, and to God belongs all praise. God is Greatest for having guided us, and praise be to God for what He has bestowed upon us. There is no god but God alone, with no partner; to Him belongs the dominion and to Him belongs all praise; He gives life and causes death; in His hand is all good; and He is over all things competent." Then he supplicates with whatever he wishes, for his religion and his worldly affairs. I say: And he repeats the remembrance and supplication a second and third time — and God knows best. It is Sunnah to walk at the beginning and end of the course (masʿā), and to supplicate in the middle; the location of both types is well known.

# فصل
# يستحب للإمام أو منصوبه أن يخطب بمكة في سابع ذي الحجة بعد  صلاة الظهر

خطبة فردة يأمر فيها بالغدو إلى منى ويعلمهم ما أمامهم من المناسك ويخرج

بهم من الغد إلى منى ويبيتون بها فإذا طلعت الشمس قصدوا عرفات.
# قلت: ولا يدخلونها بل يقيمون بنمرة بقرب عرفات حتى نزول الشمس والله أعلم

ثم يخطب الإمام بعد الزوال خطبتين ثم يصلي بالناس الظهر والعصر جمعا ويقفوا

بعرفة إلى الغروب ويذكروا الله تعالى ويدعوه ويكثروا التهليل فإذا غربت

الشمس قصدوا مزدلفة وأخروا المغرب ليصلوها مع العشاء بمزدلفة جمعا وواجب

الوقوف حضوره بجزء من أرض عرفات وإن كان مارا في طلب آبق ونحوه بشرط كونه

أهلا للعبادة لا مغمى عليه ولا بأس بالنوم ووقت الوقوف من الزوال يوم عرفة

والصحيح بقاؤه إلى الفجر يوم النحر ولو وقف نهارا ثم فارق عرفة قبل الغروب

ولم يعد أراق دما استحبابا وفي قول يجب وإن عاد فكان بها عند الغروب فلا دم

وكذا إن عاد ليلا في الأصح ولو وقفوا اليوم العاشر غلطا أجزأهم إلا
# 
# أن يقلوا على خلاف العادة فيقضون في الأصح وإن وقفوا في الثامن وعلموا

قبل فوات الوقت وجب الوقوف في الوقت وإن علموا بعده وجب القضاء في الأصح.

# فصل
# ويبيتون بمزدلفة ومن دفع منها بعد نصف الليل أو قبله وعاد قبل الفجر فلا

شيء عليه ومن لم يكن بها في النصف الثاني أراق دما وفي وجوبه القولان ويسن

تقديم النساء والضعفة بعد نصف الليل إلى منى ويبقى غيرهم حتى يصلوا الصبح

مغلسين ثم يدفعون إلى منى ويأخذون من مزدلفة حصى الرمي فإذا بلغوا المشعر

الحرام وقفوا ودعوا إلى الأسفار ثم يسيرون فيصلون منى بعد طلوع الشمس فيرمي

كل شخص حينئذ سبع حصيات إلى جمرة العقبة ويقطع التلبية عند ابتداء الرمي

ويكبر مع كل حصاة ثم يذبح من معه هدى ثم يحلق أو يقصر والحلق أفضل وتقصر

المرأة والحلق نسك على المشهور وأقله ثلاث شعرات حلقا أو تقصيرا أو نتفا أو

إحراقا أو قصا ومن لا شعر برأسه يستحب إمرار الموصى عليه فإذا حلق أو  قصر

دخل مكة وطاف طواف الركن وسعى إن لم يكن سعى ثم يعود إلى منى وهذا الرمي

والذبح والحلق والطواف يسن ترتيبها كما ذكرنا ويدخل وقتها بنصف ليلة النحر

ويبقى وقت الرمي آخر يوم النحر ولا يختص الذبح بزمن.
# قلت: الصحيح اختصاصه بوقت الأضحية وسيأتي في آخر باب محرمات الإحرام على

الصواب والله أعلم والحلق والطواف والسعي لا آخر لوقتها وإذا قلنا الحلق

نسك
# 
# ففعل اثنين من الرمي والحلق والطواف حصل التحلل الأول وحل به اللبس

والحلق والقلم وكذا الصيد وعقد النكاح في الأظهر.
# قلت: الأظهر لا يحل عقد النكاح، والله أعلم. وإذا فعل الثالث: حصل التحلل

الثاني وحل به باقي المحرمات.

# فصل
# إذا عاد إلى منى بات بها ليلتي التشريق ورمى كل يوم إلى الجمرات الثلاث

كل جمرة سبع حصيات فإذا رمى اليوم الثاني فأراد النفر قبل غروب الشمس جاز

وسقط مبيت الليلة الثالث: ة ورمى يومها فإن لم ينفر حتى غربت وجب مبيتها

ورمى الغد ويدخل رمي التشريق بزوال الشمس ويخرج بغروبها وقيل: يبقى إلى

الفجر ويشترط رمي السبع واحدة واحدة وترتيب الجمرات وكون المرمى حجرا وأن

يسمى رميا فلا يكفي الوضع والسنة أن يرمي بقدر حصى الخزف ولا يشترط بقاء

الحجر في المرمى ولا كون الرامي خارجا عن الجمرة ومن عجز عن الرمي استناب

وإذا ترك رمى يوم تداركه في باقي الأيام على الأظهر ولا دم وإلا فعليه دم

والمذهب تكميل الدم في ثلاث حصيات رمي وإذا أراد الخروج من مكة طاف للوداع

ولا يمكث بعده وهو واجب يجبر تركه بدم وفي قول سنة لا يجبر فإن أوجبناه

فخرج بلا وداع فعاد قبل مسافة القصر سقط الدم أو بعدها فلا على الصحيح

وللحائض النفر بلا وداع ويسن شرب ماء زمزم وزيارة قبر رسول الله صلى الله

عليه وسلم بعد فراغ الحج.

  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To address, deliver an oration; a solemn public speech (khuṭbah) with ritual standing.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): The khuṭbah as a formal act of worship (ʿibādah) tied to communal obligation, distinct from mere admonition.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal (ḥaqīqah) — a structured address; metaphorical (majāz) — any elevated proclamation of divine commands.
- Root: و ق ف (wa-qa-fa)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To stand still, halt; the core ritual of ʿArafāt (wuqūf).
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): The wuqūf as the essential pillar (rukn) of ḥajj, symbolizing the soul’s presence before God.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal — physical standing; metaphorical — spiritual attentiveness (ḥuḍūr al-qalb).
- Root: ر م ي (ra-ma-ya)

  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Ritual casting as an act of obedience and repulsion of the devil.
