chapters.arabic_text:
# فصل
# يشترط في المقر به أن لا يكون ملكا للمقر فلو قال داري أو ثوبي أو ديني

الذي على زيد لعمرو فهو لغو ولو قال هذا لفلان وكان ملكي إلى أن أقررت به

فأول كلامه إقرار وآخره لغو وليكن المقر به في يد المقر ليسلم بالإقرار

للمقر له فلو أقر ولم يكن في يده ثم صار عمل يمقتضى الإقرار فلو أقر بحرية

عبد في يد غيره ثم اشتراه حكم بحريته ثم إن كان قال هو حر الأصل فشراؤه

افتداء وإن قال أعتقه  فافتداء من جهته وبيع من جهة البائع على المذهب فيثبت

فيه الخياران للبائع فقط ويصح الإقرار بالمجهول فإذا قال له على شيء قبل

تفسيره بكل ما يتمول وإن قل ولو فسره بما لا يتمول لكنه من جنسه كحبة حنطة

أو بما يحل اقتناؤه ككلب معلم وسرجين قبل في الأصح ولا يقبل بما لا يقتني

كخنزير وكلب لا نفع فيه ولا بعيادة ورد سلام ولو أقر بمال أو مال عظيم أو

كبير أو كثير قبل تفسيره بما قل منه وكذا بالمستولدة في الأصح لا بكلب وجلد

ميتة وقوله له كذا كقوله شيء وقوله شيء شيء أو كذا كذا كما لو لم يكرر ولو

قال شيء وشيء أو كذا وكذا وجب شيئان ولو قال كذا درهما أو رفع الدرهم أو

جره لزمه درهم والمذهب أنه لو قال كذا وكذا درهما بالنصب
# 
# وجب درهمان وأنه لو رفع أو جر فدرهم ولو حذف الواو فدرهم في الأحوال ولو

قال ألف ودرهم قبل تفسير الألف بغير الدراهم ولو قال خمسة وعشرون درهما

فالجميع دراهم على الصحيح ولو قال الدراهم التي أقررت بها ناقصة الوزن فإن

كانت دراهم البلد تامة الوزن فالصحيح قبوله إن ذكره متصلا ومنعه إن فصله عن

الإقرار وإن كانت ناقصة قبل إن وصله وكذا إن فصله في النص والتفسير

بالمغشوشة كهو بالناقصة ولو قال له علي من درهم إلى عشرة لزمه تسعة في

الأصح وإن قال درهم في عشرة فإن أراد المعية لزمه أحد عشر أو الحساب فعشرة

وإلا فدرهم.

# فصل
# قال له عندي سيف في غمد أو ثوب في صندوق لا يلزمه الظرف أو غمد فيه سيف

أو صندوق فيه ثوب لزمه الظرف وحده أو عبد على رأسه عمامة لم تلزمه العمامة

على الصحيح أو دابة بسرجها أو ثوب مطرز لزمه الجميع ولو قال في ميراث أبي

ألف فهو إقرار على أبيه بدين ولو قال في ميراثي من أبي فهو وعد هبة ولو قال

له علي درهم درهم لزمه درهم فإن  قال ودرهم لزمه درهمان ولو قال له درهم

ودرهم ودرهم لزمه بالأولين درهمان وأما الثالث: فإن أراد به تأكيد الثاني

لم يجب به شيء وإن نوى الاستئناف لزمه ثالث وكذا إن نوى تأكيد الأول أو

أطلق في الأصح ومتى أقر بمبهم كشيء وثوب وطولب بالبيان فامتنع
# 
# فالصحيح أنه يحبس ولو بين وكذبه المقر له فليبين وليدع والقول قول

المقرفي نفيه ولو أقر له بألف ثم أقر له بألف في يوم آخر لزمه ألف فقط وإن

اختلف القدر دخل الأقل في الأكثر فلو وصفهما بصفتين مختلفتين أو أسندهما

إلى جهتين أو قال قبضت يوم السبت عشرة ثم قال قبضت يوم الأحد عشرة لزما ولو

قال له علي ألف من ثمن خمر أو كلب أو ألف قضيته لزمه الألف في الأظهر ولو

قال من ثمن عبد لم أقبضه إذا سلمه سلمت قبل على المذهب وجعل ثمنا ولو قال

له علي ألف إن شاء الله لم يلزمه شيء على المذهب ولو قال ألف لا يلزم لزمه

ولو قال له علي ألف ثم جاء بالألف وقال أردت به هذا وهو وديعة فقال المقر

له لي عليه ألف آخر صدق المقر في الأظهر بيمينه فإن كان قال في ذمتي أو

دينا صدق المقر له على المذهب
# قلت: فإذا قبلنا التفسير بالوديعة فالأصح أنها أمانة فيقبل دعواه التلف

بعد الإقرار ودعوى الرد وإن قال له عندي أو معي ألف صدق في دعوى الوديعة

والرد والتلف قطعا والله أعلم ولو أقر ببيع أو هبة وإقباض ثم قال كان فاسدا

وأقررت لظني الصحة لم يقبل وله تحليف المقر له فإن نكل حلف المقر وبرىء ولو

قال هذه الدار لزيد بل لعمرو أو غصبتها من زيد بل من عمر وسلمت لزيد

والأظهر أن المقر يغرم قيمتها لعمر وبالإقرار ويصح الاستثناء إن اتصل ولم

يستغرق فلو قال له علي عشرة إلا تسعة إلا ثمانية وجب تسعة ويصح من غير

الجنس كألف إلا نوبا ويبين بثوب قيمته دون ألف ومن المعين  كهذه الدار له

إلا هذا البيت أو هذه الدراهم له إلا ذا الدرهم وفي المعين وجه شاذ.
# قلت: ولو قال هؤلاء العبيد له إلا واحدا قبل ورجع في البيان إليه فإن

ماتوا إلا واحدا وزعم أنه المستثنى صدق بيمينه على الصحيح. والله أعلم.
#
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ق-ر-ر (q-r-r)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To settle, affirm, establish firmly; in legal context, a declarative admission that fixes a right.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Iqrār as an epistemic act of truth-telling (iṣdāq) that binds the confessor, distinct from testimony (shahādah) which binds others.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal (ḥaqīqah) — verbal acknowledgment; metaphorical (majāz) — any act implying admission, e.g., handing over property.
- Root: م-ل-ك (m-l-k)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Possession, ownership; dominion over an object.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Milk as legal capacity (qudrah) over an object, entailing exclusive disposal rights.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal — actual ownership; metaphorical — authority or control, as in "malik al-amr" (master of the affair).
- Root: خ-ص-م (kh-ṣ-m)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To dispute, litigate; a party in a legal claim.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Khuṣūmah as the adversarial process where confession (iqrār) preempts dispute by establishing a claim.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal — verbal contention; metaphorical — any situation of conflicting rights requiring adjudication.
- Sībawayh Rule: Taʿlīq al-Ḥukm bi al-Sharṭ (Conditional Suspension of Ruling) — The legal effect of an utterance is suspended on its syntactic and semantic completeness; a confession interrupted by a contradictory clause (istithnāʾ) is parsed for its operative part, with the exception (mustathnā) either nullifying or qualifying the admission based on connectivity (ittiṣāl) and exhaustiveness (istighrāq).
chapters.translation:
I say: Know that the conditions for the one against whom a confession is made (al-muqarr lahu) and the subject of confession (al-muqarr bihi) are established in this section.

Chapter: It is required that the object of confession (al-muqarr bihi) not be the property of the confessor (al-muqarr). Thus, if he says, "My house," or "My garment," or "My debt which Zayd owes me, belongs to ʿAmr," it is void (laghw). But if he says, "This belongs to so-and-so, and it was my property until I confessed it to him," then the first part of his speech is a valid confession (iqrār) and the last part is void. The object of confession should be in the possession of the confessor so that it may be delivered to the claimant by virtue of the confession. If he confesses without the object being in his possession, then later it comes into his possession, it is acted upon according to the confession. Thus, if he confesses to the freedom (ḥurriyyah) of a slave who is in the possession of another, then later purchases him, the slave is judged to be free. Then, if he said, "He is free by origin (ḥurr al-aṣl)," his purchase is an act of ransom (iftidāʾ). If he said, "I freed him (aʿtaqtuhu)," then it is a ransom from his side and a sale from the seller's side, according to the authoritative school (al-madhhab). Thus, both options (khiyārān) are established for the seller only.

A confession of an unknown thing (majhūl) is valid. So if he says, "He has a thing (shayʾ) against me," it is accepted with its interpretation as anything of monetary value (mutamawwal), however little. If he interprets it as something without monetary value but of the same genus (jins), like a grain of wheat, or something permissible to possess, like a trained dog or dung (sirjīn), it is accepted in the soundest view (al-aṣaḥḥ). It is not accepted for something impermissible to possess, like a pig or a dog with no benefit, nor for a visit to the sick (ʿiyādah) or returning a greeting (radd salām). If he confesses to "property (māl)," or "great property," or "large property," or "much property," it is accepted with its interpretation as something small of that kind. Likewise, for a "slave-mother (mustawlada)" in the soundest view, but not for a dog or the skin of a dead animal (jild maytah).

His saying, "He has such-and-such (kadhā) against me," is like his saying, "a thing." His saying, "a thing, a thing," or "such-and-such, such-and-such," is as if he did not repeat it. But if he says, "a thing and a thing," or "such-and-such and such-and-such," two things are obligatory. If he says, "such-and-such a dirham (kadhā dirhaman)," with the accusative (naṣb) of "dirham," or raises it (rafʿ), or lowers it (jarr), one dirham is obligatory. The authoritative school holds that if he says, "such-and-such and such-and-such a dirham (kadhā wa-kadhā dirhaman)," with the accusative, two dirhams are obligatory; if he raises or lowers it, then one dirham. If he omits the conjunction (wāw), then one dirham in all cases.

If he says, "a thousand and a dirham," the thousand is interpreted as something other than dirhams. If he says, "five and twenty dirhams," all are dirhams in the correct view (al-ṣaḥīḥ). If he says, "The dirhams I confessed are deficient in weight (nāqiṣat al-wazn)," then if the dirhams of the land are of full weight, the correct view is that it is accepted if he mentions it contiguously (muttaṣilan), and rejected if he separates it (faṣala) from the confession. If they are deficient, it is accepted whether he connects it or separates it, according to the text (al-naṣṣ). Interpretation with adulterated coins (maghshūshah) is like interpretation with deficient ones.

If he says, "He has against me from a dirham to ten," nine dirhams are obligatory in the soundest view. If he says, "a dirham in ten," then if he intends concomitance (maʿiyyah), eleven are obligatory; if he intends calculation (ḥisāb), then ten; otherwise, one dirham.

Chapter: If he says, "I have a sword in a sheath," or "a garment in a chest," the container (ẓarf) is not obligatory. If he says, "a sheath with a sword in it," or "a chest with a garment in it," the container alone is obligatory. If he says, "a slave with a turban on his head," the turban is not obligatory in the soundest view. If he says, "an animal with its saddle," or "an embroidered garment," all of it is obligatory.

If he says, "In my father's inheritance is a thousand," it is a confession against his father of a debt. If he says, "In my inheritance from my father is a thousand," it is a promise of a gift (waʿd hibah).

If he says, "He has against me a dirham, a dirham," one dirham is obligatory. If he says, "and a dirham," two dirhams are obligatory. If he says, "He has a dirham, and a dirham, and a dirham," two dirhams are obligatory by the first two. As for the third, if he intends it as an emphasis (taʾkīd) of the second, nothing is obligatory by it; if he intends a fresh start (istiʾnāf), a third is obligatory. Likewise, if he intends emphasis of the first, or leaves it unqualified (muṭlaq), in the soundest view.

Whenever he confesses to something ambiguous (mubham), like "a thing" or "a garment," and is demanded to clarify (bayān) but refuses, the correct view is that he is imprisoned (yuḥbas). If he clarifies and the claimant denies him, he must clarify and claim, and the word is the word of the confessor in denying [the claimant's interpretation].

If he confesses to a thousand, then confesses to another thousand on another day, only one thousand is obligatory. If the amounts differ, the lesser is included in the greater. If he describes them with two different descriptions, or attributes them to two different sources, or says, "I received on Saturday ten," then says, "I received on Sunday ten," both are obligatory.

If he says, "He has against me a thousand from the price of wine (khamr) or a dog," or "a thousand which I have paid (qaḍaytuhu)," the thousand is obligatory in the most apparent view (al-aẓhar). If he says, "from the price of a slave I have not received, when he is delivered to me, I will deliver [the price]," it is accepted in the authoritative school and is made a price (thaman).

If he says, "He has against me a thousand, if God wills (in shāʾ Allāh)," nothing is obligatory in the authoritative school. If he says, "a thousand, not obligatory (lā yalzam)," it is obligatory.

If he says, "He has against me a thousand," then brings the thousand and says, "I meant by it this, and it is a deposit (wadīʿah) with me," and the claimant says, "He has another thousand against me," the confessor is believed in the most apparent view, with his oath. But if he said, "in my liability (dhimmah)" or "as a debt (dayn)," the claimant is believed in the authoritative school.

I say: If we accept the interpretation as a deposit, the soundest view is that it is a trust (amānah). Thus, his claim of loss (talaf) after the confession, and his claim of return (radd), are accepted. If he says, "I have with me (ʿindī) or in my possession (maʿī) a thousand," he is believed in his claim of deposit, return, and loss, categorically (qaṭʿan). And God knows best.

If he confesses to a sale (bayʿ) or gift (hibah) and delivery (iqbāḍ), then says, "It was invalid (fāsid), and I confessed thinking it valid," it is not accepted. He may administer an oath to the claimant; if the claimant refuses (nukūl), the confessor swears and is absolved.

If he says, "This house belongs to Zayd, rather (bal) to ʿAmr," or "I usurped it from Zayd, rather from ʿAmr," and delivered it to Zayd, the most apparent view is that the confessor pays its value (qīmah) to ʿAmr, by virtue of the confession.

An exception (istithnāʾ) is valid if it is contiguous (muttaṣil) and does not exhaust the confession (mustaghriq). Thus, if he says, "He has against me ten, except nine, except eight," nine is obligatory. It is valid from a different genus, like "a thousand, except a garment (thawb)," clarified as a garment worth less than a thousand. It is valid from a specified thing (muʿayyan), like "This house is his, except this room," or "These dirhams are his, except this dirham." In the case of a specified thing, there is an anomalous view (wajh shādhdh).

I say: If he says, "These slaves are his, except one," it is accepted, and the clarification (bayān) reverts to him. If they all die except one, and he claims that it is the excepted one, he is believed with his oath in the soundest view. And God knows best.

chapters.arabic_text:
# فصل
# أقر بنسب إن ألحقه بنفسه اشترط لصحته أن لا يكذبه الحس ولا الشرع بأن

يكون معروف النسب من غيره وأن يصدقه المستلحق إن كان أهلا للتصديق فإن كان

بالغا فكذبه لم يثبت إلا ببينة وإن استحلق صغيرا ثبت فلو بلغ وكذبه لم يبطل

في الأصح ويصح أن يستلحق ميتا صغيرا وكذا كبيرا في الأصح ويرثه ولو استلحق

اثنان بالغا ثبت لمن صدقه وحكم الصغير يأتي في اللقيط إن شاء الله تعالى

ولو قال لولد أمته هذا ولدي ثبت نسبه ولا يثبت الاستيلاد في الأظهر وكذا لو

قال ولدي ولدته في ملكي فإن قال علقت به في ملكي ثبت الإستيلاد فإن كانت

فراشا له لحقه بالفراش من غير استلحاق وإن كانت مزوجة فالولد للزوج

واستلحاق السيد باطل وأما إذا ألحق النسب بغيره كهذا أخي أو عمي ثبت نسبه

من الملحق به بالشروط السابقة ويشترط كون الملحق به ميتا ولا يشترط أن لا

يكون نفاه في الأصح ويشترط كون المقر وارثا حائزا والأصح أن المستلحق لا

يرث ولا يشارك المقر في حصته وأن البالغ من الورثة لا ينفرد بالإقرار وأنه

لو أقر أحد الوارثين وأنكر الآخر ومات ولم يرثه إلا المقر ثبت النسب وأنه

لو أقر ابن حائز بأخوة مجهولة فأنكر المجهول نسب المقر لم يؤثر فيه ويثبت

أيضا نسب المجهول وأنه إذا كان الوارث الظاهر يحجبه المستلحق كأخ أقر بابن

للميت ثبت النسب ولا إرث
# 

| كتاب العارية
# شرط المعير صحة تبرعه وملكه المنفعة فيعير مستأجر لا مستعير على الصحيح

وله أن يستنيب من يستوفي المنفعة له والمستعار كونه منتفعا به مع بقاء عينه

وتجوز إعارة جارية لخدمة امرأة أو محرم ويكره إعارة عبد مسلم لكافر والأصح

اشتراط  لفظ كأعرتك أو أعرني ويكفي لفظ أحدهما مع فعل الآخر ولو قال أعرتكه

لتعلفه أو لتعيرني فرسك فهو إجارة فاسدة توجب أجرة المثل ومؤنة الرد على

المستعير فإن تلفت لا باستعمال ضمنها وإن لم يفرط والأصح أنه لا يضمن ما

ينمحق أو ينسحق باستعمال والثالث: يضمن المنمحق والمستعير من مستأجر لا

يضمن في الأصح ولو تلفت دابته في يد وكيل بعثه في شغله أو في يد من سلمها

إليه ليروضها فلا ضمان وله الانتفاع بحسب الإذن فإن أعار لزراعة حنطة زرعها

ومثلها إن لم ينهه أو لشعير لم يزرع فوقه كحنطة ولو أطلق الزراعة صح في

الأصح ويزرع إن شاء وإذا استعار لبناء أو غراس فله الزرع ولا عكس والصحيح

أنه لا يغرس مستعير لبناء وكذا العكس وأنه لا تصح إعارة الأرض مطلقة بل

يشترط تعيين نوع المنفعة.
#
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ن-س-ب (n-s-b)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Core meaning of relation, affiliation, or lineage; establishing a connection between a person and another through descent.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In legal-theological terms, it denotes the formal establishment of filial or kinship ties (nasab) with attendant inheritance and guardianship rights.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Used literally (ḥaqīqah) for genealogical linkage; metaphorically (majāz) for any attributed relation, but here strictly literal in juristic context.
- Root: ع-ر-ض (ʿ-r-ḍ) [for ʿāriyah]
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Root meaning of lending, granting temporary use of an object while retaining ownership.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): A contractual transfer of usufruct (manfaʿah) without transfer of ownership, distinct from gift (hibah).
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal for the act of lending; metaphorical extension to any temporary concession, but juristically confined to the literal sense.
- Sībawayh Rule: Conditional Clause Structure (al-Sharṭ wa al-Jawāb) — Governing the syntactic linkage of conditions (e.g., 'if he acknowledges... then it is established') with precise apodosis placement, as applied throughout the legal rulings.
chapters.translation:
I say: Know that if a person acknowledges a lineage, attaching it to himself, it is a condition for its validity that neither sensory perception nor sacred law (al-sharʿ) renders it false — such as when the person is known by others to have a different lineage — and that the one whose lineage is acknowledged affirms it, if he is qualified to give affirmation. If he is an adult and denies it, the lineage is not established except by evidence (bayyinah). If he acknowledges a minor, it is established; then if the minor reaches adulthood and denies it, it is not invalidated in the soundest opinion (al-aṣaḥḥ). It is valid to acknowledge a deceased minor, and likewise a deceased adult in the soundest opinion, and he inherits from him. If two persons acknowledge an adult, it is established for the one whom he affirms. The ruling for a minor will come in the chapter on the foundling (al-laqīṭ), God willing.

If he says of his slave-girl's child, 'This is my son,' his lineage is established, but the establishment of motherhood (istīlād) is not affirmed in the most apparent opinion (al-aẓhar). Likewise, if he says, 'My son, born in my possession.' If he says, 'I conceived him in my possession,' then istīlād is established. If she is his wife (farāsh), the child is attributed to him by virtue of the marriage bed without any acknowledgment. If she is married to another, the child belongs to the husband, and the master's acknowledgment is void.

As for when he attaches the lineage to another, such as saying, 'This is my brother' or 'my uncle,' the lineage is established for the one to whom it is attached, subject to the aforementioned conditions. It is a condition that the one to whom it is attached be deceased, and it is not a condition that he had not denied him in the soundest opinion. It is a condition that the acknowledger be an heir in possession (wārith ḥāʾiz). The soundest opinion is that the one whose lineage is acknowledged does not inherit and does not share in the acknowledger's portion; that an adult among the heirs cannot make an exclusive acknowledgment; that if one of two heirs acknowledges and the other denies, and the deceased dies and only the acknowledger inherits from him, the lineage is established; that if an heir in possession acknowledges an unknown brother, and the unknown one denies the acknowledger's lineage, it does not affect him, and the unknown one's lineage is also established; and that if the apparent heir is veiled (maḥjūb) by the one whose lineage is acknowledged — such as a brother acknowledging a son of the deceased — the lineage is established but there is no inheritance.

Then begins the Book of Borrowing (Kitāb al-ʿĀriyah).

The lender (muʿīr) is required to have valid capacity for gratuitous donation (ṣiḥḥat tabarruʿ) and ownership of the usufruct. Thus, a lessor may lend, but a borrower may not lend in the soundest opinion. He may appoint a deputy to receive the usufruct on his behalf. The borrowed item must be one from which benefit can be derived while its substance remains intact. It is permissible to lend a slave-girl for the service of a woman or a maḥram (unmarriageable kin). It is disliked (makrūh) to lend a Muslim slave to a disbeliever. The soundest opinion is that a verbal formula is required, such as 'I lend you' (aʿartuka) or 'Lend me' (aʿirnī). It suffices if one party utters the formula and the other performs the act. If he says, 'I lend it to you to fodder it' or 'so that you lend me your horse,' it is a corrupt lease (ijārah fāsidah) requiring the equivalent rent (ujrat al-mithl). The cost of returning the item falls on the borrower. If it perishes without use, he is liable for it even without negligence. The soundest opinion is that he is not liable for what is consumed or ground down by normal use. A third opinion holds liability for what is consumed. A borrower from a lessee does not bear liability in the soundest opinion. If his beast perishes in the hand of an agent he sent for his affair, or in the hand of one to whom he handed it for training, there is no liability. He may use it according to the permission granted. If he lends land for planting wheat, he may plant wheat or its like if he was not prohibited; if lent for barley, he may not plant above it something like wheat. If the permission is absolute, it is valid in the soundest opinion, and he may plant as he wishes. If he borrows for building or planting trees, he may plant crops, but not the reverse. The soundest opinion is that a borrower for building may not plant trees, and likewise the reverse. And it is not valid to lend land absolutely; rather, the type of usufruct must be specified.

chapters.title_en: Section 46 — The Return of Borrowed Items and the Book of Usurpation (Kitāb al-Ghaṣb)
chapters.arabic_text:
# فصل
# لكل منهما رد العارية متى شاء إلا إذا أعار لدفن فلا يرجع حتى يندرس أثر

المدفون وإذا أعار للبناء أو الغراس ولم يذكر مدة ثم رجع إن كان شرط القلع

مجانا لزمه وإلا فإن اختار المستعير القلع قلع ولا يلزمه تسوية الأرض في

الأصح
# قلت: الأصح يلزمه والله أعلم وإن لم يختر لم يقلع مجانا بل للمعير الخيار

بين أن يبقيه بأجرة أو يقلع ويضمن أرش النقص قيل: أو يتملكه بقيمته فإن لم

يختر لم يقلع مجانا إن بذل المستعير الأجرة وكذا إن لم يبذلها في الأصح ثم

قيل: يبيع الحاكم الأرض وما فيها وتقسم بينهما والأصح أنه يعرض عنهما حتى

يختارا شيئا وللمعير دخولها والانتفاع بها ولا يدخلها المستعير بغير إذن

للتفرج ويجوز للسقي والإصلاح في الأصح ولكل بيع ملكه وقيل: ليس للمستعير

بيعه لثالث والعارية المؤقتة كالمطلقة وفي قول له القلع فيها مجانا إذا رجع

وإذا أعار لزراعة ورجع قبل إدراك الزرع فالصحيح أن عليه الإبقاء إلى الحصاد

وأن له الأجرة فلو عين مدة ولم يدرك فيها لتقصيره بتأخير الزراعة قلع مجانا

ولو حمل السيل بذرا إلى أرضه فنبت  فهو لصاحب البذر والأصح أنه يجبر على

قلعه ولو ركب دابة وقال لمالكها أعرتنيها فقال بل أجرتكها أو اختلف مالك

الأرض وزارعها كذلك فالمصدق المالك على المذهب وكذا لو قال أعرتني وقال بل

غصبت مني فإن تلفت العين فقد اتفقا على الضمان لكن الأصح أن العارية تضمن

بقيمة يوم التلف لا بأقصى القيم ولا بيوم القبض فإن كان ما يدعيه المالك

أكثر حلف للزيادة.
# 

| كتاب الغصب
# هو الاستيلاء على حق الغير عدوانا فلو ركب دابة أو جلس على فراش فغاصب

وإن لم ينقل ولو دخل داره وأزعجه عنها أو أزعجه وقهره على الدار ولم يدخل

فغاصب وفي الثانية وجه واه ولو سكن بيتا ومنع المالك منه دون باقي الدار

فغاصب للبيت فقط ولو دخل بقصد الاستيلاء وليس المالك فيها فغاصب وإن كان

ولم يزعجه فغاصب لنصف الدار إلا أن يكون ضعيفا لا يعد مستوليا على صاحب

الدار وعلى الغاصب الرد فإن تلف عنده ضمنه ولو أتلف مالا في يد مالكه ضمنه

ولو فتح رأس زق مطروح على الأرض فخرج ما فيه بالفتح أو منصوب فسقط بالفتح

وخرج ما فيه ضمن وإن سقط بعارض ريح لم يضمن ولو فتح قفصا عن طائر وهيجه

فطار ضمن وإن اقتصر على الفتح فالأظهر أنه إذا طار في الحال ضمن وإن وقف ثم

طار فلا والأيدي المترتبة على يد الغاصب أيدي ضمان وإن جهل صاحبها الغصب ثم

إن علم فكغاصب من غاصب فيستقر عليه ضمان ما تلف عنده وكذا إن جهل وكانت يده

في أصلها يد ضمان كالعارية وإن كانت يد أمانة كوديعة فالقرار على الغاصب

ومتى أتلف الآخذ من الغاصب مستقلا به فالقرار عليه مطلقا وإن حمله الغاصب

عليه بأن قدم له طعاما مغصوبا ضيافة فأكله فكذا في الأظهر وعلى هذا لو قدمه

لمالكه فأكله برىء الغاصب.
#

# فصل
# تضمن نفس الرقيق بقيمة تلف أو أتلف تحت يد عادية وأبعاضه التي لا يتقدر

أرشها من الحر بما نقص من قيمته وكذا المقدرة إن تلفت وإن  أتلفت فكذا في

القديم وعلى الجديد تتقدر من الرقيق والقيمة فيه كالدية في الحر ففي يده

نصف قيمته وسائر الحيوان بالقيمة وغيره مثلى ومتقوم والأصح أن المثلى ما

حصره كيل أو وزن وجاز السلم فيه كماء وتراب ونحاس وتبر ومسك وكافور وقطن

وعنب ودقيق لا غالية ومعجون فيضمن المثلى بمثله تلف أو أتلف فإن تعذر

فالقيمة والأصح أن المعتبر أقصى قيمة من وقت الغصب إلى تعذر المثل ولو نقل

المغصوب المثلى إلى بلد آخر فللمالك أن يكلفه رده وأن يطالبه بالقيمة في

الحال فإذا رده ردها فإن تلف في البلد المنقول إليه طالبه بالمثل في أي

البلدين شاء فإن فقد المثل غرمه قيمة أكثر البلدين قيمة ولو ظفر بالغاصب في

غير بلد التلف فالصحيح أنه إن كان لا مؤنة لنقله كالنقد فله مطالبته بالمثل

وإلا فلا مطالبة بالمثل بل يغرمه قيمة بلد التلف وأما المتقوم فيضمن بأقصى

قيمه من الغصب إلى التلف وفي الإتلاف بلا غصب بقيمة يوم التلف فإن جنى وتلف

بسراية فالواجب الأقصى أيضا ولا تضمن الخمر ولا تراق على ذمي إلا أن يظهر

شربها أو بيعها وترد عليه إن بقيت العين وكذا المحترمة إذا غصبت من مسلم

والأصنام وآلات الملاهي لا يجب في إبطالها شيء والأصح أنها لا تكسر الكسر

الفاحش بل تفصل لتعود كما قبل التأليف فإن عجز المنكر عن رعاية هذا الحد

لمنع صاحب المنكر أبطله كيف تيسر وتضمن منفعة الدار والعبد ونحوهما

بالتفويت والفوات في يد عادية ولا تضمن منفعة البضع إلا بتفويت وكذا منفعة

بدن الحر في الأصح وإذا نقص المغصوب بغير استعمال وجب الأرش مع الأجرة وكذا

لو نقص به بأن بلى الثوب في الأصح.
#
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ع-و-ر (ʿ-w-r)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To return to a state of defect or vacancy; the core sense of 'ʿārah' is a loan that leaves a void in the possessor's hand, hence its temporary nature.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In legal theology, ʿāriyah denotes a gratuitous transfer of usufruct (manfaʿah) with ownership of the corpus retained by the lender—its temporality is intrinsic.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal (ḥaqīqah) in the sense of 'lending' as a void-filling act; metaphorical (majāz) when applied to the right of recall, which is a juristic extension.
- Root: غ-ص-ب (gh-ṣ-b)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To take something by force or oppression; the root implies a violent seizure that strips the owner of control.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Technically, ghaṣb is the unlawful usurpation of another's right (ḥaqq) with transgression (ʿudwān)—a foundational tort in Islamic law.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal for physical seizure; metaphorical for any act that usurps a right, such as intimidation or entry without transfer.
- Root: ض-م-ن (ḍ-m-n)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To include, contain, or guarantee; the root conveys the idea of bearing responsibility for what is encompassed.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In legal discourse, ḍamān is the liability for compensation (damān) arising from tortious acts or breach of trust.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal for 'surety' or 'liability'; metaphorical for the jurisprudential rule that a usurper's hand is a hand of guarantee (yad ḍamān).
- Sībawayh Rule: Conditional and Disjunctive Constructions (al-Sharṭ wa al-Taqsīm) — For parsing complex rulings with 'if...then...' (fa-in... fa-...) and 'either...or...' (immā... aw...), ensuring each legal branch is syntactically isolated yet logically connected.
chapters.translation:
I say: Each of the two parties—the lender and the borrower—has the right to demand the return of the borrowed item (radd al-ʿāriyah) whenever he wishes, except when the loan was given for burial; in that case, the lender may not reclaim it until the traces of the buried person have completely vanished. And if the loan was given for construction or planting, and no duration was specified, then the lender may revoke the loan. If the revocation stipulated that the borrower must remove the construction or plants for free, that stipulation is binding upon him. Otherwise, if the borrower chooses to remove them, he may do so, and he is not obligated to level the ground—this is the sounder opinion (al-aṣaḥḥ).

I say: The sounder opinion is that he is obligated to level it, and God knows best. But if the borrower does not choose to remove, then it is not removed for free. Rather, the lender has the option between leaving it in place for rent or removing it and claiming compensation for the diminution in value. It was also said: or he may take ownership of it at its market value. If the lender does not choose any of these, it is not removed for free if the borrower offers the rent—and likewise if he does not offer it, according to the sounder opinion. Then it was said: the judge sells the land and what is upon it, and the proceeds are divided between them. But the sounder opinion is that the judge leaves them both alone until they choose something. The lender may enter the land and benefit from it, but the borrower may not enter it without permission merely for leisure; however, he may enter for irrigation and repair—this is the sounder opinion. Each of them may sell what he owns. It was also said: the borrower may not sell it to a third party. A time-limited loan (al-ʿāriyah al-muʾaqqatah) is treated like an absolute one; and in one saying, the borrower has the right to remove for free if the lender revokes. And if the loan was for cultivation and the lender revokes before the crop ripens, the correct view (al-ṣaḥīḥ) is that he must leave it until harvest, and he is entitled to rent. But if a specific duration was set and the crop did not ripen within it due to the borrower's negligence in delaying the sowing, then it is removed for free. If a flood carries seeds into a man's land and they sprout, the crop belongs to the owner of the seeds, and the sounder opinion is that he is compelled to remove it. And if a man rides an animal and says to its owner, 'You lent it to me,' but the owner says, 'Rather, I rented it to you,' or if the owner of the land and its cultivator dispute similarly, then the owner is believed (al-muṣaddaq) according to the school (al-madhhab). Likewise, if the borrower says, 'You lent it to me,' and the owner says, 'Rather, you usurped it from me,' then if the object perishes, they agree on liability, but the sounder opinion is that a borrowed item is guaranteed by its value on the day of destruction, not by the highest value nor by the day of receipt. If what the owner claims is greater, he takes an oath for the increase.

[Book of Usurpation (Kitāb al-Ghaṣb)]

Usurpation (ghaṣb) is the seizure of another's right with transgression. Thus, if a man rides an animal or sits on a carpet, he is a usurper (ghāṣib), even if he does not move it. And if he enters another's house and disturbs him from it, or disturbs him and overpowers him regarding the house without entering, he is a usurper—though in the second case there is a weak view (wajh wāhin). And if he occupies a room and prevents the owner from it, but not the rest of the house, he is a usurper of that room only. And if he enters with the intent of seizure while the owner is not present, he is a usurper. And if he enters without disturbing the owner, he is a usurper of half the house, unless he is so weak that he is not deemed to have overpowered the owner. The usurper is obligated to return the property; if it perishes in his possession, he is liable for it. And if he destroys property in the owner's hand, he is liable. If he opens the head of a waterskin lying on the ground and its contents spill out due to the opening, or if it was upright and fell due to the opening and its contents spilled, he is liable. But if it fell due to a gust of wind, he is not liable. And if he opens a cage for a bird and startles it so it flies away, he is liable. If he merely opens the cage, the most apparent view (al-aẓhar) is that if it flies immediately, he is liable; but if it pauses and then flies, he is not. Hands that are subsequent to the usurper's hand are hands of liability (aydī ḍamān), even if the subsequent holder was ignorant of the usurpation. Then, if he learns of it, he is like a usurper from a usurper, and liability for what perished in his possession settles upon him. Likewise, if he was ignorant but his hand was originally a hand of liability, like a borrowed item. But if his hand was a hand of trust (yad amānah), like a deposit (wadīʿah), then the ultimate liability falls upon the original usurper. Whenever the taker from the usurper destroys the property independently, the ultimate liability falls upon him absolutely. And if the usurper caused him to do so—for example, by presenting usurped food as hospitality and he ate it—then likewise, according to the most apparent view. And upon this, if the usurper presented it to the owner himself and he ate it, the usurper is absolved of liability.

[Section]

The slave himself is guaranteed by his value if he perishes or is destroyed under a wrongful hand. His parts that have no fixed compensation (arsh) from a free person are guaranteed by the diminution in his value. Likewise, parts with fixed compensation, if they perish—and if they are destroyed, then likewise according to the old view (al-qadīm). But according to the new view (al-jadīd), they are assessed proportionally from the slave, and the value therein is like the blood-money (diyah) for a free person; thus, for a hand, half his value. Other animals are guaranteed by their value. Other property is either fungible (mithlī) or non-fungible (mutaqawwim). The sounder opinion is that fungible is what is confined by measure or weight and in which salam (advance payment) is valid—like water, earth, copper, unrefined silver, musk, camphor, cotton, grapes, and flour—but not perfumed mixtures or pastes. A fungible is guaranteed by its like (mithl) whether it perishes or is destroyed; if its like is unavailable, then by its value. The sounder opinion is that the consideration is the highest value from the time of usurpation until the time when the like becomes unavailable. And if a usurped fungible is transported to another land, the owner may compel its return or demand its value immediately. If it is returned, he returns the value. If it perishes in the land to which it was transported, he may demand its like in whichever of the two lands he wishes. If the like is unavailable, the usurper pays the value of the more valuable of the two lands. And if the owner finds the usurper in a land other than the place of destruction, the correct view is that if there is no cost to transport it—like currency—he may demand its like; otherwise, he may not demand its like but must pay the value of the land of destruction. As for the non-fungible, it is guaranteed by its highest value from usurpation to destruction. In destruction without usurpation, it is by the value on the day of destruction. If it commits an injury and perishes from the spread of that injury, the highest value is also obligatory. Wine is not guaranteed, nor is it spilled over a dhimmī unless its drinking or sale becomes apparent; and if the substance remains, it is returned to him. Likewise, property respected (muḥtaramah) if usurped from a Muslim. Idols and instruments of amusement (ālāt al-malāhī) incur no obligation for their destruction. The sounder opinion is that they are not broken with a severe break, but rather disassembled so they may return to their prior state before assembly. If the one who disapproves is unable to observe this limit due to the owner of the disapproved object preventing him, he may destroy it in whatever manner is feasible. The usufruct (manfaʿah) of a house, a slave, and similar items is guaranteed by its loss (tafwīt) or by its passing away (fawāt) under a wrongful hand. The usufruct of sexual intimacy (manfaʿat al-buḍʿ) is not guaranteed except by its loss; likewise, the usufruct of a free person's body, according to the sounder opinion. And if a usurped object diminishes in value without use, the compensation for the defect (arsh) is obligatory along with the rent. Likewise, if it diminishes due to use—such as a garment wearing out—this is the sounder opinion.

chapters.arabic_text:
# فصل
# ادعى تلفه وأنكر المالك صدق الغاصب بيمينه على الصحيح فإذا حلف غرمه

المالك في الأصح ولو اختلف في قيمته أو الثياب التي على العبد المغصوب أو

في عيب خلقي صدق الغاصب بيمينه وفي عيب حادث يصدق المالك بيمينه في الأصح

ولو رده ناقص القيمة لم يلزمه  شيء ولو غصب ثوبا قيمته عشرة فصار بالرخص

درهما فلبسه فأبلاه فصارت نصف درهم فرده لزمه خمسة وهي قسط التالف من أقصى

القيم.
# قلت: ولو غصب خفين قيمتهما عشرة فتلف أحدهما ورد الآخر وقيمته درهمان أو

أتلف أحدهما غصبا أو في يد مالكه لزمه ثمانية في الأصح والله أعلم ولو حدث

نقص يسرى إلى التلف بأن جعل الحنطة هريسة فكالتالف وفي قول يرده مع أرش

النقص ولو جنى المغصوب فتعلق برقبته مال لزم الغاصب تخليصه بالأقل من قيمته

والمال فإن تلف في يده غرمه المالك وللمجني عليه تغريمه وأن يتعلق بما أخذه

المالك ثم يرجع المالك على الغاصب ولو رد العبد إلى المالك فبيع في الجناية

رجع المالك بما أخذه المجني عليه على الغاصب ولو غصب أرضا فنقل ترابها

أجبرها المالك على رده أو رد مثله وإعادة الأرض كما كانت وللناقل الرد وإن

لم يطالبه المالك إن كان له فيه غرض وإلا فلا يرده بلا إذن في الأصح ويقاس

بما ذكرنا حفر البئر وطمها إذا أعاد الأرض كما كانت ولم يبق نقص فلا أرش

لكن عليه أجرة المثل لمدة الإعادة وإن بقي نقص وجب أرشه معها ولو غصب زيتا

ونحوه وأغلاه فنقصت عينه دون قيمته رده ولزمه الذاهب في الأصح وإن نقصت
# 
# القيمة فقط لزمه الأرش وإن نقصتا غرم الذاهب ورد الباقي مع أرشه إن كان

نقص القيمة أكثر والأصح أن السمن لا يجبر نقص هزال قبله وإن تذكر صنعة

نسيها يجبر النسيان وتعلم صنعة لا يجبره نسيان أخرى قطعا ولو غصب عصيرا

فتخمر ثم تخلل فالأصح أن الخل للمالك وعلى الغاصب الأرش إن كان الخل أنقص

قيمة ولو غصب خمرا فتخللت أو جلد ميتة فدبغه فالأصح أن الخل والجلد للمغصوب

منه
chapters.anchors:
- Root: غ-ر-م (gh-r-m)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Core meaning is "to be burdened with a debt or liability" — the obligatory payment of what one owes as recompense.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In legal-theological usage, it denotes the imposition of financial liability (ḍamān) as a consequence of wrongful acts, distinct from penal or ritual obligations.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Used literally here — actual financial liability — not metaphorically as "sin" or "fault" (which is a secondary Majāz).
- Root: ق-و-م (q-w-m)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Root signifies "standing" or "being upright"; from it derives "value" (qīmah) as that which makes a thing stand in exchange.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Technical term for market value (qīmah) in transactional justice — the equitable measure of compensation.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal in legal context — objective exchange value; not metaphorical "standing" or "status."
- Root: ع-و-ر (ʿ-w-r)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Core meaning is "defect" or "blemish" — that which renders a thing deficient in its essence or appearance.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In legal discourse, ʿayb denotes a physical or intrinsic deficiency affecting the object's utility or value.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal — a tangible flaw; distinct from metaphorical "blindness" (also from this root) in rhetorical usage.
- Sībawayh Rule: Conditional-Responsive Construction (al-Sharṭ wa al-Jawāb) — The text employs "if... then..." (law... fa...) structures where the protasis establishes a hypothetical legal scenario and the apodosis states the binding ruling, requiring precise temporal and causal sequencing.
chapters.translation:
I say: Know that this section addresses disputes arising from usurpation (ghaṣb) and the consequent financial liabilities.

If the usurper claims that the usurped object has perished, and the owner denies this claim, then the usurper is credited upon his oath — this is the soundest (al-ṣaḥīḥ) position. When he swears, he is liable for its value (ghurmah) to the owner — this is the most correct (al-aṣaḥḥ) ruling.

If they differ concerning its value, or concerning the garments worn by the usurped slave, or concerning a congenital defect (ʿayb khalqī) in the slave, then the usurper is credited upon his oath. However, if the dispute concerns a defect that arose after the usurpation (ʿayb ḥādith), then the owner is credited upon his oath — this is the most correct position.

If the usurper returns the object while it has diminished in value, nothing further is incumbent upon him. For example: if he usurped a garment worth ten dirhams, and its market price fell to one dirham, then he wore it until it wore out, and its value became half a dirham, and he returned it — he owes five dirhams, which is the proportion of the perished portion relative to the highest value.

I say: If he usurped two sandals worth ten dirhams, and one of them perished while he returned the other whose value is two dirhams — or if he destroyed one of them, whether by further usurpation or while in the owner's hand — he owes eight dirhams, this being the most correct position. And Allah knows best.

If a deficiency arises that inevitably leads to total destruction — such as turning wheat into a paste (harīsah) — then it is treated as if it had perished entirely. In another opinion (qawl), he returns it along with compensation for the diminution (arsh al-naqṣ).

If the usurped object commits an injury (jināyah), and a financial claim becomes attached to its neck (i.e., its value becomes liable for the injury), then the usurper is obligated to redeem it by paying the lesser of two amounts: its value or the claim. If it perishes in his hand, the owner may claim its value from him, and the injured party may also claim compensation from the usurper, or may attach his claim to whatever the owner has received. Then the owner may seek recourse against the usurper for what the injured party took.

If the usurper returns the slave to the owner, and the slave is then sold to satisfy the injury claim, the owner may seek recourse against the usurper for what the injured party received.

If he usurped land and removed its soil, the owner may compel him to return it, or to return an equivalent amount, and to restore the land to its original state. The one who removed the soil may return it even if the owner does not demand it, provided he has some interest in doing so. Otherwise, he may not return it without permission — this is the most correct position.

By analogy with what we have mentioned: digging a well and filling it — if he restores the land to its original state and no deficiency remains, then no compensation (arsh) is due. However, he owes the equivalent wage (ujrat al-mithl) for the period of restoration. If a deficiency remains, its compensation is obligatory in addition to that wage.

If he usurped oil or the like, and it thickened (ightalā) such that its substance diminished but its value did not, he returns it and owes the amount of the lost substance — this is the most correct position. If only its value diminished, he owes the compensation for the diminution. If both substance and value diminished, he owes the lost amount and returns the remainder along with compensation for the diminution, if the loss in value is greater.

The most correct position is that clarified butter (samn) does not require compensation for the loss of weight due to emaciation that occurred prior to the usurpation. If a craftsman forgets a skill he once knew, the forgetfulness is compensated for. But if he learns a new skill, the forgetfulness of another skill does not excuse him — this is certain (qaṭʿan).

If he usurped grape juice (ʿaṣīr) and it fermented into wine, then turned to vinegar, the most correct position is that the vinegar belongs to the owner, and the usurper owes compensation if the vinegar is of lesser value.

If he usurped wine and it turned to vinegar, or usurped the skin of a dead animal (maytah) and tanned it, the most correct position is that the vinegar and the tanned skin belong to the one from whom they were usurped.

chapters.title_en: Section 48 — On the Increase of the Usurped Property, Its Mixture, and the Chapter of Preemption (Kitāb al-Shufʿah)
chapters.arabic_text:
# فصل
# زيادة المغصوب إن كانت أثرا محضا كقصارة فلا شيء للغاصب بسببها وللمالك

تكليفه رده كما كان إن أمكن وأرش النقص وإن كانت عينا كبناء وغراس كلف

القلع وإن صبغ الثوب بصبغه وأمكن فصله اجبر عليه في الأصح  وإن لم يمكن فإن

لم تزد قيمته فلا شيء للغاصب فيه وإن نقصت لزمه الأرش وإن زادت اشتركا فيه

ولو خلط المغصوب بغيره وأمكن التمييز لزمه وإن شق فإن تعذر فالمذهب أنه

كالتالف فله تغريمه وللغاصب أن يعطيه من غير المخلوط ولو غصب خشبة وبنى

عليها أخرجت ولو أدرجها في سفينة فكذلك إلا أن يخاف تلف نفس أو مال معصومين

ولو وطىء المغصوبة عالما بالتحريم حد وإن جهل فلا حد وفي الحالين يجب المهر

إلا أن تطاوعه فلا يجب على الصحيح وعليها الحد إن علمت ووطء المشتري من

الغاصب كوطئه في الحد والمهر فإن غرمه لم يرجع به على الغاصب في الأظهر وإن

أحبل عالما بالتحريم فالود رقيق غير نسيب وإن جهل فحر نسيب
# 
# وعليه قيمته يوم الانفصال ويرجع بها المشتري على الغاصب ولو تلف المغصوب

عند المشتري وغرمه لم يرجع به وكذا لو تعيب عنده في الأظهر ولا يرجع بغرم

منفعة استوفاها في الأظهر ويرجع بغرم ما تلف عنده وبأرش نقض بنائه وغراسه

إذا نقض في الأصح وكل ما لو غرمه المشتري رجع به لو غرمه الغاصب لم يجرع به

على المشتري وما لا فيرجع.
# قلت: وكل من انبنت يده على يد الغاصب فكالمشتري. والله أعلم.
# 

| كتاب الشفعة
# لا تثبت في منقول بل في أرض وما فيها من بناء وشجر تبعا وكذا ثمر لم يؤبر

في الأصح ولا شفعة في حجرة بنيت على سقف غير مشترك وكذا مشترك في الأصح وكل

ما لو قسم بطلت منفعته المقصودة كحمام ورحى لا شفعة فيه في الأصح ولا شفعة

إلا لشريك ولو باع دارا وله شريك في ممرها فلا شفعة له فيها والصحيح ثبوتها

في الممر إن كان للمشتري طريق آخر إلى الدار أو أمكن فتح باب إلى شارع وإلا

فلا وإنما تثبت فيما ملك بمعاوضة ملكا لازما متأخرا عن ملك الشفيع كمبيع

ومهر وعوض خلع وصلح دم ونجوم وأجرة ورأس مال سلم ولو شرط في البيع الخيار

لهما أو للبائع لم  يؤخذ بالشفعة حتى ينقطع الخيار وإن شرط للمشتري وحده

فالأظهر أنه يؤخذ إن قلنا الملك للمشتري وإلا فلا ولو وجد المشتري بالشقص

عيبا وأراد رده بالعيب وأراد الشفيع أخذه ويرضى بالعيب فالأظهر إجابة

الشفيع ولو اشترى اثنان دارا أو بعضها فلا شفعة لأحدهما على الآخر ولو كان

للمشتري شرك في الأرض فالأصح أن الشريك لا يأخذ كل المبيع بل حصته ولا

يشترط في التملك بالشفعة حكم حاكم ولا إحضار الثمن ولا حضور المشتري ويشترط

لفظ من الشفيع كتملكت أو أخذت بالشفعة ويشترط مع ذلك إما تسليم العوض إلى

المشتري فإذا تسلمه أو ألزمه القاضي التسلم ملك الشفيع الشقص وإما رضا

المشتري
# 
# بكون العوض في ذمته وإما قضاء القاضي له بالشفعة إذا حضر مجلسه وأثبت حقه

فيملك به في الأصح ولا يتملك شقضا لم يره الشفيع على المذهب.
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ز-ي-د (z-y-d)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Increase, augmentation, surplus added to a thing.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): An accidental accretion (ziyādah) distinct from the essence of the property, bearing legal consequence in liability.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal in physical growth; metaphorical in value increment.
- Root: غ-ص-ب (gh-s-b)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Taking another's property by force or unjust seizure.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Unlawful dominion (yad ʿādiyah) entailing strict liability (ḍamān).
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal for physical seizure; extended to any unlawful possession.
- Root: ش-ف-ع (sh-f-ʿ)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To join, pair, or add; preemption as joining a co-owner's share.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Legal right of a co-owner to acquire a sold share to prevent harm (ḍarar).
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal in pairing; metaphorical in the legal claim of substitution.
- Sībawayh Rule: Conditional and Exceptive Constructions (al-sharṭ wa al-istithnāʾ) — Governing the nuanced rulings of "if possible" (in amkana) and "the soundest view" (al-aṣaḥḥ), requiring precise parsing of apodosis and protasis.
chapters.translation:
I say: Know that the increase of the usurped property (al-maghṣūb) — if it is a mere trace (atharan maḥḍan), such as the fulling of cloth (qiṣārah) — then the usurper (al-ghāṣib) has no claim therein by reason of it, and the owner is charged with its restoration to its former state if that is possible, along with the compensation for the diminution (arsh al-nuqṣān). But if the increase is a corporeal entity (ʿaynan), such as a building or a planting (ghirās), the usurper is compelled to uproot it. And if he dyed the garment with his own dye, and separation is possible, he is compelled to do so in the soundest view (al-aṣaḥḥ). If separation is not possible, then: if the value has not increased, the usurper has no claim therein; if it has diminished, he is liable for the diminution; and if it has increased, they share in it.

And if the usurped property is mixed with another thing, and separation is possible, he is compelled to separate it; but if that is difficult, and if separation becomes impossible, then the established doctrine (al-madhhab) is that it is treated as destroyed (kāltāf), so the owner may compel him to pay its value, and the usurper may give him [compensation] from the unmixed property. And if he usurped a beam and built it into a structure, it is extracted. And if he incorporated it into a ship, the same applies, unless one fears the loss of a protected life or property (nafs aw māl maʿṣūmayn).

And if he fornicated with the usurped slave-girl (al-maghṣūbah) knowing the prohibition, the prescribed punishment (ḥadd) is inflicted upon him; if he was ignorant, there is no punishment. In both cases, the bridal due (mahr) is obligatory, unless she consented willingly — then it is not obligatory upon him in the sound view (al-ṣaḥīḥ), and the punishment falls upon her if she knew [the prohibition]. And the fornicating of the buyer (al-mushtarī) from the usurper is like the usurper's own act in respect of punishment and bridal due. If he pays it, he does not recover it from the usurper in the most apparent view (al-aẓhar). And if he impregnated her knowing the prohibition, the offspring is a slave, not free-born (raqīq ghayr nasīb); if he was ignorant, it is free-born (ḥurr nasīb). And he owes its value on the day of separation, and the buyer recovers that from the usurper.

And if the usurped property perishes in the buyer's possession, and he pays its value, he does not recover it [from the usurper]. Likewise, if it becomes defective in his possession, in the most apparent view. And he does not recover the compensation for a usufruct (manfaʿah) he has enjoyed, in the most apparent view. But he does recover the compensation for what perished in his possession, and the compensation for the demolition of his building and the uprooting of his planting, if he demolished or uprooted, in the soundest view. And every liability that, if the buyer paid it, he would recover [from the usurper] — if the usurper paid it, he does not recover it from the buyer; and what is not [recoverable in the former case], he does [not recover in the latter].

I say: And everyone whose hand is built upon the hand of the usurper (man ibnat yaduhu ʿalā yad al-ghāṣib) is like the buyer [in these rulings]. And God knows best.

---

THE BOOK OF PREEMPTION (KITĀB AL-SHUFʿAH)

Preemption is not established in movable property (manqūl), but rather in land, and in what is upon it of buildings and trees as a dependent (tabaʿan). Likewise, unripe fruit (thamar lam yuʾabbir) [is included] in the soundest view. And there is no preemption in a chamber (ḥujrah) built upon a ceiling that is not shared, and likewise [no preemption] in a shared [ceiling] in the soundest view. And everything which, if divided, would nullify its intended benefit (manfaʿatuhu al-maqṣūdah) — such as a bathhouse (ḥammām) or a mill (raḥā) — has no preemption therein in the soundest view.

And preemption is only for a co-owner (sharīk). And if one sold a house, and he has a co-owner in its passageway (mamarr), the latter has no preemption in the house itself. The sound view (al-ṣaḥīḥ) is that preemption is established in the passageway if the buyer has another route to the house, or if it is possible to open a door onto the public road; otherwise, no. And it is only established in what is owned by a commutative contract (muʿāwaḍah), with a binding ownership (milkan lāziman) subsequent to the ownership of the preemptor (shafīʿ) — such as a sale (mabīʿ), a bridal due (mahr), the consideration of a divorce at the wife's request (khulʿ), a settlement for homicide (ṣulḥ dam), installments (nujūm), rent (ujrah), and the capital of a salam sale (raʾs māl salam).

And if a condition of option (khiyār) is stipulated in the sale — for both parties or for the seller — the preemptor is not given the property until the option expires. If the option is stipulated for the buyer alone, then the most apparent view (al-aẓhar) is that he is given it if we hold that ownership belongs to the buyer; otherwise, no.

And if the buyer finds a defect (ʿayb) in the share (shiqṣ) and wishes to return it due to the defect, while the preemptor wishes to take it and is content with the defect, then the most apparent view is that the preemptor's request is granted. And if two persons buy a house, or part of it, neither has preemption against the other. And if the buyer has a share in the land, then the soundest view is that the co-owner does not take the entire sold property, but rather his own portion only.

It is not a condition for ownership by preemption that a judge issue a ruling, nor that the price be produced, nor that the buyer be present. But a verbal formula (lafẓ) from the preemptor is required, such as "I have taken ownership" (tamallaktu) or "I have taken by preemption" (akhathtu bil-shufʿah). And along with that, one of three things is required: either the delivery of the consideration to the buyer — and when he receives it, or the judge compels him to receive it, the preemptor owns the share; or the buyer's consent that the consideration remain as a debt in the preemptor's liability (dhimmah); or the judge's decree of preemption for him, when he attends his session and establishes his right — then he owns by it in the soundest view. And he does not take ownership of a share (shiqṣ) he has not seen, according to the established doctrine (al-madhhab).

# فصل
# إن اشترى بمثلي أخذه الشفيع بمثله أو بمتقوم فبقيمته يوم البيع وقيل: يوم

استقراره بانقطاع الخيار أو بمؤجل فالأظهر أنه مخير بين أن يعجل ويأخذ في

الحال أو يصبر إلى المحل ويأخذ ولو بيع شقص وغيره أخذه بحصته من القيمة

ويؤخذ الممهور بمهر مثلها وكذا عوض الخلع ولو اشترى بجزاف وتلف امتنع الأخذ

فإن عين الشفيع قدرا وقال المشتري لم يكن معلوم القدر حلف على نفي العلم

وإن ادعى علمه ولم يعين قدرا لم تسمع دعواه في الأصح وإذا ظهر الثمن مستحقا

فإن كان معينا بطل البيع والشفعة وإلا أبدل وبقيا وإن دفع الشفيع مستحقا لم

تبطل شفعته إن جهل وكذا إن علم في الأصح وتصرف المشتري في الشقص كبيع ووقف

وإجارة صحيح وللشفيع نقض ما لا شفعة فيه كالوقف وأخذه ويتخير فيما فيه شفعة

كبيع بين أن يأخذ بالبيع الثاني أو ينقضه ويأخذ بالأول ولو اختلف المشتري

والشفيع في قدر الثمن صدق المشتري وكذا لو أنكر الشراء أو كون الطالب شريكا

فإن اعترف الشريك بالبيع فالأصح ثبوت الشفعة ويسلم الثمن إلى البائع إن لم

يعترف بقبضه وإن اعترف فهل يترك في  يد الشفيع أم يأخذه القاضي ويحفظه فيه

خلاف سبق في الإقرار نظيره ولو استحق الشفعة جمع أخذوا على قدر الحصص وفي

قول على الرؤس ولو باع أحد الشريكين نصف حصته لرجل ثم باقيها لآخر فالشفعة

في النصف
# 
# الأول للشريك القديم والأصح أنه إن عفا عن النصف الأول شاركه المشتري

الأول في النصف الثاني وإلا فلا والأصح أنه لو عفا أحد شفيعين سقط حقه

ويخبر الآخر بين أخذ الجميع وتركه وليس له الإقتصار على حصته وأن الواحد

إذا أسقط بعض حقه سقط كله ولو حضر أحد شفيعين فله اخذ الجميع في الحال فإذا

حضر الغائب شاركه والأصح أن له تأخير الأخذ إلى قدوم الغائب ولو اشتريا

شقصا فللشفيع أخذ نصيبهما ونصيب أحدهما ولو اشترى واحد من اثنين فله أخذ

حصة أحد البائعين في الأصح والأظهر أن الشفعة على الفور فإذا علم الشفيع

بالبيع فليبادر على العادة فإن كان مريضا أو غائبا عن بلد المشتري أو خائفا

من عدو فليوكل إن قدر وإلا فليشهد على الطلب فإن ترك المقدور عليه منهما

بطل حقه في الأظهر فلو كان في صلاة أو حمام أو طعام فله الإتمام ولو أخر

وقال لم أصدق المخبر لم يعذر إن أخبره عدلان وكذا ثقة في الأصح ويعذر أن

أخبره من لا يقبل خبره ولو أخبر بالبيع بألف فترك فبان بخمسمائة بقي حقه

وإن بان بأكثر بطل ولو لقي المشتري فسلم عليه أو قال بارك الله في صفقتك لم

يبطل وفي الدعاء وجه ولو باع الشفيع حصته جاهلا بالشفعة الأصح بطلانها
# 

| كتاب القراض
# القراض والمضاربة أن يدفع إليه مالا ليتجر فيه والربح مشترك ويشترط لصحته

كون المال دراهم أو دنانير خالصا فلا يجوز على تبر وحلي ومغشوش وعروض

ومعلوما معينا وقيل: يجوز على إحدى الصرتين ومسلما إلى العامل فلا يجوز شرط

كون المال في يد المالك ولا عمله معه ويجوز شرط عمل غلام المالك معه على

الصحيح ووظيفة العامل التجارة وتوابعها كنشر الثياب وطيها فلو قارضه ليشتري

حنطة فيطحن  ويخبز أو غزلا ينسجه ويبيعه فسد القراض ولا يجوز أن يشترط عليه

شراء متاع معين أو نوع يندر وجوده أو معاملة شخص ولا يشترط بيان مدة القرض

فلو ذكر مدة ومنعه التصرف بعدها فسد وإن منعه الشراء بعدها فلا في الأصح

ويشترط اختصاصهما بالربح واشتراكهما فيه ولو قال قارضتك على أن كل الربح لك

فقراض فاسد وقيل: قراض صحيح وإن اقل كله لي فقراض فاسد وقيل: إبضاع وكونه

معلوما بالجزئية فلو قال على أن لك فيه شركة أو نصيبا فسد أو بيننا فالأصح

الصحة ويكون نصفين ولو قال لي النصف فسد في الأصح وإن قال لك النصف صح على

الصحيح ولو شرط لأحدهما عشرة أو ربح صنف فسد.
#
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ش-ف-ع (sh-f-ʿ)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To join, add, or pair; the root conveys the notion of completing a pair or filling a gap — hence the preemptor (shafīʿ) who "joins" the sold share to his own.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In legal-theological usage, it denotes the right of co-ownership to interpose and take the sold share by virtue of partnership, a divinely sanctioned preference (taʿabbudī).
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal sense is "making odd even" (shafʿ = even number); here it is a juristic extension (majāz ʿaqlī) — the preemptor "evens" his holding by annexing the co-owned portion.
- Root: ق-ر-ض (q-r-ḍ)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To cut or sever; qarḍ is a loan that "cuts off" a portion of one's wealth for another's use.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In commercial law, qirāḍ/muḍārabah is a partnership of capital and labor — the owner "cuts" his capital for the agent's enterprise, with profit shared.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal "cutting" is transferred metaphorically to the contractual division of profit between owner and agent.
- Sībawayh Rule: Conditional and Disjunctive Constructions (al-sharṭ wa al-taqsīm) — The text frequently uses "فإن" (if) and "قيل" (it was said) to present legal alternatives; parsing requires identifying the protasis (condition) and apodosis (result) to preserve the author's precise ruling hierarchy.
chapters.translation:
I say: Know that the section on preemption (shufʿah) comprises the following rulings.

If the sale was made for a fungible (mithlī), the preemptor takes it by paying its like; if for a non-fungible (mutaqawwim), then by its value on the day of sale. And it was said: on the day of its stabilization (istiqrār) upon the lapse of the option (khiyār). If the sale was for a deferred price, the stronger view (al-aẓhar) is that he is given the choice between paying immediately and taking the property at once, or waiting until the term matures and then taking it. If a share (shiqṣ) was sold together with other property, he takes it by his proportionate share of the total price. The dower (mahr) is taken by the like of its value (mahr al-mithl), and likewise the consideration for khulʿ (divorce at the wife's request). If the purchase was made by bulk (juzāf) and the goods perished, taking is precluded. If the preemptor specifies an amount and the seller says, "It was not known in amount," the seller swears to his denial of knowledge. If the seller claims knowledge but does not specify an amount, his claim is not heard, according to the soundest view (al-aṣaḥḥ). When the price turns out to be claimed by a third party (mustaḥaqq): if it was specified, the sale and the preemption are void; otherwise, it is substituted and both remain. If the preemptor pays a price that is later claimed by another, his preemption is not voided if he was ignorant; likewise if he knew, according to the soundest view. If the buyer disposes of the share — such as selling, endowing (waqf), or leasing — validly, the preemptor may annul that which admits no preemption, such as the endowment, and take it; and he has the choice regarding that which admits preemption, such as a sale, between taking by the second sale or annulling it and taking by the first. If the buyer and the preemptor differ over the amount of the price, the buyer is believed. Likewise if he denies the purchase or that the claimant is a co-owner. If the co-owner admits the sale, the soundest view is that preemption is established, and the price is handed to the seller if he does not admit receipt; if he admits receipt, there is a dispute — whether it is left in the preemptor's hand or the judge takes and preserves it — the like of which has preceded in the chapter on acknowledgment (iqrār). If several persons are entitled to preemption, they all take according to their shares; and in one saying, according to heads. If one of two co-owners sells half of his share to a man, then the remainder to another, preemption applies to the first half for the original co-owner; and the soundest view is that if he waives the first half, he shares with the first buyer in the second half; otherwise not. The soundest view is that if one of two preemptors waives, his right lapses, and the other is given the choice between taking the whole or leaving it; he may not restrict himself to his own share. And that if a single preemptor drops part of his right, the whole lapses. If one of two preemptors is present, he may take the whole immediately; when the absent one arrives, he shares with him. The soundest view is that he may delay taking until the absent one's arrival. If two persons buy a share, the preemptor may take the portions of both, or the portion of one of them. If one person buys from two sellers, he may take the share of one of the two sellers, according to the soundest view. The most manifest view (al-aẓhar) is that preemption is immediate (ʿalā al-fawr): when the preemptor learns of the sale, he must hasten according to custom. If he is sick, or absent from the buyer's town, or fearful of an enemy, he should appoint an agent if able; otherwise, he should bear witness to his claim. If he neglects what he is able to do of these, his right lapses, in the most manifest view. If he is in prayer, or the bath, or at a meal, he may complete it. If he delays and says, "I did not believe the informant," he is not excused if two just witnesses informed him; likewise a trustworthy single person, in the soundest view. He is excused if informed by one whose report is unacceptable. If he was informed of a sale for a thousand and he desisted, then it became apparent it was for five hundred, his right remains; if it became apparent it was for more, it lapses. If he met the buyer and greeted him, or said, "May Allah bless your transaction," it does not lapse; regarding supplication (duʿāʾ) there is a face (wajh). If the preemptor sells his own share while ignorant of the preemption, the soundest view is that his right is voided.

| The Book of Qirāḍ (Commenda Partnership)

Qirāḍ and muḍārabah consist of one party handing over to another wealth to trade with it, the profit being shared between them. For its validity it is required that the capital be dirhams or dīnārs, pure — so it is not valid upon uncoined gold (tibr), jewelry, alloyed coinage, or commodities — and that it be known and specified. It was said: it is valid upon one of the two currencies. It must be handed over to the agent, so it is not valid to stipulate that the capital remain in the owner's hand, nor that he work alongside him. It is valid to stipulate the work of the owner's slave with him, according to the sound (al-ṣaḥīḥ). The agent's function is trade and its accessories, such as spreading and folding garments. If he contracts with him to buy wheat, then grind and bake it, or yarn to weave and sell, the qirāḍ is corrupted. It is not valid to stipulate upon him the purchase of a specific commodity, or a type rarely found, or dealing with a particular person. It is not required to specify a term for the qirāḍ; if a term is mentioned and he is prevented from transacting after it, it is corrupted; if he is prevented only from buying after it, then no — in the soundest view. It is required that the two parties be exclusively entitled to the profit and share in it. If he says, "I contract qirāḍ with you on condition that all the profit is yours," it is a corrupt qirāḍ; and it was said: a valid qirāḍ. If he says, "all of it is mine," it is a corrupt qirāḍ; and it was said: it is a deposit (ibḍāʿ). The profit must be known by fraction — if he says, "on condition that you have a share in it" or "a portion," it is corrupted; if he says, "between us," the soundest view is validity, and it is half and half. If he says, "mine is half," it is corrupted in the soundest view; if he says, "yours is half," it is valid on the sound view. If he stipulates for one of them a fixed ten, or the profit of a particular type of goods, it is corrupted.

chapters.arabic_text:
# فصل
# يشترط إيجاب وقبول وقيل: يكفي القبول بالفعل وشرطهما كوكيل وموكل ولو

قارض لعامل آخر بإذن المالك ليشاركه في العمل والربح لم يجز في الأصح وبغير

أذنه فاسد فإن تصرف الثاني فتصرف غاصب فإن اشترى في الذمة وقلنا بالجديد

فالربح للعامل الأول في الأصح وعليه للثاني أجرته وقيل: هو للثاني وإن

اشترى بعين مال القراض فباطل ويجوز أن يقارض الواحد اثنين متفاضلا متساويا

والإثنان واحدا والربح بعد نصيب العامل بينهما بحسب المال وإذا فسد القراض

نفذ تصرف العامل والربح للمالك وعليه للعامل أجرة مثل عمله إلا إذا قال

قارضتك وجميع الربح لي فلا شيء له في الأصح ويتصرف العامل محتاطا لا بغبن

ولا نسيئة بلا إذن وله البيع بعرض وله الرد بعيب تقتضيه مصلحة فإن اقتضت

الإمساك فلا في الأصح وللمالك الرد فإن اختلفا عمل بالمصلحة ولا يعامل

المالك ولا يشتري للقراض بأكثر من رأس المال ولا من يعتق على المالك بغير

إذنه وكذا زوجه في الأصح ولو فعل لم يقع للمالك ويقع للعامل إن اشترى في

الذمة ولا يسافر بالمال بلا إذن ولا ينفق منه على نفسه حضرا وكذا سفرا في

الأظهر وعليه فعل ما يعتاد كطي الثوب ووزن الخفيف كذهب ومسك لا الأمتعة

الثقيل: ة ونحوه وما لا يلزمه له  الاستئجار عليه والأظهر أن العامل يملك

حصته من الربح بالقسمة لا بالظهور وثمار الشجر والنتاج وكسب الرقيق والمهر

الحاصلة من مال القراض يفوز بها المالك وقيل: مال قراض والنقص الحاصل

بالرخص محسوب من الربح ما أمكن ومجبور به وكذا لو تلف بعضه بآفة أو غصب أو

سرقة بعد تصرف العامل في الأصح وإن تلف قبل تصرفه فمن رأس المال في الأصح.
#

# فصل
# لكل فسخه ولو مات أحدهما أو جن أو أغمى عليه انفسخ ويلزم العامل

الاستيفاء إذا فسخ أحدهما وتنضيض رأس المال إن كان عرضا وقيل: لا يلزمه

التنضيض إن لم يكن ربح ولو استرد المالك بعضه قبل ظهور ربح وخسران رجع رأس

المال إلى الباقي وإن استرد بعد الربح فالمسترد شائع ربحا ورأس مال مثاله

رأس المال مائة والربح عشرون واسترد عشرين فالربح سدس المال فيكون المسترد

سدسه من الربح فيستقر للعامل المشروط منه وباقيه من رأس المال وإن استرد

بعد الخسران فالخسران موزع على المسترد والباقي فلا يلزم جبر حصة المسترد

لو ربح بعد ذلك مثاله المال مائة والخسران عشرون ثم استرد عشرين فربع

العشرين حصة المسترد ويعود رأس المال إلى خمسة وسبعين ويصدق العامل بيمينه

في قوله أربح أو لم أربح إلا كذا أو اشتريت هذا للقراض أولى أولم تنهني عن

شراء كذا وفي قدر رأس المال ودعوى التلف وكذا دعوى الرد في الأصح ولو

اختلفا في المشروط له تحالفا وله أجرة المثل.
# 

| كتاب المساقاة
# تصح من جائز التصرف ولصبي ومجنون بالولاية وموردها النخل والعنب وجوزها

القديم في سائر الأشجار المثمرة ولا تصح المخابرة وهي عمل الأرض ببعض ما

يخرج منها والبذر من العامل ولا المزارعة وهي هذه المعاملة والبذر من

المالك فلو كان بين النخل بياض صحت المزارعة عليه مع المساقاة على البخل

بشرط اتحاد العامل وعسر أفراد النخل بالسقي والبياض بالعمارة والأصح انه

يشترط أن لا يفصل بينهما وأن لا يقدم المزارعة وإن كثير البياض كقليله وأنه

لا يشترط تساوي الجزء المشروط من الثمر والزرع  وأنه لا يجوز أن يخابر تبعا

للمساقاة فإن أفردت أرض بالمزارعة فالمغل للمالك وعليه للعامل أجرة عمله

ودوابه وآلاته وطريق جعل الغلة لهما ولا أجرة أن يستأجره بنصف البذر ليزرع

له النصف لآخر ويعيره نصف الأرض أو يستأجره بنصف البذر ونصف منفعة الأرض

ليزرع النصف الآخر في النصف الآخر من الأرض.
#
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ق-ب-ل (qabila)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Acceptance, reception; taking with the hand; opposing rejection (radd).
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In contracts, the second party's consent completing the offer (ījāb); a pillar (rukn) of transactional validity.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal in physical taking; metaphorical (majāz) in contractual assent.
- Sībawayh Rule: Conditional Clause (al-sharṭ wa-l-jawāb) — The particle "wa-law" introduces a hypothetical protasis whose apodosis is governed by the preceding ruling, requiring careful nesting of exceptions.
chapters.translation:
I say: A chapter on the conditions of qirāḍ (mudārabah). Its validity requires an offer and an acceptance; and it was said: acceptance by act suffices. Their conditions are like those of an agent and a principal. And if a mudārib contracts qirāḍ with another worker with the owner's permission, for the latter to share in the work and the profit, it is not permissible in the soundest (al-aṣaḥḥ) view. Without his permission, it is void; if the second party then transacts, he is a usurper (ghāṣib). If he purchases on credit (fī al-dhimmah) and we adopt the new view (al-jadīd), the profit belongs to the first worker in the soundest view, and the second worker is owed his wage. It was said: the profit belongs to the second. If he purchases with the specific capital of the qirāḍ, the purchase is void. It is permissible for one person to contract qirāḍ with two workers, whether with differing or equal shares, and for two to contract with one; the profit, after the worker's share, is divided between them according to the capital. When the qirāḍ becomes void, the worker's transactions are executed, the profit belongs to the owner, and the worker is owed the equivalent wage for his labor — unless he said, "I contract qirāḍ with you on condition that all profit is mine," in which case he receives nothing in the soundest view. The worker must transact cautiously, without gross negligence (ghubn) and without deferred sale (nasī'ah) without permission. He may sell for goods (ʿarḍ), and he may return goods for a defect if the interest (maṣlaḥah) requires it; if interest requires retention, he may not return it in the soundest view, and the owner may return it. If they differ, they act according to what serves the interest. He may not deal with the owner, nor purchase for the qirāḍ more than the capital amount, nor purchase anyone who would be freed upon the owner without his permission; likewise his wife in the soundest view. If he does so, it does not take effect for the owner, but takes effect for the worker if he purchased on credit. He may not travel with the capital without permission, nor spend from it on himself while resident; likewise while traveling in the most apparent (al-aẓhar) view. He is obligated to do what is customary, like folding garments and weighing light items such as gold and musk, but not heavy goods and the like. What is not obligatory upon him, he may hire someone to do. The most apparent view is that the worker owns his share of the profit by division (qismah), not by its mere appearance (ẓuhūr). Fruits of trees, offspring of livestock, earnings of slaves, and dowries (mahr) arising from the qirāḍ capital belong to the owner; it was said: they are qirāḍ capital. A loss occurring due to price depreciation is counted against the profit as much as possible and is compensated thereby; likewise, if part of it perishes by calamity, usurpation, or theft after the worker has transacted, in the soundest view. If it perishes before his transaction, it is from the capital in the soundest view.

I say: A chapter on termination. Each party may rescind it. If either dies, becomes insane, or falls unconscious, it is dissolved. The worker is obligated to complete the collection (istīfā') when either rescinds, and to liquidate the capital (tanḍīḍ) if it is goods; it was said: liquidation is not obligatory if there is no profit. If the owner reclaims part of the capital before profit appears and a loss occurs, the capital reverts to the remainder. If he reclaims after profit, the reclaimed portion is shared proportionally between profit and capital. Example: capital is one hundred, profit twenty; he reclaims twenty — the profit is one-sixth of the total, so the reclaimed portion's sixth is from profit, which becomes fixed for the worker as his contracted share, and the rest is from capital. If he reclaims after a loss, the loss is distributed between the reclaimed portion and the remainder, so the reclaimed portion's share of the loss need not be compensated if profit later accrues. Example: capital one hundred, loss twenty; then he reclaims twenty — one-fourth of the twenty is the reclaimed portion's share, and the capital reverts to seventy-five. The worker is believed under oath regarding his claim of profit or no profit except such-and-such, or "I bought this for the qirāḍ," or "you did not forbid me from buying such," and regarding the amount of capital and claims of perishing; likewise claims of return in the soundest view. If they differ regarding what is stipulated for whom, they both take oaths (taḥāluf), and he is owed the equivalent wage.

| The Book of Musāqāh (Sharecropping of Orchards)

Musāqāh is valid from one who may lawfully dispose of property, and for a child or an insane person through a guardian. Its subject is date palms and grapevines; the old view (al-qadīm) permitted it for all fruit-bearing trees. Mukhābarah is not valid — that is, working the land for a share of its produce with the seed from the worker — nor is muzāraʿah, which is this same transaction but with the seed from the owner. If there is open land (bayāḍ) among the palms, muzāraʿah on that land is valid alongside musāqāh on the palms, on condition that the worker is the same person and that it is difficult to water the palms separately from cultivating the open land. The soundest view is that it is required that the two not be separated, that the muzāraʿah not precede, that abundant open land be like little, that equality between the stipulated share of fruit and of crop is not required, and that mukhābarah is not permissible as a subsidiary to musāqāh. If land is singled out for muzāraʿah, the produce belongs to the owner, and the worker is owed the wage for his labor, his animals, and his tools. The way of making the produce for both is not valid, nor is hiring him with half the seed to sow the other half for another, nor lending him half the land, nor hiring him with half the seed and half the land's usufruct to sow the other half in the other half of the land.

# فصل
# يشترط تخصيص الثمر بهما واشتراكهما فيه والعلم بالنصيبين بالجزئية

كالقراض والأظهر صحة المساقاة بعد ظهور الثمر لكن قبل بدو الصلاح ولو ساقاه

على ودي ليغرسه ويكون الشجر لهما لم يجز ولو كان مغروسا وشرط له جزأ من

الثمر على العمل فإن قدر له مدرة يثمر فيها غالبا صح وإلا فلا وقيل: أن

تعارض الاحتمالان صح وله مساقاة شريكه في الشجر إذا شرط له زيادة على حصته

ويشترط أن لا يشرط على العامل ما ليس من جنس أعمالها وأن ينفرد بالعمل

وباليد في الحديقة ومعرفة العمل بتقدير المدة كسنة أو أكثر ولا يجوز

التوقيت بإدراك الثمر في الأصح وصيغتها ساقيتك على هذا النخل بكذا أو سلمته

إليك لتتعهده ويشترط القبول دون تفصيل الأعمال ويحمل المطلق في كل ناحية

على العرف الغالب وعلى العامل ما يحتاج إليه لصلاح المثمر واستزادته مما

يتكرر كل سنة كسقي وتنقية نهر وإصلاح الإجاجين التي يثبت فيها الماء وتلقيح

وتنحية حشيش وقضبان مضرة وتعريش جرت به عادة وكذا حفظ الثمر وجذاذه وتجفيفه

في الأصح وما قصد به حفظ الأصل ولا يتكرر كل سنة كبناء الحيطان وحفر نهر

جديد فعلى المالك والمساقاة لازمة فلو هرب العامل قبل الفراغ وأتمه المالك

متبرعا بقي استحقاق العامل وإلا استأجر الحاكم عليه من يتمه وإن لم يقدر

على الحاكم فليشهد على الإنفاق إن أراد الرجوع ولو مات وخلف تركه أتم

الوارث العمل منها له أن يتم العمل بنفسه أو بماله ولو ثبتت خيانة عامل ضم

إليه مشرف فإن لم يتحفظ به استؤجر من ماله ولو خرج الثمر مستحقا فللعامل

على المساقي أجره المثل.
# 

| كتاب الإجارة
# شرطها كبائع ومشتر والصيغة آجرتك  هذا أو أكريتك أو ملكتك منافعه سنة بكذا

فيقول قبلت أو استأجرت أو اكتريت والأصح انعقادها بقوله آجرتك منفعتها

ومنعها بقوله بعتك منفعتها وهي قسمان واردة على عين كإجارة العقار ودابة أو

شخص معينين وعلى الذمة كاستئجار دابة موصوفة وبأن يلزم ذمته خياطة أو بناء

ولو قال استأجرتك لتعمل كذا فإجارة عين وقيل: ذمة ويشترط في إجارة الذمة

تسليم الأجرة في المجلس وإجارة العين لا يشترط ذلك فيها ويجوز فيها التعجيل

والتأجيل إن كانت في الذمة وإذا أطلقت تعجلت وإن كانت معينة ملكت في الحال

ويشترط كون الأجرة معلولة فلا تصح بالعمارة والعلف ولا ليسلخ بالجلد ويطحن

ببعض الدقيق أو بالنخالة ولو استأجرها لترضع رقيقا ببعضه في الحال جاز على

الصحيح وكون المنفعة متقومة فلا يصح استئجار بياع على كلمة لا تتعب وإن

روجت السلعة وكذا دراهم ودنانير للتزيين وكلب للصيد في الأصح وكون المؤجر

قادرا على تسليمها فلا يصح استئجار آبق ومغصوب وأعمى للفحظ وأرض للزراعة لا

ماء لها دائم ولا يكفيها المطر المعتاد ويجوز أن كان لها ماء دائم وكذا إن

كفاها
# 
# المطر المعتاد أو ماء الثلوج المجتمعة والغالب حصولها في الأصح والامتناع

الشرعي كالحسي فلا يصح استئجار لقلع سن صحيحة ولا حائض لخدمة مسجد وكذا

منكوحة لرضاع أو غيره بغير إذن الزوج في الأصح ويجوز تأجيل المنفعة في

إجارة الذمة كألزمت ذمتك الحمل إلى مكة أول شهر كذا ولا يجوز إجارة عين

لمنفعة مستقبلة فلو أجر السنة الثانية لمستأجر الأولى قبل انقضائها جاز في

الأصح ويجوز كراء العقب في الأصح وهو أن يؤجر دابة رجلا ليركبها بعض الطريق

أو رجلين ليركب هذا أياما وذا أياما ويبين البعضين ثم يقتسمان.

# فصل
# يشترط كون المنفعة معلومة ثم تارة تقدر بزمان كدار سنة وتارة بعمل كدابة

إلى مكة وكخياطة ذا الثوب فلو جمعهما فاستأجره ليخيطه بياض النهار لم يصح

في الأصح وبقدر تعليم القرآن بمدة أو تعيين سور وفي البناء يبين الموضع

والطول والعرض والسمك وما يبني به إن قدر  بالعمل وإذا صلحت الأرض لبناء

وزراعة وغراس اشترط تعيين المنفعة ويكفي تعيين الزراعة عن ذكر ما يزرع في

الأصح ولو قال لتنتفع بها بما شئت صح وكذا لو قال إن شئت فازرع وإن شئت

فاغرس في الأرض ويشترط في إجارة دابة لركوب معرفة الراكب بمشاهدة أو وصف

تام وقيل: لا يكفي الوصف وكذا الحكم فيما يركب عليه من محمل وغيره إن كان

له ولو شرط حمل المعاليق مطلقا فسد العقد في الأصح وإن لم يشرطه لم يستحق

ويشترط في إجارة العين تعيين الدابة وفي اشتراط رؤيتها الخلاف في بيع

الغائب وفي إجاره الذمة ذكر الجنس والنوع والذكورة أو الأنوثة ويشترط فيهما

بيان قدر
# 
# السير كل يوم إلا أن يكون بالطريق منازل مضبوطة فينزل عليها ويجب في

الإيجار للحمل أن يعرف المحمول فإن حضر رآه وامتحنه بيده إن كان في ظرف وإن

غاب قدر بكيل أو وزن وجنسه لا جنس الدابة وصفتها إن كانت إجارة ذمة إلا أن

يكون المحمول زجاجا ونحوه.
