- Root: ث-م-ر (th-m-r)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Fruit, produce, yield; the tangible outcome of a tree or vine.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): The realized benefit (manfaʿah) that is the object of a commutative contract; its existence is the precondition for validity in mushāqāt.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Used literally (ḥaqīqah) for actual fruit; metaphorically (majāz) for any resultant profit or benefit in contractual language.
- Sībawayh Rule: Conditional Clause (al-Sharṭ) — The particle "لو" (law) introduces hypothetical conditions that negate the consequent, requiring careful parsing of the protasis and apodosis in legal hypotheticals.
chapters.translation:
---

**SECTION 51**

**Chapter: On Mushāqāt (Sharecropping of Fruit-Bearing Trees)**

It is a condition that the fruit be specified to both parties, that they share in it jointly, and that the two shares be known by fraction (bi-al-juzʾiyyah), as in qirāḍ (silent partnership). The soundest view (al-aẓhar) is the validity of mushāqāt after the fruit has appeared but before it reaches ripeness (buduww al-ṣalāḥ). If one contracts mushāqāt on a young shoot (wadī) for the worker to plant it, with the tree becoming jointly owned by both, it is not permissible. If the tree is already planted and the owner stipulates for the worker a portion of the fruit in return for his labor, then if the portion is estimated at an amount that would normally bear fruit, it is valid; otherwise, it is not. It was said: if the two probabilities conflict, it is valid. It is permissible for a man to contract mushāqāt with his partner in the trees if he stipulates for him an increase over his share.

It is a condition that the owner not stipulate upon the worker any task not of the same genus as the work of the trees, and that the worker be exclusively responsible for the labor and for the manual care of the garden. Knowledge of the work is established by estimating the duration, such as one year or more. It is not permissible to fix the term by the ripening of the fruit, according to the soundest view (al-aṣaḥḥ). Its formula (ṣīghah) is: "I give you mushāqāt on this palm grove for such-and-such," or "I have delivered it to you for you to tend it." Acceptance is required, without detailing the specific tasks. The unqualified expression is construed in each matter according to prevailing custom (al-ʿurf al-ghālib). Upon the worker falls whatever is needed for the well-being of the fruit-bearing trees and its increase, including what recurs every year, such as watering, cleaning the irrigation channel, repairing the basins (al-ijājīn) in which water is held, pollination (talqīḥ), removing weeds and harmful branches, and trellising (taʿrīsh) as is customary. Likewise, guarding the fruit, harvesting it (jidhādh), and drying it, according to the soundest view. Whatever is intended for the preservation of the root (aṣl) and does not recur every year—such as building walls or digging a new channel—falls upon the owner.

The mushāqāt contract is binding (lāzimah). If the worker flees before completion and the owner completes the work voluntarily (mutabarriʿan), the worker's entitlement remains. Otherwise, the judge (al-ḥākim) hires someone from the worker's account to complete it. If one cannot reach the judge, let him bear witness to his expenditure if he wishes to seek reimbursement. If the worker dies leaving an estate, the heir completes the work from it; he may complete it himself or with his wealth. If treachery (khiyānah) is established against a worker, a supervisor (mushrif) is appointed over him; if he is not thereby restrained, someone is hired from his wealth. If the fruit turns out to be owned by another (mustaḥaqqan), the worker is entitled to equivalent wages (ajr al-mithl) from the mushāqī (the owner).

---

**Book of Ijārah (Hiring and Leasing)**

Its condition is like that of seller and buyer. Its formula is: "I have hired you this," or "I have leased you this," or "I have transferred to you the usufruct of this for one year for such-and-such," and the other says, "I accept," or "I have hired," or "I have leased." The soundest view is that it is concluded by his saying, "I have hired you its usufruct," and also by his saying, "I have sold you its usufruct." It is of two types: one applies to a specific entity (ʿayn), such as hiring a property, an animal, or a specific person; and one applies to the liability (dhimmah), such as hiring a described animal, or obligating one's liability to perform tailoring or construction. If one says, "I have hired you to do such-and-such," it is a hiring of a specific person (ʿayn); it was said: of the liability (dhimmah).

In hiring against the liability (ijārat al-dhimmah), it is a condition that the wage be delivered in the session (majlis). Hiring of a specific entity does not require this. Deferment or advancement of the wage is permissible if it is against the liability; when left unqualified, it is due immediately. If it is for a specific entity, ownership is established immediately. It is a condition that the wage be known (maʿlūmah); thus it is not valid to pay with building work or fodder, nor to slaughter in exchange for the skin, nor to mill in exchange for some of the flour or the bran. If one hires a woman to nurse a slave in exchange for part of the slave himself, it is valid, according to the correct view (al-ṣaḥīḥ). It is a condition that the usufruct be of monetary value (mutaqawwimah); thus it is not valid to hire a seller for a word that causes no exertion, even if the merchandise is sold thereby. Likewise, dirhams and dinars for adornment, and a dog for hunting, according to the soundest view. It is a condition that the lessor be able to deliver; thus it is not valid to hire a runaway slave (ābiq), a usurped object (maghṣūb), a blind man for guarding, or land for cultivation that has no permanent water and is not sufficiently watered by normal rain. It is valid if it has permanent water, and likewise if normal rain or collected snow-water suffices it, with the prevailing likelihood of its occurrence, according to the soundest view.

Legal impediment (al-imtināʿ al-sharʿī) is like physical impediment. Thus it is not valid to hire someone to extract a healthy tooth, nor a menstruating woman to serve a mosque, nor likewise a married woman for nursing or anything else without her husband's permission, according to the soundest view. It is permissible to defer the usufruct in hiring against the liability, such as saying, "I have obligated your liability to carry to Mecca at the beginning of such-and-such a month." It is not permissible to hire a specific entity for a future usufruct; however, if one leases the second year to the first lessee before the first year has elapsed, it is valid, according to the soundest view. It is permissible to lease "the succession" (kirāʾ al-ʿuqab), according to the soundest view—that is, hiring out an animal to one man to ride part of the road, or to two men, one riding certain days and the other other days, specifying the two portions, and then they divide it.

---

**Chapter: On the Specification of the Usufruct**

It is a condition that the usufruct be known. Sometimes it is estimated by time, such as a house for a year; sometimes by work, such as an animal to Mecca, or tailoring this garment. If one combines both—hiring him to tailor it during the daytime—it is not valid, according to the soundest view. Teaching the Quran is specified either by a duration or by designating the chapters (suwar). In construction, one must specify the location, length, width, thickness, and the material of construction, if it is estimated by work. If land is suitable for building, cultivation, and planting, specifying the usufruct is required; specifying cultivation suffices without mentioning what is to be sown, according to the soundest view. If one says, "Use it as you wish," it is valid. Likewise, if he says, "If you wish, cultivate; if you wish, plant in the land."

In hiring an animal for riding, it is a condition to know the rider by sight or by a complete description. It was said: description is not sufficient. The same applies to what is ridden upon, such as a litter (maḥmil) or otherwise, if it has one. If one stipulates the carrying of hanging loads (maʿālīq) in an unqualified manner, the contract is void, according to the soundest view; if he does not stipulate it, he is not entitled to it. In hiring a specific entity, it is a condition to designate the animal; regarding the stipulation of seeing it, the same disagreement applies as in the sale of an absent object (bayʿ al-ghāʾib). In hiring against the liability, one must mention the genus, type, and whether male or female. In both types, it is a condition to specify the daily distance of travel, unless the route has fixed way-stations (manāzil), in which case one descends according to them.

In hiring for carriage, it is obligatory to know the thing carried. If it is present, he sees it and tests it with his hand if it is in a container. If it is absent, it is specified by measure or weight, and by its genus—not the genus of the animal—and its description, if it is a hiring against the liability, unless the thing carried is glass or the like.

# فصل
# لا تصح إجارة مسلم لجهاد ولا عبادة تجب لها نية إلا الحج وتفرقة زكاة

وتصح لتجهيز ميت ودفنه وتعليم القرآن ولحضانة وإرضاع معا ولأحدهما فقط

والأصح أنه لا يستتبع أحدهما الآخر والحضانة حفظ صبي وتعهده بغسل رأسه

وبدنه وثيابه ودهنه وكحله وربطه في المهد وتحريكه لينام ونحوها ولو استأجر

لهما فانقطع اللبن فالمذهب انفساخ العقد في الإرضاع دون الحضاة والأصح أنه

لا يجب حبر وخيط وكحل على وراق وخياط وكحال.
# قلت: صحح الرافعي في الشرح الرجوع فيه إلى العادة فإن اضطربت وجب البيان

وإلا فتبطل الإجارة. والله أعلم.

# فصل
# يجب تسليم مفتاح الدار إلى المكتري وعمارتها على المؤجر فإن بادر وأصلحها

وإلا فللمكتري الخيار وكسح الثلج عن السطح على المؤجر وتنظيف عرصة الدار عن

ثلج وكناسه على المكتري وإن أجر دابة لركوب فعلى المؤجر الكاف وبرذعة وخرام

وثفر وبرة وخطام وعلى المكتري محمل ومظلة ووطاء وغطاء وتوابعها والأصح في

السرج اتباع العرف وظرف المحمول على المؤجر في إجارة  الذمة وعلى المكتري في

إجارة العين وعلى المؤجر في
# 
# إجارة الذمة الخروج مع الدابة لتعهدها وإعانة الراكب في ركوبه ونزوله

بحسب الحاجة ورفع الحمل وحطه وشد المحمل وحله وليس عليه في إجارة العين إلا

التخلية بين المكتري والدابة وتنفسخ إجارة العين بتلف الدابة ويثبت الخيار

بعيبها ولا خيار في إجارة الذمة بل يلزمه الإبدال والطعام المحمول ليؤكل

يبدل إذا أكل في الأظهر.

# فصل
# يصح عقد الإجارة مدة تبقى فيها العين غالبا وفي قول لا يزاد على سنة وفي

قوله ثلاثين وللمكتري استيفاء المنفعة بنفسه وبغيره فيركب ويسكن مثله ولا

يسكن حدادا ولا قصارا وما يستوفي منه كدار ودابة معينة لا يبدل وما يستوفي

به كثوب وصبي عين للخياطة والإرتضاع يجوز إبداله في الأصح ويد المكتري على

الدابة والثوب يد أمانة مدة الإجارة وكذا بعدها في الأصح ولو ربط دابة

اكتراها لحمل أو ركوب ولم ينتفع بها لم يضمن إلا إذا انهدم عليها اصطبل في

وقت لو انتفع بها لم يصبها الهدم ولو تلف المال في يد أجير بلا تعد كثوب

استؤجر لخياطته أو صبغه لم يضمن إن لم ينفرد باليد بأن قعد المستؤجر معه أو

أحضره منزله وكذا إذا انفرد في أظهر الأقوال والثالث: يضمن المشترك وهو من

التزم عملا في ذمته لا المنفرد وهو من أجر نفسه مدة معينة لعمل ودفع ثوبا

إلى قصار ليقصره أو خياط ليخيطه ففعل ولم يذكر أجرة فلا أجرة له وقيل: له

وقيل: إن كان معروفا بذلك العمل فله وإلا فلا وقد يستحسن ولو تعدى المستأجر

بأن ضرب الدابة وكبحها فوق العادة أو أركبها أثقل منه أو أسكن حدادا أو

قصارا ضمن العين وكذا لو اكترى لحمل مائة رطل من حنطة فحمل مائة شعيرا أو

عكس أو لعشرة أقفزة شعير فحمل حنطة دون عكسه ولو
# 
# اكترى لمائة فحمل مائة وعشرة لزمه أجرة المثل للزيادة وإن تلفت بذلك

ضمنها إن لم يكن صاحبها معها فإن كان ضمن قسطا للزيادة وفي قول نصف القيمة

ولو سلم  المائة والعشرة إلى المؤجر فحملها جاهلا ضمن المكتري على المذهب

ولو وزن المؤجر وحمل فلا أجرة للزيادة ولا ضمان إن تلفت ولو أعطاه ثوبا

ليخيطه فخاطه قباء وقال أمرتني بقطعه قباء فقال بل قميصا فالأظهر تصديق

المالك بيمينه ولا أجرة عليه وعلى الخياط أرش النقص.
chapters.anchors:
- Root: أ-ج-ر (ajara)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Core meaning is recompense or wage for a benefit (manfaʿah) rendered; the contract of hire is a sale of usufruct.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In Kalām, ajr is the countervalue for a service, distinct from thaman (price of a substance); here it denotes the juristic exchange of usufruct for compensation.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal (ḥaqīqah) in commercial transactions; metaphorical (majāz) when applied to divine reward, which is not a true exchange.
- Sībawayh Rule: ʿAṭf al-Bayān (Appositional Coordination) — The phrase "لحضانة وإرضاع معا ولأحدهما فقط" uses wa to coordinate alternatives, requiring precise parsing of the disjunctive (aw) and conjunctive (wa) to distinguish joint versus sole hiring.
chapters.translation:
I say: Know that the hire (ijārah) of a Muslim is not valid for jihād, nor for any act of worship (ʿibādah) that requires intention (niyyah), except for the ḥajj pilgrimage and the distribution of zakāh (alms). It is valid for preparing a deceased person (tajhīz al-mayyit), his burial (dafn), teaching the Qurʾān, and for child custody (ḥiḍānah) and suckling (riḍāʿah) jointly, or for either one of them alone. The more correct position (al-aṣaḥḥ) is that neither one entails the other. Custody (ḥiḍānah) consists of preserving a young child and attending to him by washing his head, his body, and his garments, applying oil to him, applying kohl to his eyes, swaddling him in the cradle, rocking him to sleep, and similar acts. If one hires [a woman] for both [custody and suckling], and then her milk ceases, the madhhab (school) holds that the contract is dissolved (infisākh) with respect to suckling, but not with respect to custody. The more correct position is that ink, thread, and kohl are not obligatory upon the copyist (warraq), the tailor (khayyāṭ), or the kohl-applier (kaḥḥāl) [as part of their hire]. I say: Al-Rāfiʿī corrected in his commentary (al-Sharḥ) that recourse in this matter is to custom (al-ʿādah); if custom is inconsistent, then clarification (bayān) becomes obligatory, and otherwise the hire contract is rendered void. And Allah knows best.

Another Section: The delivery of the house key (miftāḥ al-dār) to the lessee (muktarī) is obligatory, while the maintenance (ʿimārah) of the house is upon the lessor (muʾjir). If the lessor hastens and repairs it, [that suffices]; otherwise, the lessee has the option [to rescind or demand repair]. Clearing snow from the roof is upon the lessor, while cleaning the courtyard (ʿarṣah) of the house of snow and sweeping its refuse is upon the lessee. If one rents an animal for riding, then upon the lessor are the saddle (kāf), the packsaddle (bardhaʿah), the girth (khirām), the crupper (thafar), the nose-ring (burah), and the halter (khitām); and upon the lessee are the howdah (maḥmil), the canopy (miẓallah), the cushion (wiṭāʾ), the covering (ghitāʾ), and their accessories. The more correct position regarding the saddle (saraj) is to follow custom (al-ʿurf). The container (ẓarf) of the transported goods is upon the lessor in a hire of the dhimmah (i.e., a contract for a service obligation in the abstract), and upon the lessee in a hire of a specific object (al-ʿayn). Upon the lessor in a hire of the dhimmah is the obligation to go out with the animal to attend to it, to assist the rider in mounting and dismounting according to need, to lift the load and set it down, and to fasten and unfasten the howdah. In a hire of a specific object, he is not obligated except to vacate [the animal] for the lessee (takhliyah). The hire of a specific object is dissolved by the perishing (talaf) of the animal, and the option [to rescind] is established due to its defect (ʿayb). There is no option in a hire of the dhimmah; rather, he is obligated to provide a substitute (ibdāl). Food that is transported for consumption is substituted if it is eaten, according to the more apparent position (al-aẓhar).

Another Section: The contract of hire is valid for a duration in which the object [of hire] typically remains [sound]. In one saying, it may not exceed one year; in another saying, thirty [years]. The lessee has the right to exact the usufruct (manfaʿah) personally or through another, so he may ride [the animal] or dwell [in the house] with someone like himself, but he may not house a blacksmith (ḥaddād) or a fuller (qaṣṣār) [in a rented dwelling]. What is exacted from [the object], such as a specific house or animal, may not be substituted; but what is exacted by means of [the object], such as a garment or a child designated for sewing or suckling, may be substituted, according to the more correct position. The lessee's hand over the animal and the garment is a hand of trust (yad amānah) during the term of the hire, and likewise after it, according to the more correct position. If one ties up an animal he has rented for carrying or riding and does not use it, he is not liable [for its perishing], except if a stable collapses upon it at a time when, had he used it, the collapse would not have struck it. If property perishes in the hand of a hired worker (ajīr) without transgression (taʿaddī), such as a garment hired for sewing or dyeing, he is not liable if he was not exclusively in possession (infirād bi-al-yad), i.e., if the hirer sat with him or brought it to his own home. Likewise, he is not liable even if he was exclusively in possession, according to the more apparent of the opinions. The third opinion: the common worker (ajīr mushtarak)—who is one who undertakes a task in his dhimmah—is liable, but not the exclusive worker (munfarid), who is one who hires himself for a specified period for a task. If one gives a garment to a fuller (qaṣṣār) to full it, or to a tailor to sew it, and he does so without mentioning a wage, then he has no wage. It is said: he has one. And it is said: if he is well-known for that work, he has one; otherwise, not. And this may be deemed commendable (istaḥsāna). If the lessee transgresses by striking the animal or reining it in beyond the customary limit, or by mounting upon it someone heavier than himself, or by housing a blacksmith or fuller [in the rented dwelling], he is liable for the object itself (ḍamān al-ʿayn). Likewise, if he rents [an animal] to carry one hundred raṭls of wheat and carries one hundred of barley, or the reverse, or [rents it] for ten aqfizah (measures) of barley and carries wheat—but not the reverse [i.e., renting for wheat and carrying barley is not transgression]. If he rents for one hundred and carries one hundred and ten, he owes the equivalent wage (ujrat al-mithl) for the excess; and if it perishes thereby, he is liable for it, unless its owner was present with it. If the owner was present, he is liable for a proportional share of the excess; and in one saying, half the value. If he delivered the one hundred and ten to the lessor, and the lessor carried it unknowingly, then the lessee is liable, according to the madhhab. If the lessor weighed and carried [it himself], then there is no wage for the excess and no liability if it perishes. If one gives a garment to a tailor to sew it, and he sews it as a jubba (long coat) and says, "You ordered me to cut it as a jubba," but the owner says, "Rather, as a qamīṣ (shirt)," then the more apparent position is that the owner is believed upon his oath, and no wage is due to the tailor; rather, upon the tailor is the compensation for the diminution (arsh al-nuqṣān).

chapters.title_en: Section 53 — On the Non-Dissolution of Hire Contracts Due to Excuses, and the Revival of Dead Lands (Iḥyāʾ al-Mawāt)
chapters.arabic_text:
# فصل
# لا تنفسخ الأجرة بعذر كتعذر وقود حمام وسفر ومرض مستأجر دابة لسفر ولو

استأجر أرضا لزراعة فزرع فهلك الزرع بجائحة فليس له الفسخ ولا حط شيء من

الأجرة وتنفسخ بموت الدابة والأجيبر المعينين في المستقبل لا الماضي في

الأظهر فيستقر قسطه من المسمى ولا تنفسخ بموت العاقدين ومتولي الوقف ولو

أجر البطن الأول مدة ومات قبل تمامها أو الولي صبيا مدة لا يبلغ فيها بالسن

فبلغ بالاحتلام فالأصح انفساخها في الوقف لا الصبي وإنها تنفسخ بانهدام

الدار لا انقطاع ماء أرض استؤجرت لزراعة بل يثبت الخيار وغصب الدابة وإباق

العبد تثبت الخيار ولو أكرى جمالا وهرب وتركها عند المكتري راجع القاضي

ليمونها من مال الجمال فإن لم يجد له مالا اقترض عليه فإن وثق بالمكتري

دفعه إليه وإلا جعله عند ثقة وله أن يبيع منها قدر النفقة ولو أذن للمكتري

في الإنفاق من ماله ليرجع جاز في الأظهر ومتى قبض المكتري الدابة أو الدار

وأمسكها حتى مضت مدة إجارة استقرت الأجرة وإن لم ينتفع وكذا لو اكترى لركوب

إلى موضع وقبضها ومضت مدة إمكان السير
# 
# إليه وسواء فيه إجارة العين والذمة إذا سلم الدابة الموصوفة وتستقر في

الإجارة الفاسدة أجرة المثل بما يستقر به المسمى في الصحيفة ولو أكرى عينا

مدة ولم يسلمها حتى مضت انفسخت ولو لم يقدر مدة وأجر لركوب إلى موضع ولم

يسلما حتى مضت مدة السير فالأصح أنها لا تنفسخ ولو أجر عبده ثم أعتقه

فالأصح أنها لا تنفسخ الإجارة وأنه لا خيار للعبد والأظهر أنه لا يرجع على

سيده بأجرة ما بعد العتق ويصح بيع المستأجرة للمكتري ولا تنفسخ الإجارة في

الأصح ولو باعها لغيره جاز في الأظهر ولا  تنفسخ.
# 

| كتاب إحياء الموات
# الأرض التي لا تعمر قط إن كانت ببلاد الإسلام فللمسلم تملكها بالأحياء

وليس هو لذمي وإن كانت ببلاد كفار فلهم إحياؤها وكذا لمسلم إن كانت مما لا

يذبون المسلمين عنها وما كان معمورا فلمالكه إن لم يعرف والعمارة إسلامية

فمال ضائع وإن كانت جاهلية فالأظهر أنه يملك بالأحياء ولا يملك بالأحياء

حريم معمور وهو ما تمس الحاجة إليه لتمام الانتفاع فحريم القرية النادي

ومرتكض الخيل ومناخ الإبل ومطرح الرماد ونحوها وحريم البئر في الموات موقف

النازح والحوض والدولاب ومجتمع الماء ومتردد الدابة وحريم الدار في الموات

مطرح رماد وكناسة وثلج وممر في صوب الباب وحريم آبار القناة ما لو حفر فيه

نقص ماؤها أو خيف الانهيار والدار المحفوفة بدور لا حريم لها ويتصرف كل

واحد في ملكه على العادة فإن تعدى ضمن والأصح أنه يجوز أن يتخذ داره

المحفوفة بمساكن حماما واصطبلا وحانوته في البزازين حانوت حداد إذا احتاط

واحكم الجدران ويجوز إحياء موات الحرم دون عرفات في الأصح.
# قلت: ومزدلفة ومنى كعرفة والله أعلم ويختلف الأحياء بحسب الغرض فإن أراد

مسكنا اشترط تحويط البقعة وسقف بعضها وتعليق باب وفي الباب وجه أو زريبة

دواب
# 
# فتحويط لا سقف وفي الباب الخلاف أو مزرعة فجمع التراب حولها وتسوية الأرض

وترتيب ماء لها إن لم يكفها المطر المعتاد لزراعة في الأصح أو بستانا فجمع

التراب والتحويط حيث جرت العادة به وتهيئة ماء ويشترط الغرس على المذهب ومن

شرع في عمل إحياء ولم يتمه أو أعلم على بقعة لنصب أحجار أو غرز خشبا فمتحجر

وهو أحق به لكن الأصح أنه لا يصح بيعه وأنه لو أحياه آخر ملكه ولو طالت مدة

التحجر قال له السلطان أحي أو أترك فإن استمهل أمهل مدة قريبة ولو أقطعه

الإمام مواتا صار أحق بإحيائه كالمتحجر ولا يقطع إلا قادرا على الإحياء

وقدرا يقدر عليه وكذا التحجر والأظهر أن للإمام أن يحمي بقعة موات لرعي نعم

جزية وصدقة وضالة وضعيف عن النجعة وإن له  نقض حماه للحاجة ولا يحمي لنفسه.

# فصل
# منفعة الشارع المرور ويجوز الجلوس به لاستراحة ومعاملة نحوهما إذا لم

يضيق على المارة ولا يشترط إذن الإمام وله تظليل مقعده ببارية وغيرها ولو

سبق إليه اثنان أقرع وقيل: يقدم لإمام برأيه ولو جلس فيه للمعالمة ثم فارقه

تاركا للحرفة أو منتقلا إلى غيره بطل حقه وإن فارقه ليعود لم يبطل إلا أن

تطول مفارقته بحيث ينقطع معاملوه عنه ويألفون غيره ومن ألف من المسجد موضعا

يفتي فيه ويقرئ كالجالس في شارع المعاملة ولو جلس فيه الصلاة لم يصر أحق به

في غيرها فلو فارقه لحاجة ليعود لم يبطل اختصاصه في تلك الصلاة في الأصح

وإن لم يترك إزاره ولو سبق رجل إلى موضع من رباط مسبل أو فقيه إلى مدرسة أو

صوفي إلى خانقاه لم يزعج ولم يبطل حقه بخروجه لشراء حاجة ونحوه.
#
chapters.anchors:
- Root: أ-ج-ر (a-j-r)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Recompense, wage, or hire; the exchange of usufruct for a known payment.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In contractual theology, the wage (ujrah) is a determined countervalue (ʿiwad) for a defined benefit (manfaʿah), binding by mutual consent.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal in financial transactions; metaphorical when applied to divine reward (ajr) — here strictly literal.
- Sībawayh Rule: Conditional Clause with Implied Apodosis (al-sharṭ wa-l-jawāb bi-l-taqdīr) — The phrase "لو استأجر..." (if one hires...) sets a protasis whose apodosis is governed by the preceding ruling, requiring careful parsing of the legal consequence.
chapters.translation:
I say: The hire contract (ijārah) is not dissolved by an excuse, such as the failure of a bathhouse's fuel supply, or the interruption of travel, or the illness of the one who hires a beast for a journey. And if one hires land for cultivation, and sows it, and the crop perishes by a calamity (jāʾiḥah), he has no right of dissolution, nor any reduction of the hire. But the contract is dissolved by the death of the specific beast (al-dābbah) or the specific hired laborer (al-ajīr al-muʿayyan) with respect to the future period, not the past, in the most apparent (al-aẓhar) opinion; thus the apportioned share of the named hire for the elapsed time is established. It is not dissolved by the death of the two contracting parties, nor by the death of the administrator of a waqf (mutawallī al-waqf). And if the first class (al-baṭn al-awwal) of a waqf leases [the property] for a term, and dies before its completion, or a guardian leases [the property of] a minor for a term during which the minor would not reach puberty by age, but he reaches puberty by nocturnal emission (iḥtilām), then the soundest (al-aṣaḥḥ) opinion is that the contract is dissolved in the case of the waqf, but not in the case of the minor. And it is dissolved by the collapse of the house, but not by the cutting off of water from land hired for cultivation; rather, the option (khiyār) is established. And the usurpation (ghaṣb) of the beast, or the running away (ibāq) of the slave, establishes the option [of rescission]. And if one lets out camels (jammāl) and flees, leaving them with the hirer, the judge (al-qāḍī) is to return to sell them from the camel-owner's wealth. If he finds no wealth for him, he may borrow on his behalf. If he trusts the hirer, he gives them to him; otherwise, he places them with a trustworthy person. And he may sell from them an amount sufficient for their upkeep (nafaqah). And if he permits the hirer to spend from his own wealth with the right of recourse, that is permissible in the most apparent opinion. And whenever the hirer takes possession of the beast or the house, and retains it until the term of the hire has elapsed, the hire is established, even if he derived no benefit. Likewise, if one hires [a beast] for riding to a place, and takes possession of it, and the period sufficient for the journey elapses. This applies equally to the hire of a specific entity (ijārat al-ʿayn) and to a hire on liability (ijārat al-dhimmah), when the described beast is delivered. And in a corrupt hire (ijārah fāsidah), the equivalent hire (ujrat al-mithl) is established by whatever establishes the named hire in a valid contract. And if one leases a specific entity for a term, and does not deliver it until the term elapses, the contract is dissolved. But if no term was specified, and he hired [a beast] for riding to a place, and neither was delivered until the period of the journey elapsed, the soundest opinion is that it is not dissolved. And if one hires out his slave, then emancipates him, the soundest opinion is that the hire is not dissolved, and that the slave has no option. And the most apparent opinion is that the slave does not have recourse against his master for the hire of the period after emancipation. And it is valid for the hirer to purchase the hired property for himself, and the hire is not dissolved in the soundest opinion. And if he sells it to another, that is permissible in the most apparent opinion, and it is not dissolved.

[Book of Reviving Dead Lands (Kitāb Iḥyāʾ al-Mawāt)]

Land that has never been cultivated: if it lies in the lands of Islam, a Muslim may own it by reviving it (iḥyāʾ), and this is not [permissible] for a dhimmī. If it lies in the lands of the unbelievers, they may revive it, and likewise a Muslim may do so if it is land from which they do not defend the Muslims. And whatever land is cultivated belongs to its owner, if known. And if the cultivation is Islamic [in origin], and the owner is unknown, it is lost property (māl ḍāʾiʿ). If it is from the pre-Islamic era (jāhilī), the most apparent opinion is that it is owned by revival. And the protected precinct (ḥarīm) of cultivated land is not owned by revival — that is, what is needed for the completion of benefit. Thus, the ḥarīm of a village includes its meeting place (al-nādī), the tethering ground for horses, the resting place for camels, the ash dump, and the like. The ḥarīm of a well in dead land includes the standing place of the water-drawer, the trough, the water-wheel, the gathering place of water, and the turning area of the beast. The ḥarīm of a house in dead land includes its ash dump, refuse area, snow pit, and a passage in the direction of its door. The ḥarīm of the wells of an underground water channel (qanāt) is such that if one dug there, its water would diminish or its collapse would be feared. A house surrounded by other houses has no ḥarīm. And each person disposes of his property according to custom (al-ʿādah); if he transgresses, he is liable. And the soundest opinion is that it is permissible for one to make his house, surrounded by dwellings, into a bathhouse, a stable, or — for a cloth merchant (bazzāz) — a blacksmith's shop, if he takes precautions and strengthens the walls. And it is permissible to revive dead land within the Sacred Precinct (al-ḥaram), but not within ʿArafāt, in the soundest opinion.

I say: And Muzdalifah and Minā are like ʿArafah [in this regard], and God knows best. And revival varies according to the purpose. If one intends a dwelling, it is required to enclose the plot with walls, roof part of it, and hang a door; and regarding the door, there is a view [that it must be fixed] or [merely] a pen for beasts. If one intends a pen for beasts, enclosure without roofing suffices, and regarding the door there is the aforementioned difference of opinion. If one intends a farm, he must gather soil around it, level the ground, and arrange water for it, if the customary rain is insufficient for cultivation, in the soundest opinion. If one intends an orchard, he must gather soil and enclose it where custom so requires, and prepare water; and planting (ghars) is required on the [established] school (al-madhhab). And whoever begins an act of revival but does not complete it, or marks a plot by placing stones or planting wood, is a squatter (muḥajjir), and he has priority right to it. But the soundest opinion is that its sale is not valid, and that if another revives it, he owns it. And if the period of squatting (taḥajjur) is prolonged, the sultan says to him: "Revive or abandon." If he requests a delay, he is granted a short period. And if the Imām grants him dead land (iqṭāʿ), he becomes more entitled to revive it, like a squatter. And he may not grant [land] except to one capable of revival, and [only] an amount he can manage; likewise for squatting. And the most apparent opinion is that the Imām may reserve a plot of dead land for the grazing of cattle of jizyah, ṣadaqah, stray animals, and the weak who cannot journey far for pasture; and he may revoke his reservation when needed, but he may not reserve for himself.

[Section]

The benefit of the public thoroughfare (al-shāriʿ) is passage. It is permissible to sit therein for rest or for trade and the like, if one does not cause constriction to passersby, and the Imām's permission is not required. And one may shade his sitting place with a reed mat (bāriyah) or the like. And if two precede to the same spot, lots are cast. It was said: the Imām may give precedence by his own judgment. And if one sits therein for trade, then leaves it, abandoning the craft or moving to another [place], his right is void. If he leaves intending to return, it is not void, unless his absence is prolonged such that his customers break away from him and become accustomed to another. And whoever habituates a place in the mosque for giving legal opinions (fatwā) or teaching the Quran is like one sitting in the thoroughfare for trade. And if one sits therein for prayer, he does not acquire priority right over it for other purposes. Thus, if he leaves it for a need intending to return, his special claim to that prayer is not void in the soundest opinion, even if he does not leave his garment. And if a man precedes to a place in a dedicated hospice (ribāṭ), or a jurist to a school (madrasah), or a Sufi to a convent (khānqāh), he is not to be displaced, and his right is not void by his leaving to purchase a need or the like.

# فصل
# المعدن الظاهر وهو ما خرج بلا علاج كنفط وكبريت وقار وموميا وبرام وأحجار

رحى لا يملك بإحياء ولا يثبت فيه اختصاص بتحجر ولا اقطاع فإن ضاق نيله قدم

السابق بقدر حاجته فإن طلب زيادة فالأصح إزعاجه ولو جاءآ معا أقرع في الأصح

والمعدن الباطن وهو ما لا يخرج إلا بعلاج كذهب وفضة وحديد ونحاس لا يملك

بالحفر والعمل في الأظهر ومن أحيا مواتا فظهر فيه معدن باطن ملكه والمياه

المباحة من الأودية والعيون في الجبال يستوي الناس فيها فإن أراد قوم سقي

أراضيهم منها فضاق سقي الأعلى فالأعلى وحبس كل واحد الماء حتى يبلغ الكعبين

فإن كان في الأرض ارتفاع وانخفاض أفرد كل طرف بسقي وما أخذ من هذا الماء في

إناء ملك على الصحيح وحافر بئر بموات للارتفاق أولى بمائها حتى يرتحل

والمحفورة للتملك أو في ملك يملك ماؤها في الأصح وسواء ملكه أم لا لا يلزمه

بذل ما فضل عن حاجته لزرع ويجب لماشية على الصحيح والقناة المشتركة يقسم

ماؤها بنصب خشبة في عرض النهر فيها ثقب متساوية أو متفاوتة على قدر الحصص

ولهم القسمة مهايأة. 
# 

| كتاب الوقف
# شرط الوقف صحة عبارته وأهلية للتبرع والموقوف دوام الانتفاع به لا مطعوم

وريحان ويصح وقف عقار ومنقول ومشاع لا عبد وثوب في الذمة ولا وقف حر نفسه

وكذا مستولدة وكلب معلم وأحد عبديه في الأصح ولو وقف بناء أو غراسا في أرض

مستأجرة لهما فالأصح جوازه فإن وقف على معين واحد أو جمع اشترط إمكان

تمليكه فلا يصح على جنين ولا على العبد لنفسه فلو أطلق لوقف عليه فهو وقف

على سيده ولو أطلق الوقف على بهيمة لغا وقيل: هو وقف على مالكها ويصح على

ذمي لا مرتد وحربي ونفسه في الأصح وإن وقف على جهة معصية كعمارة الكنائس

فباطل أو جهة قربة كالفقراء والعلماء والمساجد والمدارس صح أو جهة لا تظهر

فيها القرية كالأغنياء صح في الأصح ولا يصح إلا بلفظ وصريحه وقفت كذا أو

أرضى هو موقوفة عليه والتسبيل والتحبيس صريحان على الصحيح ولو قال تصدقت

بكذا صدقة محرمة أو موقوفة أو لا تباع أولا توهب فصريح في الأصح وقوله

تصدقت فقط ليس بصريح وإن نوى إلا أن يضيف إلى جهة عامة وينوي والأصح أن

قوله حرمته أو أبدته ليس بصريح وأن قوله جعلت البقعة مسجدا تصير به مسجدا

وأن الوقف على معين يشترط فيه قبوله ولو رد بطل حقه شرطنا القبول أم لا؟

ولو قال: وقفت
# 
# هذا سنة فباطل ولو قال: وقفت على أولادي أو على زيد ثم نسله ولم يزد

فالأظهر صحة الوقف فإذا انقرض المذكور فالأظهر أنه يبقى وقفا وأن مصرفه

أقرب الناس إلى الواقف يوم انقراض الذكور ولو كان الوقف منقطع الأول كوقفته

على من سيولد لي فالمذهب بطلانه أو منقطع الوسط كوقفت على أولادي ثم رجل ثم

الفقراء فالمذهب صحته ولو اقتصر على وقفت فالأظهر بطلانه ولا يجوز تعليقه

كقوله إذا جاء زيد فقد وقفت ولو وقف بشرط الخيار بطل على الصحيح والأصح أنه

إذا وقف بشرط أن لا يؤجر اتبع شرطه وأنه إذا شرط في وقف المسجد اختصاصه

لطائفة كالشافعية  اختص كالمدرسة والرباط ولو وقف على شخصين ثم الفقراء فمات

أحدهما فالأصح المنصوص أن نصيبه يصرف إلى الآخر.

# فصل
# قوله: وقفت على أولادي وأولاد أولادي يقتضي التسوية بين الكل وكذا لو زاد

ما تناسلوا أو بطنا بعد بطن ولو قال على أولادي ثم أولاد أولادي ثم أولادهم

ما تناسلوا أو على أولادي وأولاد أولادي الأعلى فالأعلى أو الأول فالأول

فهو للترتيب ولا يدخل أولاد الأولاد في الوقف على الأولاد في الأصح ويدخل

أولاد البنات في الوقف على الذرية والنسل والعقب وأولاد الأولاد إلا أن

يقول على من ينتسب إلي منهم ولو وقف على مواليه وله معتق ومعتق قسم بينهما

وقيل: يبطل والصفة المتقدمة على جمل معطوفة تعتبر في الكل كوقفت على محتاجي

أولادي وأحفادي وإخوتي وكذا المتأخرة عليها والاستثناء إذا عطف بواو كقوله

على أولادي وأحفادي وإخوتي المحتاجين أو إلا أن يفسق بعضهم.
#

# فصل
# الأظهر أن الملك في رقبة الموقوف ينتقل إلى الله تعالى أي ينفك عن اختصاص

لآدمي فلا يكون للواقف ولا للموقوف عليه ومنافعه ملك للموقوف عليه يستوفيها

بنفسه وبغيره بإعارة وإجارة ويملك الأجرة وفوائده كثمرة وصوف ولبين وكذا

الولد في الأصح والثاني يكون وقفا ولو ماتت البهيمة اختص بجلدها وله مهر

الجارية إذا وطئت بشبهة أو نكاح إن صححناه وهو الأصح والمذهب أنه لا يملك

قيمة العبد الموقوف إذا أتلف بل يشتري بها عبدا ليكون وقفا مكانه فإن تعذر

فبعض عبد ولو جفت الشجرة لم ينقطع الوقف على المذهب بل ينتفع بها جذعا

وقيل: تباع والثمن كقيمة العبد والأصح جواز بيع حصر المسجد إذا بليت وجذوعه

إذا انكسرت ولم تصلح إلا للإحراق ولو انهدم مسجد وتعذرت إعادته لم يبع

بحال.

- Root: ع-ل-ج (ʿalaja)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To treat, to work upon, to refine; implies exertion and processing.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In legal context, distinguishes natural emergence (ẓuhūr) from human intervention (muʿālajah) in acquisition.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal for physical labor; metaphorical for legal causation in property rights.
- Root: و-ق-ف (waqafa)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To stop, to detain, to immobilize; core sense of withholding from circulation.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Technical term for endowment—perpetual detention of corpus (raqabah) with release of usufruct (manfaʿah) for beneficiaries.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal standing/stopping; metaphorical for legal perpetuity and inalienability.
- Root: ح-ب-س (ḥabasa)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To confine, to restrain; synonym of waqf in prophetic usage.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Emphasizes the act of withholding property from sale, inheritance, and gift.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal imprisonment; metaphorical for legal restriction of disposal.
- Root: ق-س-م (qasama)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To divide, to apportion; distributive justice in shares.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Legal division of common rights, especially water and endowed property.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal partitioning; metaphorical for equitable allocation of usufruct.
- Sībawayh Rule: Conditional and Exceptive Syntax (al-Sharṭ wa al-Istithnāʾ) — Governing clauses with "if" (law/in) and "except" (illā), including suspended validity (taʿlīq) and sequential priority (al-aʿlā fa-al-aʿlā).
chapters.translation:
**Chapter: On Mines**

Know that the apparent mine (al-maʿdin al-ẓāhir) is that which emerges without treatment (bi-lā ʿilāj), such as naphtha, sulfur, bitumen, mummy, alum, and stones of millstones. It is not owned by reviving (iḥyāʾ) the land, nor is exclusive right established therein by staking claims (taḥajjur) or by grant from the ruler (iqṭāʿ). If access to it becomes constrained, the one who arrives first takes precedence to the extent of his need. If he seeks an increase beyond that, the soundest opinion (al-aṣaḥḥ) is that he is to be removed. If two arrive simultaneously, lots are cast, in the soundest opinion.

The hidden mine (al-maʿdin al-bāṭin) is that which does not emerge except through treatment, such as gold, silver, iron, and copper. It is not owned by digging and labor, in the most apparent opinion (al-aẓhar). Whoever revives dead land (mawāt) and a hidden mine appears therein, he owns it. The permissible waters from valleys and springs in the mountains are shared equally among all people. If a group desires to irrigate their lands therefrom and the water becomes constrained, then the higher land is irrigated first, then the next higher, and so on. Each person holds the water until it reaches the ankles (al-kaʿbayn). If the land has elevation and depression, each side is given its own irrigation turn. What is taken of this water into a vessel is owned, on the sound opinion. The digger of a well in dead land for mere convenience (irtifāq) has priority to its water until he departs. But a well dug for ownership, or dug within one's own property, its water is owned, in the soundest opinion. Whether he owns it or not, he is not obliged to give what exceeds his need for crops, but he is obliged to give for livestock, on the sound opinion.

A shared canal (al-qanāh al-mushtarakah): its water is divided by placing a wooden beam across the width of the river containing holes, either equal or varying according to the shares. They may divide it by time-allotment (muhāyāʾah).

**Book of Endowments (Kitāb al-Waqf)**

The condition of a valid endowment (waqf) is the soundness of the declarant's expression, his legal capacity for gratuitous donation (ahliyyat al-tabarruʿ), and that the endowed object is of perpetual usufruct—not food or basil. It is valid to endow real property (ʿaqār), movable property (manqūl), and undivided shares (mushāʿ). It is not valid to endow a slave or a garment owed as a debt in one's liability (thawb fī al-dhimmah), nor to endow a free person himself, nor likewise a umm walad (slave-mother of his child), nor a trained dog, nor one of two slaves, in the soundest opinion. If one endows a building or plantation on leased land, for both the building and the land, the soundest opinion is its permissibility.

If one endows upon a specific individual or a group, it is a condition that legal transfer of ownership to them be possible. Thus, it is not valid upon a fetus (janīn), nor upon a slave for himself—if he makes an absolute endowment, it is an endowment upon his master. If one makes an absolute endowment upon an animal, it is void; and it is said: it is an endowment upon its owner. It is valid upon a dhimmī (protected non-Muslim), but not upon an apostate (murtadd), nor upon a harbī (enemy combatant), nor upon oneself, in the soundest opinion.

If one endows for a purpose of disobedience (maʿṣiyah), such as building churches, it is void. If for a purpose of nearness to God (qurbah), such as the poor, scholars, mosques, and schools, it is valid. If for a purpose in which nearness is not apparent, such as the wealthy, it is valid in the soundest opinion.

It is not valid except by explicit wording (lafẓ). Its explicit forms are: "I have endowed (waqaftu) such-and-such," or "my land is endowed upon him." The terms "tasbīl" (dedicating in God's path) and "taḥbīs" (confining) are both explicit, on the sound opinion. If he says, "I have given in charity (taṣaddaqtu) such-and-such, a forbidden charity (ṣadaqah muḥarramah)," or "endowed," or "not to be sold," or "not to be gifted," it is explicit in the soundest opinion. His mere saying "I have given in charity" without more is not explicit, even if he intended it, unless he adds it to a general purpose and intends it. The soundest opinion is that his saying "I have made it forbidden (ḥarramtuhā)" or "I have made it eternal (abbadtuhā)" is not explicit. And that his saying "I have made this place a mosque" makes it a mosque thereby.

An endowment upon a specific person requires his acceptance. If he rejects it, his right is void, whether we stipulate acceptance or not. If he says, "I have endowed... this year," it is void. If he says, "I have endowed upon my children," or "upon Zayd, then his descendants," and adds nothing more, the most apparent opinion is the validity of the endowment. When the mentioned persons become extinct, the most apparent opinion is that it remains an endowment, and its expenditure is directed to the closest relatives of the endower on the day of extinction of the males.

If the endowment is severed at its beginning (munqaṭiʿ al-awwal), such as "I have endowed upon whoever will be born to me," the school (madhhab) holds its invalidity. If severed in the middle (munqaṭiʿ al-wasaṭ), such as "I have endowed upon my children, then upon a man, then upon the poor," the school holds its validity. If he merely says "I have endowed" without specifying, the most apparent opinion is its invalidity. It is not permissible to suspend it (taʿlīq), such as saying, "When Zayd comes, I have endowed." If he endows with a condition of option (khiyār), it is void, on the sound opinion.

The soundest opinion is that if he endows with the condition that it not be leased, his condition is followed. And that if he stipulates in a mosque endowment its exclusivity to a particular group, such as the Shāfiʿīs, it becomes exclusive to them, like a school (madrasah) or a hospice (ribāṭ). If he endows upon two persons, then upon the poor, and one of them dies, the soundest opinion, as stated in the text (al-manṣūṣ), is that his share is given to the other.

**Chapter: On Beneficiaries and Their Order**

His saying: "I have endowed upon my children and my children's children" entails equality among all. Likewise, if he adds "and their descendants" or "generation after generation." If he says, "upon my children, then my children's children, then their children, and their descendants," or "upon my children and my children's children, the higher then the higher," or "the first then the first," it is for order (tartīb). The children's children do not enter into an endowment upon "children" alone, in the soundest opinion. The children of daughters do enter into an endowment upon "offspring" (dhurriyyah), "progeny" (nasl), "descendants" (ʿaqib), and "children's children," unless he says "upon whoever descends from me among them."

If he endows upon his clients (mawālī) and he has both a freed slave (muʿtiq) and a patron (muʿtaq), it is divided between them. And it is said: it is void. A qualifying adjective (al-ṣifah) preceding a conjoined series of nouns applies to all, as in "I have endowed upon the needy among my children, my grandchildren, and my brothers." Likewise, an adjective following them applies to all. An exception (istithnāʾ) when conjoined with "and" (wāw), such as "upon my children, my grandchildren, and my brothers, the needy among them," or "unless some of them commit sin," applies to all.

**Chapter: On the Nature of Ownership in Endowment**

The most apparent opinion is that ownership of the corpus (raqabah) of the endowed property transfers to God Almighty—that is, it is released from any exclusive claim of any human being. Thus, it is neither for the endower nor for the beneficiary. Its usufructs (manāfiʿ) are owned by the beneficiary, who may utilize them personally or through others, by lending (iʿārah) or leasing (ijārah). He owns the rent, and its incidental benefits (fawāʾid), such as fruit, wool, and milk. Likewise, the offspring [of an endowed animal] is owned by him, in the soundest opinion; the second opinion is that it becomes an endowment itself. If the animal dies, he is entitled to its skin. He is entitled to the dower (mahr) of an endowed slave-girl if she is intercourse with under a mistaken contract (shubhah) or a valid marriage, if we uphold that—and it is the soundest opinion.

The school (madhhab) holds that he does not own the value of an endowed slave if the slave is destroyed [by a tortfeasor]; rather, a slave is purchased with it to be an endowment in his place. If that is not possible, then a portion of a slave. If an endowed tree dries up, the endowment does not cease, on the school's opinion; rather, one benefits from it as timber. And it is said: it is sold, and its price is like the value of the slave [i.e., used to replace it]. The soundest opinion is the permissibility of selling a mosque's worn-out mats and its broken beams that are fit only for burning. If a mosque collapses and its restoration becomes impossible, it is not sold under any circumstances.

chapters.arabic_text:
# فصل
# إن شرط الواقف النظر لنفسه أو غيره اتبع وإلا فالنظر للقاضي على المذهب

وشرط الناظر العدالة والكفاية والاهتداء إلى التصرف ووظيفته العمارة

والإجارة وتحصيل الغلة وقسمتها فإن فوض إليه بعض هذه الأمور لم يتعده

وللواقف عزل من ولاه ونصب غيره إلا أن يشترط نظره حال الوقف  وإذا أجر

الناظر فزادت الأجرة في المدة أو ظهر طالب بالزيادة لم ينفسخ العقد في

الأصح.
# 

| كتاب الهبة
# التمليك بلا عوض هبة فإن ملك محتاجا لثواب الآخرة فصدقة فإن نقله إلى

مكان الموهوب له إكراما له فهدية وشرط الهبة إيجاب وقبول لفظا ولا يشترطان

في الهدية على الصحيح بل يكفي البعث من هذا والقبض من ذاك ولو قال أعمرتك

هذه الدار فإذا مت فهي لورثتك فهي هبة ولو اقتصر على أعمرتك فكذا في الجديد

ولو قال فإذا مت عادت إلي فكذا في الأصح ولو قال أرقبتك أو جعلتها لك رقبي

أي إن مت قبلي عادت إلي وإن مت قبلك استقرت لك فالمذهب طرد القولين الجديد

والقديم وما جاز بيعه جاز هبته وما لا كمجهول ومغصوب وضال فلا إلا حبتي

حنطة ونحوها وهبة الدين للمدين إبراء ولغيره باطلة في الأصح ولا يملك موهوب

إلا بقبض بإذن الواهب فلو مات أحدهما بين الهبة والقبض قام وارثه مقامه

وقيل: ينفسخ العقد ويسن للوالد العدل في عطية أولاده بأن يسوي بين الذكر

والأنثى وقيل: كقسمة الإرث وللأب الرجوع في هبة ولده وكذا لسائر الأصول على

المشهور وشرط رجوعه بقاء الموهوب في سلطنة المتهب فيمتنع ببيعه ووقفه لا

برهنه وهبته قبل القبض وتعليق عتقه وتزويجها وزراعتها وكذا الإجارة على

المذهب ولو زال ملكه دعا ولم يرجع في الأصح ولو زاد رجع فيه بزيادته

المتصلة لا المنفصلة ويحصل الرجوع برجعه فيما وهبت أو استرجعته أو رددته

إلى ملكي أو نقضت الهبة لا يبيعه ووقفه
# 
# وهبته واعتاقه ووطئها في الأصح ولا رجوع لغير الأصول في هبة مقيدة بنفي

الثواب ومتى وهب مطلقا فلا ثواب إن وهب لدونه وكذا لأعلى منه في الأظهر

ولنظيره على المذهب فإن وجب فهو قيمة الموهوب في الأصح فإن لم يثبه فله

الرجوع ولو وهب بشرط ثواب معلوم فالأظهر صحة العقد ويكون بيعا على الصحيح

أو مجهول فالمذهب بطلانه ولو بعث هدية في ظرف فإن لم تجر العادة برده

كقوصرة تمر فهو هدية  أيضا وإلا فلا ويحرم استعماله إلا في أكل الهدية منه

إن اقتضته العادة.
# 

| كتاب اللقظة
# يستحب الالتقاط لواثق بأمانة نفسه وقيل: يجب ولا يستحب لغير واثق ويجوز

في الأصح ويكره لفاسق والمذهب أنه لا يجب الإشهاد على الالتقاط وأنه يصح

التقاط الفاسق والصبي والذمي في دار الإسلام ثم الأظهر أنه ينزع من الفاسق

ويوضع عند عدل وأنه لا يعتمد تعريفه بل يضم إليه رقيب وينزع الولي لقطة

الصبي ويعرف ويتملكها للصبي إن رأى ذلك حيث يجوز الاقتراض له ويضمن الولي

إن قصر في انتزاعه حتى تلف في يد الصبي والأظهر بطلان التقاط العبد ولا

يعتد بتعريفه فلو أخذه سيده منه كان التقاطا.
# قلت: المذهب صحة التقاط المكاتب كتابة صحيحة ومن بعضه حر وهي له ولسيده

فإن كانت مهايأة فلصاحب النوبة في الأظهر وكذا حكم سائر النادر من الإكساب

والمؤن إلا أرش الجناية والله أعلم.

# فصل
# الحيوان المملوك الممتنع من صغار السباع بقوة كبعير وفرس أو بعدو كأرنب

وظبي أو طيران كحمام إن وجد بمفازة للقاضي التقاطه للحفظ وكذا لغيره في

الأصح ويحرم التقاطه
# 
# لتملك وإن وجد بقرية فالأصح جواز التقاطه للتملك وما لا يمتنع منها كشاة

يجوز التقاطه لتملك في القرية والمفازة ويتخير آخذه من مفازة فإن شاء عرفه

وتملكه أو باعه وحفظ ثمنه وعرفها ثم تملكه أو أكله وغرم قيمته إن ظهر مالكه

فإن أخذ من العمران فله الخصلتان الأوليان لا الثالثة في الأصح ويجوز أن

يلتقط عبدا لا يميز ويلتقط غير الحيوان فإن كان يسرع فساده كهريسة فإن شاء

باعه وعرفه ليتملك ثمنه وإن شاء تملكه في الحال وأكله وقيل: إن وجده في

عمران وجب البيع وإن أمكن بقاؤه بعلاج كرطب يتجفف فإن كانت الغبطة في بيعه

بيع أو في تجفيفه وتبرع به الواجد وإلا بيع بعضه لتجفيف الباقي ومن أخذ

لقطة للحفظ أبدا فهي أمانة فإن دفعها إلى القاضي لزمه القبول ولم يوجب

الأكثرون التعريف والحالة هذه فلو قصد بعد ذلك الخيانة لم يصر ضامنا في

الأصح  وإن أخذ بقصد الخيانة فضامن وليس له بعده أن يعرف ويتملك على المذهب

وإن أخذ ليعرف ويتملك فأمانه مدة التعريف وكذا بعدها ما لم يختر التملك في

الأصح ويعرف جنسها وصفتها وقدرها وعفاصها ووكاءها ثم يعرفها في الأسواق

وأبواب المساجد ونحوها سنة على العادة يعرف أولا كل يوم طرفي النهار ثم كل

يوم مرة ثم كل أسبوع ثم كل شهر ولا تكفي سنة متفرقة في الأصح.
# قلت: الأصح تكفي. والله أعلم.

chapters.translation:
I say: If the endower stipulates supervision (naẓar) for himself or another, that stipulation is followed; otherwise, supervision falls to the judge (al-qāḍī) according to the established school (al-madhhab).

The conditions of the supervisor are: probity (ʿadālah), competence (kifāyah), and guidance toward proper management (al-ih tidāʾ ilā al-taṣarruf). His function is maintenance (al-ʿimārah), leasing (al-ijārah), collection of revenue (taḥṣīl al-ghallah), and its distribution. If he is delegated only some of these matters, he must not exceed them.

The endower may dismiss whomever he appointed and appoint another in his place, unless he stipulated supervision for himself at the time of the endowment. When the supervisor leases [the property] and the rent increases during the term, or a bidder appears offering more, the contract is not rescinded in the more correct opinion (al-aṣaḥḥ).

[Book of Gifts (Kitāb al-Hibah)]

Giving ownership without compensation is a gift (hibah). If one gives to someone in need seeking reward in the Hereafter, it is charity (ṣadaqah). If one transfers it to the recipient's location as an honor to him, it is a present (hadiyyah). The conditions of a gift are an offer (ījāb) and acceptance (qabūl) verbally; these are not required in a present according to the correct opinion (al-ṣaḥīḥ); rather, the sending by the giver and the taking by the recipient suffice.

If one says: "I grant you life-tenancy ('umrā) of this house; when I die, it is for your heirs," it is a gift. If he restricts himself to "I grant you life-tenancy," likewise in the new opinion (al-jadīd). If he says: "When I die, it reverts to me," likewise in the more correct opinion. If he says: "I give you ruqbā (reversionary gift)" or "I make it ruqbā for you," meaning: if I die before you, it reverts to me; if you die before me, it is settled for you — then the school (al-madhhab) applies both opinions, the new and the old (al-qawlān al-jadīd wa al-qadīm).

Whatever is permissible to sell is permissible to give as a gift; whatever is not — such as the unknown (majhūl), the usurped (maghṣūb), and the lost (ḍāll) — is not permissible, except two handfuls of wheat (ḥabbatay ḥinṭah) and the like. The gift of a debt to the debtor is an acquittal (ibrāʾ); to another is void in the more correct opinion.

The recipient does not own the gifted object except by taking possession (qabḍ) with the permission of the giver. If one of them dies between the gift and the taking, his heir stands in his place. It is said: the contract is rescinded. It is recommended (yusannu) for a parent to be just in giving to his children, equalizing between the male and the female. It is said: like the division of inheritance.

A father may revoke his gift to his child, and likewise other ascendants according to the well-known opinion (al-mashhūr). The condition of his revocation is that the gifted object remains in the dominion of the recipient; thus revocation is prevented by the recipient's sale of it or endowment of it — not by his pledging it as collateral (rahn) or gifting it before possession, nor by his suspending its manumission, nor by his marrying her [the slave-gift], nor by his cultivating it, nor likewise by leasing it according to the school. If ownership leaves his hand, he may sue but does not revoke in the more correct opinion. If it increases, he revokes it with its connected increase (ziyādah muttaṣilah), not the disconnected one.

Revocation is effected by his reclaiming what was gifted, or by his taking it back, or by his returning it to his ownership, or by his annulling the gift — not by his selling it or endowing it, nor by his gifting it, nor by his manumitting it, nor by his having intercourse with her in the more correct opinion.

There is no revocation for other than ascendants in a gift restricted by the negation of recompense (nāfī al-thawāb). Whenever one gives absolutely (muṭlaqan), no recompense is due if he gives to one below him; likewise to one above him in the most apparent opinion (al-aẓhar); and to his equal according to the school. If recompense is obligatory, it is the value of the gifted object in the more correct opinion. If he does not recompense him, he may revoke.

If one gives with the condition of a known recompense, the most apparent opinion is the validity of the contract, and it is a sale according to the correct opinion. If the recompense is unknown, the school holds its nullity.

If one sends a present in a container, and custom does not require its return — like a basket of dates (qawṣarah tamr) — it is also a present. Otherwise, it is not. It is prohibited to use it except for eating from it in the case of the present, if custom so requires.

[Book of Found Property (Kitāb al-Luqṭah)]

It is recommended (yustaḥabbu) to pick up lost property for one confident in his own trustworthiness. It is said: obligatory. It is not recommended for one not confident, though permissible in the more correct opinion; and it is disliked (makrūh) for a sinner (fāsiq).

The school holds that witnessing (ishhād) upon picking up is not obligatory, and that the picking up by a sinner, a child, and a dhimmī in the Abode of Islam (dār al-Islām) is valid. Then the most apparent opinion is that it is seized from the sinner and placed with a just person; that his announcement (taʿrīf) is not relied upon; rather, a supervisor is added to him. The guardian seizes the found property of a child, announces it, and takes ownership of it for the child if he deems that appropriate, where borrowing on his behalf is permissible. The guardian is liable if he is negligent in seizing it until it perishes in the child's hand.

The most apparent opinion is the invalidity of a slave's picking up, and his announcement is not counted. If his master takes it from him, it is [considered] picking up.

I say: The school holds the validity of picking up by a mukātab (slave under manumission contract) with a sound contract, and by one partially free; it belongs to him and his master. If there is a time-division (muhāyāʾah), then it belongs to the one whose turn it is in the most apparent opinion. Likewise is the ruling for all rare acquisitions and expenses, except the indemnity for injury (arsh al-jināyah). And God knows best.

[Section]

Owned animals that are protected from small predators by strength — like a camel or horse — or by speed — like a hare or gazelle — or by flight — like pigeons — if found in a desert, the judge may pick them up for preservation; likewise others in the more correct opinion. It is prohibited to pick them up for ownership. If found in a village, the more correct opinion permits picking them up for ownership.

What is not so protected — like a sheep — may be picked up for ownership in both village and desert. The taker from a desert has a choice: if he wishes, he announces it and takes ownership; or he sells it and preserves its price; or he announces it and then takes ownership; or he eats it and guarantees its value if the owner appears. If he takes it from inhabited land, he has the first two options, not the third, in the more correct opinion.

It is permissible to pick up a non-discerning slave. Non-animal property may also be picked up. If it spoils quickly — like harīsah (a cooked wheat dish) — then if he wishes, he sells it and announces it to take ownership of its price; or he takes ownership of it immediately and eats it. It is said: if he finds it in inhabited land, sale is obligatory.

If it can survive with treatment — like fresh dates that dry — then if selling is more beneficial, it is sold; or if drying is better and the finder donates his effort, [it is dried]; otherwise, part is sold to dry the rest.

Whoever takes found property for preservation perpetually — it is a trust (amānah). If he hands it to the judge, the judge must accept it. The majority (al-aktharūn) do not require announcement in this case. If he subsequently intends betrayal, he does not become liable in the more correct opinion. If he takes it with the intent of betrayal, he is liable, and thereafter he may not announce and take ownership according to the school.

If he takes it to announce and then take ownership, he is a trustee during the announcement period, and likewise after it as long as he has not chosen ownership in the more correct opinion.

He announces its kind (jins), description (ṣifah), quantity (qadr), its wrapper (ʿifāṣ), and its tie (wikāʾ). Then he announces it in markets, at mosque doors, and the like, for one year according to custom: first, twice daily at the two ends of the day; then once daily; then once weekly; then once monthly. One scattered year does not suffice in the more correct opinion.

I say: The more correct opinion is that it suffices. And God knows best.

chapters.arabic_text:
# فصل
# ويذكر بعض أوصافها ولا يلزمه مؤنة التعريف إن أخذ لحفظ بل يرتبها القاضي

من بيت المال أو يقترض على المالك وإن أخذ لتملك لزمته وقيل: إن لم يتملك

فعلى المالك والأصح أن الحقير لا يعرف سنة بل زمنا يظن أن فاقده يعرض عنه

غالبا.
#

# فصل
# إذا عرف سنة لم يملكها حتى يختاره بلفظ كتملكت وقيل: تكفي النية وقيل:

يملك بمضي السنة فإن تملك فظهر المالك واتفقا على رد عينها فذاك وإن أرادها

المالك وأراد الملتقط العدول إلى بدلها أجيب المالك في الأصح وإن تلفت غرم

مثلها أو قيمتها يوم التملك وإن نقصت بعيب فله أخذها مع الأرش في الأصح

وإذا ادعاها رجل ولم يصفها ولا بينة لم تدفع إليه وإن وصفها وظن صدقه جاز

الدفع إليه ولا يجب على المذهب فإن دفع فأقام آخر بينة بها حولت إليه فإن

تلفت عنده فلصاحب البينة تضمين الملتقط والمدفوع إليه والقرار عليه.
# قلت: لا تحل لقطة الحرم للتملك على الصحيح ويجب تعريفها قطعا. والله

أعلم.
# 

| كتاب اللقيط
# التقاط المنبوذ فرض كفاية ويجب الإشهاد عليه في الأصح وإنما تثبت ولاية

الالتقاط لمكلف حر مسلم عدل رشيد ولو التقط عبد بغير إذن سيده انتزع منه

فإن علمه فأقره عنده أو التقط بإذنه فالسيد الملتقط ولو التقط صبي أو فاسق

أو محجور عليه أو كافر مسلما انتزع ولو ازدحم اثنان على أخذه جعله الحاكم

عند من يراه منهما أو من غيرهما وإن سبق واحد فالتقطه منع الآخر من مزاحمته

وإن التقطاه معا وهما أهل  فالأصح انه يقدم غني على فقير وعدل على مستور فإن

استويا أقرع وإذا وجد بلدي لقيطا ببلد فليس له نقله إلى بادية والأصح أن له

نقله إلى بلد آخر وأن للغريب إذا التقط ببلد أن ينقله إلى بلده وإن وجد

ببادية فله نقله إلى بلد وإن وجده بدوي ببلد فكالحضري أو ببادية أقر بيده

وقيل: إن كانوا ينتقلون للنجعة لم يقر ونفقته في ماله العام كوقف على

اللقطاء أو الخاص وهو ما اختص به كثياب ملفوفة عليه ومفروشة تحته وما في

جيبه من دراهم وغيرها ومهده ودنانير منثورة فوقه وتحته وإن وجد في دار فهي

له وليس له مال مدفون تحته وكذا ثياب وأمتعة موضوعة بقربة في الأصح فإن لم

يعرف له مال فالأظهر أنه ينفق عليه من بيت المال فإن لم يكن قام المسلمون

بكفايته قرضا وفي قول نفقة وللملتقط الاستقلال بحفظ ماله في الأصح ولا ينفق

عليه منه إلا بإذن القاضي قطعا.
#

# فصل
# إذا وجد لقيط بدار الإسلام وفيها أهل ذمة أو بدار فتحوها وأقروها بيد

كفار صلحا أو بعد ملكها بجزية وفيها مسلم حكم بإسلام اللقيط وإن وجد بدار

كفار فكافر إن لم يسكنها مسلم كأسير وتاجر وإلا فمسلم في الأصح ومن حكم

بإسلامه بالدار فأقام ذمي بينة بنسبه لحقه وتبعه في الكفر وإن اقتصر على

الدعوى فالمذهب أنه لا يتبعه في الكفر ويحكم بإسلام الصبي بجهتين أخريين لا

تفرضان في لقيط إحداهما الولادة فإذا كان أحد أبويه مسلما وقت العلوق فهو

مسلم فإن بلغ ووصف كفرا فمرتد ولو علق بين كافرين ثم أسلم أحدهما حكم

بإسلامه فإن بلغ ووصف كفرا فمرتد وفي قول كافر أصلي الثانية إذا سبى مسلم

طفلا تبع السابي في الإسلام إن لم يكن معه احد أبويه ولو سباه ذمي لم يحكم

بإسلامه في الأصح ولا يصح إسلام صبي مميز استقلالا على الصحيح.
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ع-ر-ف (ʿ-r-f)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Recognition, knowledge by acquaintance; the act of identifying something after repeated exposure.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): ʿIrfān as the cognitive act of discerning an object's identity, distinct from ʿilm (certain knowledge); here, the legal duty of public announcement.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Ḥaqīqah — literal recognition of the object; Majāz — the legal construct of the announcement period (sannah) as a proxy for the owner's search.
- Sībawayh Rule: Conditional Clause (al-Sharṭ wa al-Jawāb) — The protasis (in, 'if') governs the apodosis (the legal ruling), requiring precise temporal and modal sequencing.
chapters.translation:
I say: The finder mentions some of its distinguishing features, and he is not obligated to bear the expense of the announcement if he took it for the purpose of safekeeping; rather, the judge arranges that from the public treasury (bayt al-māl), or he may borrow against the owner's liability. But if he took it with the intention of ownership, then the expense is incumbent upon him. It was said: If he did not intend ownership, then it falls upon the owner. The soundest opinion (al-aṣaḥḥ) is that a trifling object (al-ḥaqīr) is not announced for a full year, but rather for a period of time in which it is presumed that its loser would generally abandon seeking it.

I say: When he has announced it for a year, he does not own it until he chooses it by an explicit utterance (lafẓ), such as saying, 'I have taken possession' (tamallaktu). It was said: Intention (niyyah) suffices. It was said: He owns it merely by the passage of the year. If he then takes possession, and the owner appears, and both agree to return the very same object (ʿayn), then that is permissible. But if the owner wants the object itself, and the finder wants to divert to its equivalent (badal), the owner is answered (yujāb) in the soundest opinion. If it perishes, he must guarantee its equivalent (mithl) or its value (qīmah) on the day of taking possession. If it has diminished due to a defect, he may take it along with compensation for the defect (arsh) in the soundest opinion. When a man claims it but does not describe it, and brings no evidence (bayyinah), it is not handed over to him. If he describes it, and the finder deems him truthful, it is permissible to hand it over to him, though not obligatory according to the school (madhhab). If he hands it over, and then another man establishes evidence of ownership over it, it is transferred to the latter. If it perishes in the first recipient's possession, then the one with the evidence may hold liable (taḍmīn) both the finder and the one to whom it was handed, and the ultimate liability (al-qarār) rests upon the latter.

I say: The found property of the Sacred Precinct (al-Ḥaram) is not permissible for ownership in the soundest opinion, and its announcement is absolutely obligatory. And God knows best.

[Book of the Foundling (Kitāb al-Laqīṭ)]

The picking up of an abandoned infant (al-munbadh) is a communal obligation (farḍ kifāyah), and it is obligatory to have witnesses (ishhād) to it in the soundest opinion. The guardianship of picking up (wilāyat al-iltiqāṭ) is established only for a legally responsible (mukallaf), free, Muslim, upright (ʿadl), and judicious (rashīd) person. If a slave picks up without his master's permission, it is seized from him. If the master knows of it and lets him keep it, or if he picked it up with permission, then the master is the picker-up (al-multaqiṭ). If a child, a corrupt person (fāsiq), one under legal interdiction (maḥjūr ʿalayh), or an unbeliever picks up a Muslim infant, it is seized from him. If two persons crowd together to take it, the judge places it with whichever of them he deems fit, or with someone else entirely. If one precedes the other and picks it up, the other is prevented from contesting him. If they pick it up simultaneously, and both are qualified, the soundest opinion is that the wealthy one is preferred over the poor, and the upright over the one of unknown status (mastūr). If they are equal, lots are cast (qurʿah). When a settled dweller (baladī) finds a foundling in a town, he may not transfer it to the desert (bādiyah). The soundest opinion is that he may transfer it to another town, and that a stranger (gharīb) who picks up a foundling in a town may transfer it to his own land. If he finds it in the desert, he may transfer it to a town. If a Bedouin (badawī) finds it in a town, he is treated like a settled dweller (ḥaḍarī); or if in the desert, it is left in his hands. It was said: If they are a people who move about for pasture (nujʿah), it is not left with him. Its maintenance (nafaqah) comes from its general wealth (al-māl al-ʿāmm), such as an endowment (waqf) for foundlings, or from its specific wealth (al-khāṣṣ), which is what is exclusively attached to it, like clothes wrapped around it, bedding spread beneath it, dirhams and other items in its pocket, its cradle, and dinars scattered above and beneath it. If found in a house, that house belongs to it, but not wealth buried beneath it. Likewise, clothes and goods placed nearby are not its property in the soundest opinion. If no wealth of its own is known, the most manifest opinion (al-aẓhar) is that it is maintained from the public treasury (bayt al-māl). If that is not available, then the Muslims undertake its sufficiency as a loan (qarḍ). In one saying, it is a maintenance obligation (nafaqah). The picker-up has the sole authority to preserve its wealth in the soundest opinion, but he may not spend from it upon the foundling except with the judge's permission, absolutely.

I say: When a foundling is found in the Abode of Islam (dār al-Islām) in which there are people of the dhimmah, or in a territory which the Muslims conquered and left in the hands of unbelievers by treaty (ṣulḥ), or after possessing it by tribute (jizyah) while a Muslim resides therein, the foundling is adjudged a Muslim. If found in the Abode of Unbelief (dār al-kufr), then it is an unbeliever, unless a Muslim resides there, such as a captive (asīr) or a merchant; otherwise, it is a Muslim in the soundest opinion. If one adjudged Muslim by virtue of the abode, and then a dhimmī establishes evidence of his lineage to it, the foundling follows him and shares his unbelief. If he confines himself to a mere claim (daʿwā), then according to the school, it does not follow him in unbelief. The Islam of a child is also established by two other means, which are not posited in the case of a foundling. The first is birth (wilādah): if either of its parents was Muslim at the time of conception (ʿalq), then it is Muslim. If it reaches maturity and professes unbelief, it is an apostate (murtadd). If it was conceived between two unbelievers, and then one of them embraces Islam, it is adjudged Muslim; if it reaches maturity and professes unbelief, it is an apostate, and in one saying, an original unbeliever (kāfir aṣlī). The second is when a Muslim takes a child captive (sabā): the child follows the captor in Islam, provided neither of its parents is with it. If a dhimmī takes it captive, it is not adjudged Muslim in the soundest opinion. The independent Islam of a discerning child (ṣabīy mumayyiz) is not valid on his own accord in the soundest opinion.

chapters.title_en: Section 57 — The Foundling, Reward Contracts (Juʿālah), and the Laws of Inheritance (Farāʾiḍ)
chapters.arabic_text:
# فصل
# إذا لم يقر اللقيط برق فهو حر إلا أن يقيم أحد بينة برقه وإن أقر به لشخص

فصدقه قبل  إن لم يسبق إقراره بحرية والمذهب أنه لا يشترط أن لا يسبق تصرف

يقتضي نفوذه حرية كبيع ونكاح بل يقبل إقراره في أصل الرق وأحكامه المستقبلة

لا الماضية المضرة بغيره في الأظهر فلو لزمه دين فأقر برق وفي يده مال قضى

منه ولو ادعى رقه من ليس في يده بلا بينة لم يقبل وكذا إن ادعاه الملتقط في

الأظهر ولو رأينا صغيرا مميزا او غيره في يد من يسترقه ولم نعرف استنادها

إلى الالتقاط حكم له بالرق فإن بلغ وقال أنا حر لم يقبل قوله في الأصح إلا

ببينة ومن أقام بينة برقه عمل بها ويشترط أن تتعرض البينة لسبب الملك وفي

قول يكفي مطلق الملك ولو استلحق اللقيط حر مسلم لحقه وصار أولى بتربيته وإن
# 
# استلحقه عبد لحقه وفي قول يشترط تصديق سيده وإن استلحقته امرأة لم يلحقها

في الأصح أو اثنان لم يقدم مسلم وحر على ذمي وعبد فإن لم تكن بينة عرض على

القائف فيلحق من ألحقه به فإن لم يكن قائف أو تحير أو نفاه عنهما أو ألحقه

بهما أمر بالانتساب بعد بلوغه إلى من يميل طبعه إليه منهما ولو أقام بينتين

متعارضتين سقطتا في الأظهر.
# 

| كتاب الجعالة
# هي كقوله من رد آبقي فله كذا ويشترط صيغه تدل على العمل بعوض ملتزم فلو

عمل بلا إذن أو أذن لشخص فعمل غيره فلا شيء له ولو قال أجنبي من رد عبد زيد

فله كذا استحقه الراد على الأجنبي وإن قال: قال زيد من رد عبدي فله كذا

وكان كاذبا لم يستحق عليه ولا على زيد ولا يشترط قبول العامل وإن عينيه

وتصح على عمل مجهول وكذا معلوم في الأصح ويشترط كون الجعل معلوما فلو قال

من رده فله ثوب أو أرضيه فسد العقد وللراد أجرة مثله ولو قال من بلد كذا

فرده من أقرب منه فله قسطه من الجعل ولو اشترط اثنان في رده اشتركا في

الجعل ولو التزم جعلا لمعين فشاركه غيره في العمل إن قصد  إعانته فله كل

الجعل وإن قصد العمل للمالك فللأول قسطه ولا شيء للمشارك بحال ولكل منهما

الفسخ قبل تمام العمل فإن فسخ قبل الشروع أو فسخ العامل بعد الشروع فلا شيء

له وإن فسخ المالك بعد الشروع فعليه أجرة المثل في الأصح وللمالك أن يزيد

وينقص في الجعل قبل الفراغ وفائدته بعد الشروع وجوب أجرة المثل ولو مات

الآبق في بعض الطريق أو هرب فلا شيء للعامل وإذا رده فليس له حبسه لقبض

الجعل ويصدق المالك إذا أنكر شرط الجعل أو سعيه في رده فإن اختلفا في قدر

الجعل تحالفا.
# 

| كتاب الفرائض
# يبدأ من تركة الميت بمؤنة تجهيزه ثم تقضى ديونه ثم وصاياه من ثلث الباقي

ثم يقسم الباقي بين الورقة.
# قلت: فإن تعلق بعين التركة حق كالزكاة والجاني والمرهون والمبيع إذا مات

المشتري مفلسا قدم على مؤنة تجهيزه. والله أعلم.
# وأسباب الإرث أربعة قرابة ونكاح وولاء فيرث المعتق العتيق ولا عكس

والرابع: الإسلام فتصرف التركة لبيت المال إرثا إذا لم يكن وارث بالأسباب

الثلاثة والمجمع على إرثهم من الرجال عشرة الابن وابنه وإن سفل والأب وأبوه

وإن علا والأخ وابنه إلا من الأم والعم إلا لأم وكذا ابنه والزوج والمعتق

ومن النساء سبع البنت وبنت الابن وإن سفل والأم والجدة والأخت والزوجة

والمعتقة فلو اجتمع كل الرجال ورث الأب والابن والزوج فقط أو كل النساء

فالبنت وبنت الابن والأم والأخت للأبوين والزوجة أو الذين يمكن اجتماعهم من

الصنفين فالأبوان والابن والبنت وأحد الزوجين ولو فقدوا كلهم فأصل المذهب

أنه لا يورث ذوو الأرحام ولا يرد على أهل الفرض بل المال لبيت المال وأفتى

المتأخرون إذا لم ينتظم أمر بيت المال بالرد على أهل الفرض غير الزوجين ما

فضل عن
# 
# فروضهم بالنسبة فإن لم يكونوا صرف إلى ذوي الأرحام وهم من سوى المذكورين

من الأقارب وهم عشرة أصناف أبو الأم وكل جد وجدة ساقطين وأولاد البنات

وبنات الإخوة وأولاد الأخوات وبنات الإخوة للأم والعم للأم وبنات الأعمام

والعمات والأخوال والخالات  والمدلون بهم.

# فصل
# الفروض المقدرة في كتاب الله تعالى ستة النصف فرض خمسة زوج لم تخلف زوجته

ولدا ولا ولد ابن وبنت أو بنت ابن أو أخت لأبوين أو لأب منفردات والربع فرض

زوج لزوجته ولد أو ولد ابن وزوجة ليس لزوجها واحد منهما والثمن فرضها مع

أحدهما والثلثان فرض بنتين فصاعادا أو بنتا ابن فأكثر وأختين فأكثر لأبوين

أو لأب والثلث فرض أم ليس لميتها ولد ولا ولد ابن والاثنان من الإخوة

والأخوات وفرض اثنين فأكثر من ولد الأم وقد يفرض للجد مع الإخوة والسدس فرض

سبعة أب وجد لميتهما ولد أو ولد ابن وأم لميتها ولد أو ولد ابن أو اثنان من

إخوة وأخوات وجدة ولبنت ابن مع بنت صلب ولأخت أو أخوات لأب مع أخت لأبوين

وللواحد من ولد الأم.
