chapters.arabic_text:
# فصل
# ليسو بين الخصمين في دخول عليه وقيام لهما واستماع وطلاقه وجه وجواب سلام

ومجلس والأصح رفع  مسلم على ذمي فيه وإذا جلسا فله إن يسكت وأن يقول ليتكلم

المدعي فإذا ادعى طالب خصمه بالجواب فإن أقر فذاك وإن أنكر فله أن يقول

للمدعي
# 
# ألك بينة وأن يسكت فإن قال لي بينة وأريد تحليفه فله ذلك أو لا بينة لي

ثم أحضرها قبلت في الأصح. وإذا ازدحم خصوم قدم الأسبق فإن جهل أو جاءوا معا

أقرع ويقدم مسافرون مستوفزون ونسوة وإن تأخروا ما لم يكثروا ولا يقدم سابق

وقارع إلا بدعوى ويحرم اتخاذ شهود معينين لا يقبل غيرهم وإذا شهد شهود فعرف

عدالة أو فسقا عمل بعلمه وإلا وجب الاستزكاء بان يكتب مما يتميز به الشاهد

والمشهود له وعليه وكذا قدر الدين على الصحيح ويبعث به مزكيا ثم يشافهه

المزكي بما عنده وقيل: تكفي كتابته وشرطه كشاهد مع معرفته الجرح والتعديل

وخبرة باطن من يعد له لصحبة أو جوار أو معاملة والأصح اشتراط لفظ شهادته

وأنه يكفي هو عدل وقيل: يزيد على ولي ويجب ذكر سبب الجرح ويعتمد فيه

المعاينة أو الاستفاضة ويقدم على التعديل فإن قال المعدل عرفت سبب الجرح

وتاب منه وأصلح قدم والأصح أنه لا يكفي في التعديل قول المدعى عليه هو عدل

وقد غلط.
# 

| باب القضاء على الغائب
# هو جائز إن كان عليه بينة وادعى المدعي جحوده فإن قال هو مقر لم تسمع

بينته وإن أطلق فالأصح أنها تسمع وأنه لا يلزم القاضي نصب مسخر ينكر على

الغائب ويجب أن يحلفه بعد البينة أن الحق ثابت في ذمته وقيل: يستحب ويجريان

في دعوى على صبي أو مجنون ولو ادعى وكيل على الغائب فلا تحليف ولو حضر

المدعى عليه وقال لوكيل المدعي أبرأني
# 
# موكلك أمر بالتسليم وإذا ثبت مال على غائب وله مال قضاه الحاكم منه وإلا

فإن سأل المدعي إنهاء الحال إلى قاضي بلد الغائب أجابه فينهى سماع بينة

ليحكم بها ثم يستوفي أو حكما ليستوفي.
# والإنهاء أن يشهد عدلين بذلك ويستحب كتاب به يذكر فيه ما يتميز به

المحكوم عليه ويختمه ويشهدان  عليه إن أنكر فإن قال لست المسمى في الكتاب

صدق بيمينه وعلى المدعي بينة بأن هذا المكتوب اسمه ونسبه فإن أقامها فقال

لست المحكوم عليه لزمه الحكم إن لم يكن هناك مشارك له في الاسم والصفات وإن

كان أحضر فإن اعترف بالحق طولب وترك الأول وإلا بعث إلى الكاتب ليطلب من

الشهود زيادة صفة تميزه ويكتبها ثانيا ولو حضر قاضي بلد الغائب ببلد الحاكم

فشافهه بحكمه ففي إمضائه إذا عاد إلى ولايته خلاف القضاء بعلمه ولو ناداه

في طرفي ولايتيهما أمضاه وإن اقتصر على سماع بينة كتب سمعت بينة على فلان

ويسميها إن لم يعدلها وإلا فالأصح جواز ترك التسمية والكتاب بالحكم يمضي مع

قرب المسافة وبسماع البينة لا يقبل على الصحيح إلا في مسافة قبول شهادة على

شهادة.

# فصل
# ادعى عينا غائبة عن البلد يؤمن اشتباهها كعقار وعبد وفرس معروفات سمع

بينة وحكم بها وكتب إلى قاضي بلد المال ليسلمه للمدعي ويعتمد في العقار

حدوده أو لا يؤمن فالأظهر سماع البينة ويبالغ المدعي في الوصف ويذكر القيمة

وأنه لا يحكم بها بل يكتب إلى
# 
# قاضي بلد المال بما شهدت به فيأخذه ويبعثه إلى الكاتب ليشهدوا على عينه

والأظهر أنه يسلمه إلى المدعي بكفيل ببدنه فإن شهدوا بعينه كتب ببراءة

الكفيل وإلا فعلى المدعي مؤنة الرد أو غائبة عن المجلس لا لبلد أمر بإحضار

ما يمكن إحضاره ليشهدوا بعينه ولا تسمع شهادة بصفة وإذا وجب إحضار فقال ليس

بيدي عين بهذه الصفة صدق بيمينه ثم للمدعي دعوى القيمة فإن نكل فحلف المدعي

أو أقام بينة كلف الإحضار وحبس عليه ولا يطلق إلا بإحضار أو دعوى تلف ولو

شك المدعي هل تلفت العين فيدعي قيمة أم لا فيدعيها فقال غصب مني كذا فإن

بقي لزمه رده وإلا فقيمته سمعت دعواه وقيل: لا بل يدعيها ويحلفه ثم يدعي

القيمة ويجريان فيمن دفع ثوبه لدلال ليبيعه فجحده وشك هل باعه فيطلب الثمن

أم أتلفه فقيمته أم هو باق فيطلبه وحيث أوجبنا الإحضار فثبت  للمدعي استقرت

مؤنته على المدعى عليه وإلا فهو ومؤنة الرد على المدعي.

# فصل
# الغائب الذي تسمع البينة عليه ويحكم عليه من بمسافة بعيدة وهي التي لا

يرجع منها مبكرا إلى موضعه ليلا وقيل: مسافة قصر ومن بقريبة كحاضر فلا تسمع

بينته ويحكم بغير حضوره إلا لتواريه أو تعززه والأظهر جواز القضاء على غائب

في قصاص وحد قذف ومنعه في حد الله تعالى ولو سمع بينة على غائب فقدم قبل

الحكم لم يستعدها بل يخبر ويمكنه من جرح ولو عزل بعد سماع بينة ثم ولى وجبت

الاستعادة وإذا استعدى على حاضر البلد أحضره بدفع ختم طين رطب أو غيره أو

بمرتب لذلك فإن امتنع بلا عذر أحضره بأعوان
# 
# السلطان وعزره أو غائب في غير ولايته فليس له إحضاره أو فيها وله هناك

نائب لم يحضره بل يسمع بينة ويكتب إليه أو لا نائب فالأصح يحضره من مسافة
chapters.anchors:
- Root: خ-ص-م (kha-ṣa-m)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Core meaning of disputation, contention, and the act of arguing a case against an adversary.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In legal-theological context, it denotes the formal adversarial parties in a judicial proceeding (al-khaṣmān), whose rights and duties are regulated by sacred law.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Used literally here for the two opposing litigants in a court session; no metaphorical extension.
- Sībawayh Rule: Conditional and Exceptive Constructions (al-Sharṭ wa al-Istithnāʾ) — Governing the legal apodoses (jazāʾ) in phrases like "if he acknowledges, then that suffices; if he denies, then he may say..." ensuring precise juristic conditionality.
chapters.translation:
---

**Section 110**

**Chapter on the Conduct Between Two Litigants**

It is not permissible for the judge to admit one of the two litigants over the other in entering upon him, nor in standing for them, nor in listening to them, nor in the salutation and its reply. And if a Muslim and a dhimmī are both present in a single session, the more correct (al-aṣaḥḥ) view is that the Muslim is given precedence in being seated.

When the two litigants have taken their seats, the plaintiff has the right to remain silent or to speak in order to present his claim. When he presents his claim, he demands that his opponent answer. If the opponent acknowledges the claim, then that suffices. If he denies it, the plaintiff may say to him: "Do you have any proof?" — or he may remain silent. If the defendant says: "I have proof and I wish to have him swear an oath," he has that right. If he says: "I have no proof," and then later produces it, it is accepted — this is the more correct view.

When multiple litigants crowd upon the judge, the one who arrived first is given precedence. If their order of arrival is unknown, or they arrived simultaneously, lots are cast among them. Travelers who are in a hurry and women are given precedence even if they arrive later, provided they are not numerous. A person who precedes others or wins the lot is not given priority except upon presenting a claim.

It is unlawful to appoint specific witnesses whose testimony alone is accepted to the exclusion of others. When witnesses testify, if the judge personally knows their uprightness (ʿadālah) or their corruption (fisq), he acts upon his own knowledge. Otherwise, he is obligated to seek their verification (istizkāʾ) by writing a letter containing sufficient distinguishing features of the witness, the person on whose behalf testimony is given, and the person against whom it is given — and likewise the amount of the debt, according to the correct view. He sends this letter with a verifier (muzakkī), who then orally informs the judge of what he knows about them. It was said: his written statement suffices. The conditions for the verifier are the same as for a witness, along with his knowledge of disparagement (jarḥ) and commendation (taʿdīl), and his familiarity with the inner state of the one he verifies, whether through companionship, neighborliness, or business dealings. The more correct view is that the verifier must utter the wording of his testimony, and that his saying "he is upright" suffices. It was said: he must add "and he is a guardian (walī)." It is obligatory to mention the reason for disparagement, and in this regard, direct observation or widespread report (istifāḍah) is relied upon. Disparagement takes precedence over commendation. If the one who commends says: "I knew the reason for his disparagement, and he repented from it and reformed," then the commendation takes precedence. The more correct view is that the statement of the defendant — "he is upright" — is not sufficient for commendation, and whoever relies on that has erred.

---

**Chapter on Judgment Against the Absent (al-Qaḍāʾ ʿalā al-Ghāʾib)**

Judgment against an absent party is permissible if there is proof against him and the plaintiff claims that he would deny the claim. If the plaintiff says: "He acknowledges the debt," his proof is not heard. If he makes an unqualified claim, the more correct view is that his proof is heard. The judge is not obligated to appoint a deputy to dispute on behalf of the absent party. It is obligatory for the judge to have the plaintiff swear an oath after presenting his proof that the right is established as a debt upon the absent party's liability (dhimmah). It was said: this oath is merely recommended. Both views apply to a claim against a minor or an insane person. If a legal agent (wakīl) brings a claim against an absent party, no oath is required from him. If the defendant appears and says to the plaintiff's agent: "Your principal has released me from the claim," he is ordered to deliver [the payment].

When a debt is established against an absent person and he has property [in the judge's jurisdiction], the judge pays the debt from it. If not, and the plaintiff requests that the case be referred (inhāʾ) to the judge of the absent party's country, the judge responds to his request. He then refers the matter by hearing the testimony so that [the other judge] may rule upon it, or by issuing a judgment so that [the other judge] may execute it.

The referral (al-inhāʾ) is done by having two upright witnesses testify to that effect. It is recommended that a written document be sent with them, mentioning the distinguishing features of the person against whom judgment was rendered, and the judge seals it. The two witnesses testify against him if he denies. If he says: "I am not the person named in the document," he is believed upon his oath. The plaintiff must then provide proof that this written name and lineage refer to him. If he provides such proof, and the defendant then says: "I am not the one against whom judgment was rendered," the judgment is binding upon him, provided there is no one else sharing his name and attributes. If there is such a namesake, and the defendant is present, then if he acknowledges the right, he is pursued for it and the first [judgment] is abandoned. Otherwise, a message is sent to the scribe to request from the witnesses an additional distinguishing feature, and he writes it a second time.

If the judge of the absent party's country appears in the country of the ruling judge and is orally informed of his judgment, there is a difference of opinion — when he returns to his jurisdiction — as to whether he executes it, [the dispute being] analogous to the question of a judge ruling by his own knowledge. If the two judges announce the matter jointly across the boundaries of their respective jurisdictions, he executes it. If the referring judge limited himself to hearing testimony, he writes: "Testimony was heard against so-and-so," naming him unless he has verified his uprightness — in which case, the more correct view is that omitting the name is permissible. A written judgment is executed even across a short distance. As for a written record of heard testimony, it is not accepted, according to the correct view, except within the distance that permits testimony upon testimony.

---

**Chapter [on Claims Involving Property Absent from the Court]**

If a claim is made regarding a specific physical object (ʿayn) absent from the country, whose identity is not feared to be confused — such as real estate, a slave, or a well-known horse — testimony is heard and judgment is rendered upon it, and a letter is written to the judge of the country where the property is located to deliver it to the plaintiff. In the case of real estate, its boundaries are relied upon. If the object's identity is feared to be confused, the more apparent view (al-aẓhar) is that testimony is still heard, and the plaintiff is required to describe it in detail, mentioning its value, and that judgment is not rendered upon it. Rather, a letter is written to the judge of the country where the property is located, containing what was testified to. He then takes the object and sends it to the scribe so that the witnesses may testify upon the very object itself. The more apparent view is that it is delivered to the plaintiff with a guarantor for his person (kafīl bi-badanihi). If the witnesses testify upon the very object, a letter is written declaring the guarantor discharged. Otherwise, the cost of returning it falls upon the plaintiff.

If the object is absent from the court session but not from the country, the judge orders that whatever can be produced be brought forth so that the witnesses may testify upon the very object itself. Testimony by description alone is not heard. When production is obligatory and the defendant says: "I do not possess an object with these attributes," he is believed upon his oath. The plaintiff may then claim its value. If the defendant refuses to swear, and the plaintiff swears or produces proof, the defendant is compelled to produce the object and is imprisoned for it. He is not released except by producing it or by claiming its destruction. If the plaintiff is uncertain whether the object was destroyed — and thus claims its value — or not — and thus claims it — he says: "He usurped from me such-and-such. If it remains, he must return it; otherwise, its value." His claim is heard. It was said: no, rather he claims the object, has the defendant swear an oath, and then claims the value. Both views apply to one who gives his garment to a broker (dallāl) to sell, and the broker denies it, and the owner is uncertain whether he sold it — so he demands the price — or destroyed it — so he demands its value — or it remains — so he demands it. Wherever we have deemed production obligatory and the plaintiff's claim is established, its cost is borne by the defendant. Otherwise, the cost of production and return falls upon the plaintiff.

---

**Chapter [on the Definition of the Absent Party]**

The absent party against whom testimony is heard and judgment is rendered is one who is at a far distance — namely, a distance from which one cannot return to his place by evening. It was said: the distance permitting the shortening of prayer (masāfat al-qaṣr). One who is at a short distance is treated like one present: his testimony is not heard, and judgment is not rendered in his absence, except in cases of his hiding (tawārī) or his arrogance (taʿazzuz). The more apparent view is that judgment against an absent party is permissible in cases of retaliation (qiṣāṣ) and the hadd punishment for slander (ḥadd al-qadhf), but it is prohibited in the hadd punishments of God Almighty. If testimony is heard against an absent party and he appears before judgment is rendered, the testimony is not repeated; rather, he is informed of it and given the opportunity to challenge the witnesses (jarḥ). If the judge is removed after hearing testimony and then reappointed, the testimony must be repeated.

When a complaint is brought against a person present in the judge's country, the judge summons him by sending a seal of moist clay or otherwise, or by appointing a marshal for that purpose. If he refuses without excuse, the judge brings him with the aid of the sultan's officers and disciplines him (yuʿazziruhu). If the defendant is absent in a place outside the judge's jurisdiction, the judge has no authority to summon him. If he is within the jurisdiction and has a deputy there who does not bring him, the judge hears testimony and writes to him. If there is no deputy, the more correct view is that the judge summons him from that distance.

chapters.title_en: Section 111 — On Contagion, Partition (Qisma), and Testimony (Shahādāt)
chapters.arabic_text:
العدوى فقط وهي التي لم يرجع منها مبكرا ليلا وأن المخدرة لا تحضر وهي من

لا يكثر خروجها لحاجات.
#

| باب القسمة
# قد يقسم شركاء أو منصوبهم أو منصوب الإمام وشرط منصوبه ذكر حر عدل يعلم

المساحة والحساب فإن كان فيها تقويم وجب قاسمان وإلا فقاسم وفي قول اثنان

وللإمام جعل القاسم حاكما في التقويم فيعمل فيه بعدلين ويقسم ويجعل الإمام

رزق منصوبه من بيت المال فإن لم يكن فأجرته على الشركاء فإن استأجروه وسمى

كل قدرا لزمه وإلا فالأجرة موزعة على الحصص وفي قول على الرؤوس ثم ما عظم

الضرر في قسمته كجوهرة وثوب نفيسين وزوجي خف إن طلب الشركاء كلهم قسمته لم

يجبهم القاضي ولا يمنعهم إن قسموا بأنفهسم إن لم تبطل منفعته كسيف يكسر وما

يبطل نفعه المقصود كحمام وطاحونة صغيرين لإيجاب طالب قسمته في الأصح فإن

أمكن جعله حمامين أجيب ولو كان له عشر دار لا يصلح لسكنى والباقي لآخر

فالأصح إجبار صاحب العشر بطلب صاحبه دون عكسه وما لا يعظم ضرره قسمته

أنواع:
# أحدها: بالأجزاء كمثلى ودار متفقة أبنية وأرض  مشتبهة الأجزاء فيجبر

الممتنع فتعدل السهام كيلا أو وزنا أو ذرعا بعدد الانصباء إن استوت ويكتب

في كل رقعة اسم شريك
# 
# أو جزء مميز بحد أو جهة وتدرج في بنادق مستوية ثم يخرج من لم يحضرها رقعة

على الجزء الأول إن كتب الأسماء فيعطى من خرج اسمه أو على اسم زيد إن كتب

الأجزاء فإن اختلفت الأنصباء كنصف وثلث وسدس جزئت الأرض على أقل السهام

وقسمت كما سبق ويحترز عن تفريق حصة واحد.
# الثاني: بالتعديل كأرض تختلف قيمة أجزائها بحسب قوة إنبات وقرب ماء ويجبر

عليها في الأظهر ولو استوت قيمة دارين أو حانوتين طلب جعل كل لواحد فلا

إجبار أو عبيد أو ثياب من نوع أجبر أو نوعين فلا.
# الثالث: بالرد بأن يكون في أحد الجانبين بئر أو شجر لا يمكن قسمته فيرد

من يأخذه قسط قيمته ولا إجبار فيه وهو بيع وكذا التعديل على المذهب وقسمة

الأجزاء إفراز في الأظهر.
# ويشترط في الرد الرضا بعد خروج القرعة ولو تراضيا بقسمة مالا إجبار فيه

اشترط الرضا بعد القرعة في الأصح كقولهما رضينا بهذه القسمة أو بما أخرجته

القرعة ولو ثبت ببينة غلط أو حيف في قسمة إجبار نقضت فإن لم تكن بينة

وادعاه واحد فله تحليف شريكه ولو ادعاه في قسمة تراض وقلنا هي بيع فالأصح

أنه لا أثر للغلط فلا فائدة لهذه الدعوى.
# قلت: وإن قلنا إفراز نقضت إن ثبت وإلا فيحلف شريكه والله أعلم ولو استحق

بعض المقسوم شائعا بطلت فهي وفي الباقي خلاف تفريق الصفة أو من النصيبين

معين سواء بقيت وإلا بطلت. والله أعلم.
#

| كتاب الشهادات
# شرط الشاهد مسلم حر مكلف عدل ذو مروءوة غير متهم وشرط العدالة اجتناب

الكبائر والإصرار على صغيرة ويحرم اللعب بالنرد على الصحيح ويكره بشطرنج

فإن شرط فيه مال من الجانبين فقمار ويباح الحداء وسماعه ويكره الغناء بلا

آلة وسماعه ويحرم استعمال آلة من شعار الشربة كطنبور وعود وصنج ومزمار

عراقي وإسماعها لا يراع في الأصح.
# قلت: الأصح تحريمه والله  أعلم ويجوز دف لعرس وختان وكذا غيرهما في الأصح

وإن كان فيه جلاجل ويحرم ضرب الكوبة وهي طبل طويل ضيق الوسط لا الرقص إلا

أن يكون فيه تكسر كفعل المخنث ويباح قول شعر وإنشاده إلا أن يهجو أو يفحش

أو يعرض بامرأة معينة والمروءة تخلق بخلق أمثاله في زمانه ومكانه فالأكل في

سوق والمشي مكشوف الرأس وقبلة زوجة وأمة بحضرة الناس وإكثار حكايات مضحكة

ولبس فقيه قباء وقلنسوة حيث لا يعتاد وإكباب على لعب الشطرنج أو غناء أو

سماعه وإدامة رقص يسقطها والأمر فيه يختلف بالأشخاص والأحوال والأماكن

وحرفة دنيئة كحجامة وكنس ودبغ ممن لا تليق به تسقطها فإن اعتادها وكانت

حرفة أبيه فلا في الأصح والتهمة أن يجر إليه نفعا أو يدفع عنه
# 
# ضررا فترد شهادته لعبده ومكاتبه وغريم له ميت أو عليه حجر فليس وبما هو

وكيل فيه وببراءة من ضمنه وبجراحة مورثه ولو شهد لمورث له مريض أو جريح

بمال قبل الاندمال قبلت في الأصح وترد شهادة عاقلة بفسق شهود قتل وغرماء

مفلس بفسق وشهودا دين آخر.
# ولو شهدا لاثنين بوصية فشهدا للشاهدين بوصية من تلك التركة قبلت

الشهادتان في الأصح ولا تقبل لأصل ولا فرع وتقبل عليهما وكذا على أبيهما

بطلاق ضرة أمهما أو قذفها في الأظهر وإذا شهد لفرع وأجنبي قبلت للأجنبي في

الأظهر.
# قلت: وتقبل لكل من الزوجين ولأخ وصديق والله أعلم ولا تقبل من عدو وهو من

يبغضه بحيث يتمنى زوال نعمته ويحزن بسروره ويفرح بمصيبته وتقبل له وكذا

عليه في عدواة دين ككافر ومبتدع وتقبل شهادة مبتدع لا نكفره لا مغفل لا

يضبط ولا مبادر وتقبل شهادة الحسبة في حقوق الله تعالى وفيما له فيه حق

مؤكد كطلاق وعتق وعفو عن قصاص وبقاء عدة وانقضائها وحد له.
# وكذا النسب على الصحيح ومتى حكم بالشاهدين فبانا كافرين أو عبدين أو

صبيين نقضه هو وغيره. وكذا فاسقان في الأظهر ولو شهد كافر أو عبد وصبي ثم

- Root: ع د و (ʿ-d-w)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Transgression, passing beyond a limit; contagion as the passing of disease from one to another.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): ʿAdwā as the divinely-ordained transmission of harm, distinct from independent natural causation.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal (ḥaqīqah) in legal context; metaphorical (majāz) if implying autonomous agency of the disease.
- Root: ق س م (q-s-m)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Division, apportionment, distribution into shares (aṣḥāb al-qisma).
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Qisma as equitable allotment of joint property, a juridical act requiring justice (ʿadl).
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal for physical partitioning; metaphorical for abstract allocation of rights.
- Root: ش ه د (sh-h-d)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Presence, witnessing, giving testimony; shāhid as one who attests.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Shahādah as legal attestation grounded in certainty (yaqīn), not conjecture.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal for oral testimony; metaphorical for divine witnessing (shahādat Allāh).
- Sībawayh Rule: Conditional Clauses (al-Sharṭ wa al-Jawāb) — Governing the protasis (e.g., "if they all request") and apodosis ("the judge does not compel"), with precise modal sequencing.
chapters.translation:
I say: Contagion (al-ʿadwā) is only [that from which one] has not returned early at night, and the woman who is veiled (al-mukhaddarah) does not attend, she being one who does not frequently go out for needs.

#

| Chapter on Partition (al-Qisma)

Know that partition may be executed by the partners themselves, or by one appointed by them, or by one appointed by the Imam. The condition for the Imam's appointee is that he be a free, just man who knows surveying and calculation. If valuation (taqwīm) is involved, two appraisers are required; otherwise, one divider suffices, though in one saying [there must be] two. The Imam may appoint the divider as an arbiter in valuation, who then acts with two just witnesses, and divides. The Imam assigns the sustenance of his appointee from the public treasury (bayt al-māl); if there is none, his fee falls upon the partners. If they hire him and each specifies a sum, it is binding; otherwise, the fee is distributed proportionally to the shares, and in one saying, per capita. Then, whatever is greatly harmed by its division—such as a precious jewel, two valuable garments, or a pair of socks—if all the partners request its division, the judge does not compel them [to divide], nor does he prevent them if they divide it among themselves, provided its utility is not destroyed, like a sword that would break. And whatever loses its intended benefit—such as a small bathhouse or mill—the one requesting its division is not compelled [to accept refusal] in the soundest view (al-aṣaḥḥ). If it is possible to make it into two bathhouses, he is granted [his request]. If one has a tenth of a house unsuitable for dwelling and another has the rest, the soundest view is that the owner of the tenth is compelled at the request of the other, not the reverse. What is not greatly harmed by division is of several types:

First: Division by parts (al-ajzāʾ)—such as fungible goods (mithlī) or a house with uniform structures and land of similar parts. The one who refuses is compelled. The shares are equalized by measure, weight, or length, according to the number of portions if they are equal. In each lot (ruqʿah), the name of a partner is written, or a distinct part is marked by a boundary or direction. These are placed in equal balls (banādiq), then the one absent draws a lot for the first part—if names were written, the one whose name emerges is given [that part]; or upon the name of Zayd if the parts were written. If the portions differ—like half, third, and sixth—the land is divided into the least common shares and partitioned as above, taking care not to scatter the share of a single person.

Second: Division by equalization (al-taʿdīl)—such as land whose parts vary in value due to fertility of growth or proximity to water. One is compelled to accept it in the apparent view (al-aẓhar). If two houses or two shops are equal in value, and one requests that each be given to one [partner], there is no compulsion. Likewise, slaves or garments of a single type compel [acceptance], but of two types, no.

Third: Division by return (al-radd)—where on one side there is a well or trees that cannot be divided; the one who takes it returns the equivalent of its value. There is no compulsion in this, and it is a sale (bayʿ). Likewise, equalization (taʿdīl) is [a sale] in the school (al-madhhab), while division by parts is a mere segregation (ifrāz) in the apparent view.

In al-radd, consent is required after the lot is drawn. If two parties agree to a division in which there is no compulsion, consent after the lot is required in the soundest view—such as their saying, "We are satisfied with this division" or "with what the lot produced." If error (ghalaṭ) or injustice (ḥayf) in a compulsory division is established by evidence, it is annulled. If there is no evidence and one claims it, he may administer an oath to his partner. If he claims it in a consensual division, and we hold it is a sale, the soundest view is that error has no effect, so this claim has no benefit.

I say: If we hold it is segregation (ifrāz), it is annulled if established; otherwise, his partner is sworn. And Allah knows best. If some of the divided property is rightfully claimed (istihqāq) as an undivided share, the division is void; regarding the remainder, there is a dispute over separating the description or from the two shares—whether specific, if it remains [intact], [it stands]; otherwise, it is void. And Allah knows best.

#

| Book of Testimonies (al-Shahādāt)

The conditions for a witness are: Muslim, free, legally accountable (mukallaf), just (ʿadl), possessing probity (murūʾah), and not suspect (mut taham). The condition of justice is avoiding major sins (kabāʾir) and not persisting in minor ones. Playing with dice (nard) is unlawful in the sound view; chess (shaṭranj) is disliked. If money is staked by both sides, it is gambling (qimār). Chanting (ḥudāʾ) and listening to it are permissible. Singing (ghināʾ) without an instrument and listening to it are disliked. Using an instrument characteristic of the dissolute—like the ṭunbūr, ʿūd, ṣanj, and Iraqi mizmār—is unlawful, and causing it to be heard is not considered [a violation] in the soundest view.

I say: The soundest view is that it is unlawful. And Allah knows best. The duff (tambourine) is permissible for a wedding and circumcision, and likewise for other occasions in the soundest view, even if it has jingles (jalājil). Striking the kūbah—a long drum narrow in the middle—is unlawful. Not dancing, unless it involves effeminate contortions like the act of a mukhan nth. Reciting poetry and declaiming it is permissible, unless it satirizes (hijāʾ), is obscene, or alludes to a specific woman. Murūʾah is diminished by acting like one's peers in his time and place. Thus, eating in the market, walking bareheaded, kissing one's wife or slave-girl in public, excessive telling of amusing anecdotes, a jurist wearing a qabāʾ and cap where it is not customary, persisting in playing chess or singing or listening to it, and continual dancing—these diminish it. The matter varies by persons, circumstances, and places. A base profession—like cupping (ḥijāmah), sweeping, or tanning—for one to whom it is unbefitting diminishes it; if he is accustomed to it and it was his father's trade, then no, in the soundest view. Suspect status (tuhmah) is that he draws benefit to himself or repels harm from himself. Thus, his testimony is rejected for his slave, his mukātab, his debtor who is dead or under guardianship, and not for what he is an agent over, nor for the discharge of one he guaranteed, nor for the injury of his testator. If he testifies for his testator who is ill or wounded regarding property before recovery, it is accepted in the soundest view. The testimony of the ʿāqilah (kinship group) is rejected regarding the immorality of witnesses to homicide, and of creditors of an insolvent regarding immorality, and of witnesses to another debt.

If two testify for two [legatees] regarding a bequest, then they testify for the two witnesses regarding a bequest from that same estate, both testimonies are accepted in the soundest view. Testimony is not accepted for an ascendant or descendant, but it is accepted against them. Likewise, against their father regarding the divorce of their mother's co-wife (ḍarrah) or her slander (qadhf), in the apparent view. If one testifies for a descendant and a stranger, it is accepted for the stranger in the apparent view.

I say: It is accepted for each of the spouses, and for a brother and a friend. And Allah knows best. It is not accepted from an enemy—one who hates him to the extent of wishing the removal of his blessing, grieves at his joy, and rejoices at his misfortune. It is accepted for him, and likewise against him, in enmity of religion—like a disbeliever or innovator (mubtadiʿ). The testimony of an innovator whom we do not declare a disbeliever is accepted, but not of one who is negligent (mughaffal) who does not retain [accurately], nor one who is hasty. The testimony of the ḥisbah (public official) is accepted in the rights of Allah Almighty, and in matters where he has a confirmed right—like divorce, manumission, pardon for retribution (qaṣāṣ), the continuance of the ʿiddah and its completion, and a prescribed punishment (ḥadd) due to him. Likewise, lineage (nasab) in the sound view. When a ruling is made on two witnesses, and they turn out to be disbelievers, slaves, or minors, the judge and others annul it. Likewise, two immoral persons in the apparent view. If a disbeliever, slave, or minor testifies, then...

chapters.title_en: Section 112 — On the Acceptance of Testimony After Repentance, the Conditions of Witnesses, and the Bearing and Delivery of Testimony
chapters.arabic_text:
أعادها بعد كماله قبلت أو فاسق تاب فلا  وتقبل شهادة غيرها بشرط اختباره بعد

التوبة مدة يظن بها صدق توبته وقدرها الأكثرون بسنة ويشترط في توبة معصية

قولية القول فيقول القاذف قذفي باطل وأنا نادم عليه لا أعود إليه وكذا

شهادة الزور.
# قلت: وغير القولية يشترط إقلاع وندم وعزم أن لا يعود ورد ظلامه آدمي إن

تعلقت به. والله أعلم.
#

# فصل
# لا يحكم بشاهد إلا في هلال رمضان في الأظهر ويشترط للزنا أربعة رجال

وللإقرار به اثنان وفي قول أربعة ولمال وعقد مالي كبيع وإقالة وحوالة وضمان

وحق مالي كخيار وأجل رجلان أو رجل وامرأتان ولغير ذلك من عقوبة الله تعالى

أو لآدمي وما يطلع عليه رجال غالبا كنكاح وطلاق ورجعة وإسلام وردة وجرح

وتعديل وموت وإعسار ووكالة ووصاية وشهادة على شهادة رجلان وما يختص بمعرفته

النساء أو لا يراه رجال غالبا كبكارة وولادة وحيض ورضاع وعيوب تحت الثياب

يثبت بما سبق وبأربع سنوة وما لا يثبت برجل وامرأتين لا يثبت برجل ويمين

وما ثبت بهم ثبت برجل ويمين إلا عيوب النساء ونحوها ولا يثبت شيء بامرأتين

ويمين وإنما يحلف المدعي بعد شهادة شاهده وتعديله ويذكر في حلفه صدق الشاهد

فإن ترك الحلف وطلب يمين خصمه فله ذلك فإن نكل فله أن يحلف يمين الرد في

الأظهر. ولو كان بيده أمة وولدها فقال رجل هذه مستولدتي علقت بهذا في ملكي

وحلف مع شاهد ثبت الإستيلاد لا نسب الولد وحريته في الأظهر.
# ولو كان بيده غلام فقال رجل كان لي وأعتقته وحلف مع شاهد فالمذهب انتزاعه

ومصيره حرا ولو ادعت ورثة مالا لمورثهم وأقاموا شاهدا وحلف معه بعضهم أخذ

نصيبه ولا يشارك فيه ويبطل حق من لم يحلف بنكوله إن حضر وهو كامل فإن كان

غائبا أو صبيا أو مجنونا
# 
# فالمذهب أنه لا يقبض نصيبه فإذا زال عذره حلف وأخذ بغير إعادة شهادة ولا

تجوز شهادة على فعل كربا وغصب وإتلاف وولادة إلا بالأبصار وتقبل من أصم

والأقوال كعقد يشترط سمعها وإبصار قائلها ولا يقبل أعمى إلا أن يقر  في أذنه

فيتعلق به حتى يشهد عند قاض به على الصحيح ولو حملها بصير ثم عمى شهد إن

كان المشهود له وعليه معروفي الاسم والنسب ومن سمع قول شخص أو رأى فعله فإن

عرف عينه واسمه ونسبه شهد عليه في حضوره إشارة وعند غيبته وموته باسمه فإن

جهلهما لم يشهد عند موته وغيبته ولا يصح تحمل شهادة على منتقبة اعتمادا على

صوتها فإن عرفها بعينها أو باسم ونسب جاز ويشهد عند الأداء بما يعلم ولا

يجوز التحمل عليها بتعريف عدل أو عدلين على الأشهر والعمل على خلافه.
# ولو قامت بينة على عينه بحق فطلب المدعي التسجيل سجل القاضي بالحلية لا

الاسم والنسب ما لم يثبتا وله الشهادة بالتسامع على نسب من أبيه وقبيله

وكذا أم في الأصح وموت على المذهب لا عتق وولاء ووقف ونكاح وملك في الأصح.
# قلت: الأصح عند المحققين والأكثرين في الجميع الجواز والله أعلم وشرط

التسامع سماعه من جمع يؤمن تواطؤهم على الكذب وقيل: يكفي من عدلين ولا تجوز

الشهادة على ملك بمجرد يد ولا بيد وتصرف في مدة قصيرة وتجوز في طويلة في

الأصح وشرطه تصرف ملاك من سكنى وهدم وبناء وبيع ورهن وتبني شهادة الإعسار

على قرائن ومخائل الضر والإضافة.
#

# فصل
# تحمل الشهادة فرض كفاية في النكاح وكذا الإقرار والتصرف المالي وكتابة

الصك في الأصح وإذا لم يكن في القضية إلا اثنان لزمهما الأداء فلو أدى واحد

وامتنع الآخر وقال احلف معه عصى وإن كان شهود فالأداء فرض كفاية فلو طولب

من اثنين لزمهما في الأصح وإن لم يكن إلا واحد لزمه إن كان فيما يثبت بشاهد

ويمين وإلا فلا وقيل: لا يلزم الأداء إلا من تحمل قصدا لا اتفاقا ولوجوب

الأداء شروط أن يدعي من مسافة العدوى وقيل: دون مسافة قصر وأن يكون عدلا

فإن ادعى ذو فسق مجمع عليه قيل: أو مختلف فيه لم يجب وأن لا يكون معذورا

بمرض ونحوه فإن كان أشهد على شهادته أو بعث القاضي من يسمعها.
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ع-و-د (ʿ-w-d)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Return, reversion to a prior state; repetition of an act.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In legal-theological context, denotes the moral reversion to sin after repentance, and by extension the re-establishment of probity (ʿadālah) after sincere tawbah.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal (ḥaqīqah) for physical return; metaphorical (majāz) for the restoration of legal standing before God and the court.
- Root: ق-ب-ل (q-b-l)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To accept, receive, admit; antonym of rejection (radd).
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Technical term for judicial acceptance of testimony (qabūl al-shahādah), contingent on the witness's moral and legal competence.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal for taking something offered; metaphorical for the court's validation of a legal claim.
- Root: ش-ه-د (sh-h-d)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To witness, attest, be present; bearing testimony (taḥammul) and delivering it (adāʾ).
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): The act of declaring what one has perceived (bi-ʿilm) before a judge; a collective obligation (farḍ kifāyah) in specific cases.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal for ocular/auricular perception; metaphorical for legal attestation based on established knowledge.
- Root: ت-و-ب (t-w-b)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To turn back, repent; cessation from sin with resolve.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Repentance (tawbah) as the composite of cessation (iqlāʿ), remorse (nadam), and resolve (ʿazm) not to return; its legal effect is the restoration of testimonial capacity.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal for turning from a path; metaphorical for moral and juridical rehabilitation.
- Sībawayh Rule: Conditional Clause with Ellipsis (al-Sharṭ wa-l-Jawāb bi-Ḥadhf) — The phrase "فلا تقبل" (so it is not accepted) functions as the apodosis of a suppressed protasis, requiring the reader to supply the condition (e.g., 'if she returns to it after completion'), a structure frequent in legal maxims for brevity.
chapters.translation:
I say: If she (the woman) repeats it (the accusation) after its completion (of the prescribed punishment), whether she was a free woman or a sinful one who has repented, it is not accepted. And the testimony of other than her (i.e., other than the one who committed qadhf) is accepted, on the condition of testing him after the repentance for a period by which the truthfulness of his repentance is presumed; the majority of scholars estimated it as one year. And it is required in the repentance of a verbal sin (such as) the utterance — so the one who commits qadhf must say: 'My accusation (qadhf) is false, and I am remorseful over it, and I shall not return to it.' Likewise (is required) for false testimony (shahādat al-zūr).

I say: And for non-verbal (sins), it is required to cease (iqlāʿ), feel remorse (nadam), and resolve (ʿazm) not to return, and to restore the right of any human being (ādamī) if it is attached to it. And God knows best.

CHAPTER
A judge does not rule on the basis of a single witness except in (the matter of) the crescent of Ramaḍān, according to the more apparent (al-aẓhar) opinion. And for (the crime of) fornication (zinā), four men are required; and for confession to it, two men — and in one saying, four. And for property and financial contracts, such as sale (bayʿ), rescission (iqālah), transfer of debt (ḥiwālah), and surety (ḍamān), and financial rights, such as the option (khiyār) and the deferred term (ajal) — two men, or one man and two women. And for other than that, whether it be a punishment of God the Exalted or (a right) of a human being, and (matters) which men generally come to know, such as marriage (nikāḥ), divorce (ṭalāq), revocation (rujʿah), conversion to Islam (islām), apostasy (riddah), disparagement (jarḥ) and accreditation (taʿdīl) of witnesses, death (mawt), insolvency (iʿsār), agency (wakālah), executorship (waṣiyyah), and testimony upon testimony — two men. And what is exclusively known by women, or which men generally do not see, such as virginity (bakārah), childbirth (wilādah), menstruation (ḥayḍ), suckling (riḍāʿ), and defects beneath the garments — it is established by what has preceded (i.e., one man and two women) and by four women. And what is not established by one man and two women is not established by one man and an oath. And what is established by them (i.e., two men or one man and two women) is established by one man and an oath, except the defects of women and the like. And nothing is established by two women and an oath. And the plaintiff (muddaʿī) only takes an oath after the testimony of his witness and his accreditation (taʿdīl), and he mentions in his oath the truthfulness of the witness. If he abandons the oath and requests the oath of his opponent, he may do so. If (the opponent) refuses (nukūl), he may take the oath of rebuttal (yamīn al-radd), according to the more apparent opinion. And if a man had in his possession a slave-girl (umm walad) and her child, and another man said: 'This is my umm walad; she conceived this child while in my ownership,' and he took an oath with a witness, the status of umm walad (istīlād) is established, but not the lineage (nasab) of the child nor his freedom, according to the more apparent opinion.

And if a man had in his possession a young male slave (ghulām), and another man said: 'He was mine and I freed him,' and he took an oath with a witness, then the school (madhhab) holds that he is taken away (from the possessor) and becomes free. And if the heirs of a deceased claim property for their testator, and they produce a single witness, and one of them takes an oath with him, he takes his share, and no one shares with him in it; and the right of the one who does not take the oath is voided by his refusal (nukūl) if he is present and legally competent (kāmil). But if he is absent, or a minor, or insane, then the school holds that his share is not taken (for him); when his impediment is removed, he takes the oath and takes (his share) without repeating the testimony. And testimony is not permissible regarding an act (fiʿl), such as usury (ribā), usurpation (ghaṣb), destruction (itlāf), and childbirth, except by direct sight (ibṣār). And it is accepted from a deaf person (for such acts). And (testimony regarding) statements (aqwāl), such as contracts, requires hearing them and seeing the speaker. And a blind person is not accepted (as a witness), except that if (the statement) is recited in his ear, it becomes attached to him (as knowledge), such that he may testify upon it before a judge, according to the sound (al-ṣaḥīḥ) opinion. And if a sighted person bore testimony (taḥammala) and then became blind, he may testify if the one for whom and against whom the testimony is given are known to him by name and lineage. And whoever hears a person's statement or sees his act — if he knows his person (ʿayn), name, and lineage, he testifies against him in his presence by pointing (ishārah), and in his absence and after his death by name. If he is ignorant of both (name and lineage), he does not testify after his death or in his absence. And it is not valid to bear testimony regarding a veiled woman (muntaqibah) relying on her voice; if he knows her by her person, or by name and lineage, it is permissible. And he testifies at the time of delivery (adāʾ) according to what he knows. And it is not permissible to bear testimony regarding her based on the identification (taʿrīf) of one just person (ʿadl) or two just persons, according to the most famous (al-ashhar) opinion — though practice (al-ʿamal) is contrary to it.

And if evidence (bayyinah) is established regarding his person (ʿayn) for a right, and the plaintiff requests the court record (tasjīl), the judge records the physical description (ḥilyah), not the name and lineage, unless both are established. And one may testify by hearsay (tasāmuʿ) regarding lineage from one's father and his tribe, and likewise (from) the mother, according to the most sound (al-aṣaḥḥ) opinion; and regarding death, according to the school (madhhab); but not regarding emancipation (ʿitq), clientage (walāʾ), endowment (waqf), marriage (nikāḥ), or ownership (milk), according to the most sound opinion.

I say: The most sound opinion according to the verifying scholars (al-muḥaqqiqīn) and the majority (al-aktharīn) is that it is permissible in all of these. And God knows best. And the condition of hearsay (tasāmuʿ) is that he hears it from a group whose collusion upon falsehood is deemed impossible (yūman tawāṭuʾuhum ʿalā al-kadhib); and it was said: two just witnesses suffice. And testimony regarding ownership is not permissible based on mere possession (yad) alone, nor by possession and disposition (taṣarruf) over a short period; but it is permissible over a long period, according to the most sound opinion. And its condition is the disposition of owners (taṣarruf al-mullāk), such as dwelling (suknā), demolition (hadm), construction (bināʾ), sale (bayʿ), and pledge (rahn). And testimony of insolvency (iʿsār) is built upon indications (qarāʾin) and signs of distress (makhāʾil al-ḍurr) and need (iḍāfah).

CHAPTER
Bearing testimony (taḥammul al-shahādah) is a collective obligation (farḍ kifāyah) in (the matter of) marriage, and likewise (in) confession (iqrār) and financial dispositions (taṣarruf mālī), and the writing of legal documents (kitābat al-ṣakk), according to the most sound opinion. And if there are only two (witnesses) in a case, delivery (al-adāʾ) is incumbent upon both of them; if one delivers and the other refuses, saying: 'Take the oath with him,' he has sinned (ʿaṣā). And if there are many witnesses, delivery is a collective obligation; if two are demanded (to testify), it is incumbent upon them, according to the most sound opinion. And if there is only one, it is incumbent upon him if it is a matter established by one witness and an oath; otherwise, no. And it was said: delivery is not obligatory except upon one who bore testimony intentionally (qaṣdan), not incidentally (ittifāqan). And for the obligation of delivery there are conditions: that the claimant (yadʿī) be within the distance permitting attendance (masāfat al-ʿadwā) — and it was said: less than the distance permitting shortening of prayer (qasr) — and that (the witness) be just (ʿadl); for if a person of established sinfulness (fisq) claims (testimony), — and it was said: or of disputed sinfulness — it is not obligatory. And that he not be excused by illness or the like; if he is (so excused), he may appoint (ashhada) someone to bear testimony on his behalf, or the judge may send someone to hear it.

chapters.arabic_text:
# فصل 
# تقبل الشهادة على الشهادة في غير عقوبة وفي عقوبة الآدمي على المذهب

وتحملها بان يسترعيه فيقول أنا شاهد بكذا وأشهدك أو أشهد على شهادتي أو

يسمعه يشهد عند قاض أو يقول أشهد أن لفلان على فلان ألفا عن ثمن مبيع أو

غيره وفي هذا وجه ولا يكفي سماع قوله لفلان على فلان كذا أو أشهد بكذا أو

عندي شهادة بكذا وليبين الفرع عند الأداء جهة التحمل فإن لم يبن ووثق

القاضي بعلمه فلا بأس ولا يصح التحمل على شهادة مردود الشهادة ولا تحمل

النسوة فإن مات الأصل أو غاب أو مرض لم يمنع شهادة الفرع وإن حدث ردة أو

فسق أو عداوة منعت وجنونه كموته على الصحيح ولو تحمل فرع فاسق أو عبد فأدى

وهو كامل قبلت ويكفي شهادة اثنين على الشاهدين وفي قول يشترط لكل رجل أو

امرأة اثنان وشرط قبولها تعذر أو تعسر الأصيل بموت أو عمى أو مرض يشق
# 
# حضوره أو غيبة لمسافة عدوى وقيل: قصر وأن يسمى الأصول ولا يشترط أن

يزكيهم الفروع فإن زكوهم ولو شهدوا على شهادة عدلين أو عدول ولم يسموهم لم

يجز.

# فصل
# رجعوا عن الشهادة قبل الحكم امتنع أو بعده وقبل استيفاء مال استوفى أو

عقوبة فلا أو بعده لم ينقض فإن كان المستوفى قصاصا أو قتل ردة أو رجم زنا

أو جلده ومات وقالوا تعمدنا فعليهم قصاص أودية مغلظة وعلى القاضي قصاص إن

قال تعمدت وإن رجع هو وهم فعلى الجميع قصاص إن قالوا تعمدنا فإن قالوا

أخطأنا فعليه نصف دية وعليهم نصف ولو رجع مزك فالأصح أنه يضمن أو ولي وحده

فعليه قصاص أو دية أو مع الشهود فكذلك.
# وقيل: هو وهم شكراء ولو شهدا بطلاق بائن أو رضاع أو لعان وفرق القاضي

فرجعا دام الفراق وعليهم طلاق مثل وفي قول نصفه إن كان قبل وطء ولو شهدا

بطلاق وفرق فرجعا فقامت بينة أنه كان بينهما رضاع فلا غرم ولو رجع شهود مال

غرموا في الأظهر ومتى رجعوا كلهم  وزع عليهم الغرم أو بعضهم وبقي نصاب فلا

غرم وقيل: يغرم قسطه وإن نقص النصاب ولم تزد الشهود عليه فقسط وإن زاد فقسط

من النصاب.
# وقيل: من العدد وإن شهد رجل وامرأتان فعليه نصف وهما نصف أو أربع في رضاع

فعليه ثلث وهن ثلثان فإن رجع هو أو ثنتان فلا غرم في الأصح وإن شهد هو

وأربع بمال فقيل: كرضاع والأصح هو نصف وهن نصف سواء رجعن معه أو وحدهن وإن

رجع ثنتان فالأصح لا غرم وأن شهود إحصان أو صفة مع شهود تعليق طلاق وعتق لا

يغرمون.
# 

| كتاب الدعوى والبينات
# تشترط الدعوى عند قاض في عقوبة كقصاص وقذف وإن استحق عينا فله أخذها إن

لم يخف فتنة وإلا وجب الرفع إلى قاض أو دينا على غير ممتنع من الأداء طالبه

ولا يحل أخذ شيء له أو على منكر ولا بينة أخذ جنس حقه من ماله وكذا غير

جنسه إن فقده على المذهب أو على مقر ممتنع أو منكر وله بينة فكذلك وقيل:

يجب الرفع إلى قاض وإذا جاز الأخذ فله كسر باب ونقب جدار لا يصل المال إلا

به ثم المأخوذ من جنسه يتملكه ومن غيره يبيعه وقيل: يجب رفعه إلى قاض يبيعه

والمأخوذ مضمون عليه في الأصح فيضمنه إن تلف قبل تملكه وبيعه ولا يأخذ فوق

حقه إن أمكن الاقتصار وله أخذ مال غريم غريمه والأظهر أن المدعي من يخالف

قوله الظاهر والمدعى عليه من يوافقه فإذا أسلم زوجان قبل وطء فقال أسلمنا

مع فالنكاح باق وقالت مرتبا فهو مدع ومتى ادعى نقدا اشترط بيان جنس ونوع

وقدر وصحة وتكسر إن اختلفت بهما قيمته أو عينا تنضبط كحيوان وصفها بصفة

السلم.
# وقيل: يجب معها ذكر القيمة فإن تلفت وهي متقومة وجب ذكر القيمة أو نكاحا

لم يكف الإطلاق على الأصح بل يقول نكحتها بولي مرشد وشاهدي عدل ورضاها إن

كان يشترط فإن كانت أمة فالأصح وجوب ذكر العجز عن طول وخوف عنت أو عقدا

ماليا كبيع وهبة كفى 
# 
# الإطلاق في الأصح ومن قامت عليه بينة ليس له تحليف المدعي فإن ادعى أداء

أو إبراء أو شراء عين أو هبتها وإقباضها حلفه على نفيه وكذا لو ادعى علمه

بفسق شاهده أو كذبه في الأصح وإذا استمهل ليأتي بدافع أمهل ثلاثة أيام ولو

ادعى رق بالغ فقال أنا حر فالقول قوله أو رق صغير ليس في يده لم يقبل إلا

ببينة أو في يده حكم له به إن لم يعرف استنادها إلى التقاط فلو أنكر الصغير

وهو مميز فإنكاره لغو وقيل: كبالغ ولا تسمع دعوى دين مؤجل في الأصح.
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ش-ه-د (sh-h-d)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Presence, witnessing, giving testimony; the act of being present and attesting to a matter.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Bearing witness as a legal act of establishing truth (ḥaqq) in judicial contexts; testimony (shahādah) as a means of verifying claims.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal (ḥaqīqah) — physical presence and attestation; metaphorical (majāz) — transmission of testimony (shahādah ʿalā al-shahādah) as a delegated act.
- Root: ح-م-ل (ḥ-m-l)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To carry, bear, or transmit; assuming a burden or responsibility.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Carrying testimony (taḥammul) as the reception and conveyance of a witnessed fact to a court.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal — physical carrying; metaphorical — bearing legal responsibility or transmitting testimony.
- Root: ر-ج-ع (r-j-ʿ)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To return, revert, or retract; turning back from a position.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Retraction (rujūʿ) of testimony as a moral and legal reversal, affecting liability.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal — physical return; metaphorical — withdrawal of a legal statement.
- Sībawayh Rule: Conditional and Exceptive Constructions (al-sharṭ wa al-istithnāʾ) — Parsing of conditional clauses (e.g., "if they retract... then...") and exceptions (e.g., "except in cases of...") to determine legal outcomes based on stated conditions.
chapters.translation:
I say: Know that testimony upon testimony (shahādah ʿalā al-shahādah) is accepted in matters other than prescribed punishments (ḥudūd) and in punishments pertaining to a human claimant (ḥuqūq al-ādamī) according to the relied-upon school (al-madhhab).

Its transmission (taḥammul) is valid when the primary witness (al-aṣl) requests the secondary witness (al-farʿ) to bear it, saying: "I am a witness to such-and-such, and I make you a witness," or "I bear witness upon my testimony," or when the secondary witness hears the primary witness testifying before a judge, or when the primary witness says: "I bear witness that so-and-so owes so-and-so a thousand [dirhams] for the price of a sale or otherwise." In this last case there is a valid opinion (wajh). It is not sufficient merely to hear him say: "So-and-so owes so-and-so such-and-such," or "I bear witness to such-and-such," or "I have testimony of such-and-such." The secondary witness must, at the time of rendering testimony, clarify the manner of transmission (jihat al-taḥammul). If he does not clarify it, but the judge is confident of his knowledge, there is no harm. Transmission is not valid from a witness whose testimony is rejected (mardūd al-shahādah), nor from women transmitting testimony. If the primary witness dies, becomes absent, or falls ill, this does not prevent the secondary witness from testifying. However, if the primary witness commits apostasy (riddah), becomes corrupt (fisq), or enmity arises, this prevents [the secondary's testimony]. His insanity is like his death according to the soundest opinion (al-ṣaḥīḥ). If a corrupt (fāsiq) or slave secondary witness transmits testimony, then renders it while fully qualified, it is accepted. Two witnesses testifying upon two primary witnesses suffice. In one opinion, two witnesses are required for each man or woman [primary witness]. The condition for its acceptance is that the primary witness is unavailable or his presence is difficult due to death, blindness, or illness that makes his attendance burdensome, or absence at a distance requiring travel (masāfat al-ʿadwā); it is said: even a short distance. The primary witnesses must be named. It is not required that the secondary witnesses certify their integrity (tazkiyah). If they do certify them, even if they testify upon the testimony of two just witnesses or several just witnesses without naming them, it is not permissible.

Section: If the witnesses retract their testimony before the judge's ruling, [the ruling] is prevented; if after the ruling but before the execution of a financial claim, it is executed; if after execution, it is not overturned. If what was executed was retaliation (qiṣāṣ), or execution for apostasy, or stoning for adultery, or flogging [for slander] and the [punished person] died, and the witnesses say: "We intended deliberately," then upon them is retaliation or heavy blood-money (diyah mughallaẓah). Upon the judge is retaliation if he says: "I acted deliberately." If the judge retracts along with them, then upon all is retaliation if they say: "We intended deliberately." If they say: "We erred," then upon the judge is half the blood-money, and upon them half. If a certifier of integrity (muzakkī) retracts, the soundest opinion is that he is liable. If a guardian (walī) alone retracts, upon him is retaliation or blood-money; if he retracts along with the witnesses, likewise. It is said: he is like a partner in liability. If two witnesses testify to an irrevocable divorce (ṭalāq bāʾin), or fosterage (riḍāʿ), or imprecation (liʿān), and the judge separates [the spouses], then they retract, the separation remains, and upon them is a divorce like it; in one opinion, half of it if it was before consummation. If two witnesses testify to a divorce, and [the judge] separates, then they retract, and evidence is established that there was fosterage between them, then no financial liability. If witnesses of a financial claim retract, they are liable in the apparent opinion (al-aẓhar). Whenever all of them retract, the liability is distributed among them. If some retract and the remaining number still constitutes a full complement (niṣāb), there is no liability. It is said: the retractor pays his share. If the number falls below the complement, and the remaining witnesses do not exceed [the retractors], then [the retractor pays] his share; if they exceed, then his share from the complement. It is said: from the total number. If a man and two women testify, then upon the man is half and upon the two women half. If four women testify in a case of fosterage, upon the man is one-third and upon them two-thirds. If the man retracts or two of the women retract, there is no liability in the soundest opinion. If a man and four women testify to a financial claim, it is said: like fosterage; the soundest opinion is that the man pays half and they pay half, whether they retract with him or alone. If two of them retract, the soundest opinion is no liability. Witnesses to [a prior] marriage (iḥṣān) or to a quality [of the claim], along with witnesses to a suspended divorce or manumission, do not incur liability.

| The Book of Claims and Evidence (Kitāb al-Daʿwā wa al-Bayyināt)

A claim before a judge is required in cases of punishment, such as retaliation and slander (qadhf). If one is entitled to a specific property, he may take it himself if he does not fear discord (fitnah); otherwise, he must raise the matter to a judge. If it is a debt owed by one who is not refusing payment, he may demand it. It is not lawful to take anything of his own from a denier (munkir) without evidence. He may take the equivalent of his right from the denier's property, and likewise a non-equivalent if the equivalent is unavailable, according to the relied-upon school. If [the debtor] is an acknowledging refuser (muqirr mumtaniʿ) or a denier, and he has evidence, likewise; it is said: he must raise it to a judge. When taking is permissible, he may break a door or breach a wall if he cannot access the property otherwise. Then, what is taken, if it is of the same type [as his right], he owns it; if of another type, he sells it. It is said: he must raise it to a judge to sell it. What is taken is a trust in his possession in the soundest opinion, so he is liable for it if it perishes before he owns or sells it. He may not take more than his right if he can limit himself. He may take the property of his debtor's debtor. The apparent opinion is that the claimant (al-muddaʿī) is the one whose statement contradicts the apparent state of affairs, and the defendant (al-muddaʿā ʿalayhi) is the one whose statement aligns with it. Thus, if two spouses convert to Islam before consummation, and the husband says: "We converted together, so the marriage remains," and the wife says: "We converted sequentially," then he is the claimant. Whenever one claims a debt (naqd), he must specify its genus (jins), type (nawʿ), amount (qadr), soundness (ṣiḥḥah), and minting (kasar) if value differs by it. If claiming a specific item that can be described, like an animal, he must describe it with the description required in salam contracts. It is said: he must also mention its value; if it perishes and it is a valuable item, mentioning the value is obligatory. If claiming a marriage, mere generality is not sufficient in the soundest opinion; rather, he must say: "I married her with a guardian (walī), two just witnesses, and her consent," if consent is required. If she is a slave-woman, the soundest opinion is that he must mention the inability to afford a free woman and the fear of fornication (ʿanat). If claiming a financial contract, like a sale or gift, generality suffices in the soundest opinion. If evidence is established against someone, the claimant is not to be put under oath. If the defendant claims payment, release (ibrāʾ), purchase of the item, or its gift and delivery, he is put under oath denying it. Likewise, if he claims knowledge of his witness's corruption or falsehood, in the soundest opinion. If he requests a delay to bring a defense, he is granted three days. If one claims the slavery of an adult, and the adult says: "I am free," then his statement is accepted. If claiming the slavery of a minor not in his possession, it is not accepted without evidence. If the minor is in his possession, judgment is given for him unless it is known that the possession originated from picking up a foundling (iltiqāṭ). If the minor, being discerning (mumayyiz), denies [the claim], his denial is void; it is said: like an adult. A claim for a deferred debt is not heard in the soundest opinion.

# فصل
# أصر المدعى عليه على السكوت عن جواب الدعوى جعل كمنكر ناكل فإن ادعى عشرة

فقال لا تلزمني العشرة لم يكف حتى يقول ولا بعضها وكذا يحلف فإن حلف على

نفي العشرة واقتصر عليه فناكل فيحلف المدعي على استحقاق دون عشرة بجزء

ويأخذه وإذا ادعى مالا مضافا إلى سبب كأقرضتك كذا كفاه في الجواب لا تستحق

علي شيئا أو شفعة كفاه لا تستحق علي شيئا أو لا تستحق تسلم الشقص ويحلف على

حسب جوابه هذا فإن أجاب بنفي السبب المذكور حلف عليه.
# وقيل: له حلف بالنفي المطلق ولو كان بيده مرهون أو مكرى وادعاه مالكه

كفاه لا يلزمني تسليمه فلو اعترف بالملك وادعى الرهن والإجارة فالصحيح أنه

لا يقبل إلا ببينة فإن عجز عنها وخاف أولا إن اعترف بالملك مجده الرهن وإلا

جاز فحيلته أن يقول إن ادعيت ملكا مطلقا فلا يلزمني تسليم وإن ادعيت مرهونا

فاذكره لأجيب وإذا ادعى عليه عينا
# 
# فقال ليس هي لي أو هي لرجل لا أعرفه أو لابني الطفل أو وقف على الفقراء

أو مسجد كذا في الأصح أنه لا تنصرف الخصومة ولا تنزع منه بل يحلفه المدعي

أنه لا يلزمه التسليم إن لم تكن بينة وإن أقر به لمعين حاضر يمكن مخاصمته

وتحليفه سئل فإن صدقه صارت الخصومة معه وإن كذبه ترك في يد المقر وقيل:

يسلم إلى المدعي وقيل: يحفظه الحاكم لظهور مالك وإن  أقر به لغائب فالأصح

انصراف الخصومة عنه ويوقف الأمر حتى يقدم الغائب فإن كان للمدعي بينة قضى

بها وهو قضاء على غائب فيحلف معه وقيل: على حاضر وما قبل إقرار عبد به

كعقوبة فالدعوى عليه وعليه الجواب ومالا كأرش فعلى السيد.

# فصل
# تغلظ يمين مدع ومدعى عليه فيما ليس بمال ولا يقصد به مال وفي مال يبلغ

نصاب زكاة وسبق بيان التغليظ في اللعان ويحلف على البت في فعله وكذا فعل

غيره إن كان إثباتا وإن كان نفيا فعلى نفي العلم ولو ادعى دينا لمورثه فقال

أبرأني حلف على نفي العلم بالبراءة ولو قال جنى عبدك علي بما يوجب كذا

فالأصح حلفه على البت.
# قلت: ولو قال جنت بهيمتك حلف على البت قطعا والله أعلم ويجوز البت بظن

مؤكد يعتمد خطه أو خط أبيه وتعتبر نية القاضي المستحلف فلو ورى أو تأول

خلافها أواستثنى بحيث لا يسمع القاضي لم يدفع إثم اليمين الفاجرة ومن توجهت

عليه يمين لو أقر بمطلوبها لزمه فأنكر حلف ولا يحلف قاض على تركه الظلم في

حكمه ولا شاهد أنه لم يكذب ولو قال مدعى عليه أنا صبي لم يحلف ووقف حتى

يبلغ واليمين تفيد قطع الخصومة في الحال لا براءة فلو حلفه ثم أقام بينة

حكم بها ولو قال المدعى عليه قد حلفني مرة فليحلف أنه لم يحلفني مكن في

الأصح وإذا نكل حلف المدعي وقضى له ولا يقضي
# 
# بنكوله والنكول أن يقول أنا ناكل أو يقول له القاضي احلف فيقول لا أحلف

فإن سكت حكم القاضي بنكوله وقوله للمدعي احلف حكم بنكوله واليمين المردودة

في قوله كبينة وفي الأظهر كإقرار المدعى عليه فلو أقام المدعى عليه بعدها

بينة بأداء أو إبراء لم تسمع فإن لم يحلف المدعي ولم يتعلل بشيء سقط حقه من

اليمين وليس له مطالبة الخصم وإن تعلل بإقامة بينة أو مراجعة حساب أمهل

ثلاثة أيام وقيل: أبدا وإن استمهل المدعى عليه حين استحلف لينظر حسابه لم

يمهل وقيل: ثلاثة ولو استمهل  في ابتداء الجواب أمهل إلى آخر المجلس ومن

طولب بزكاة فادعى دفعها إلى ساع آخر أو غلط خارص وألزمناه اليمين فنكل

وتعذر رد اليمين فالأصح أنها تؤخذ منه ولو ادعى ولى صبي دينا له فأنكر ونكل

لم يحلف المولي وقيل: يحلف وقيل: إن ادعى مباشرة سببه حلف.

- Root: ن-ك-ل (n-k-l)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Refusal, abstention, shrinking from a matter; the act of declining an oath.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Technical legal term for the defendant's refusal to swear, triggering the oath's return to the plaintiff.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal in judicial procedure; metaphorical extension to any refusal of a binding claim.
- Root: خ-ص-م (kh-ṣ-m)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Dispute, contention; the two parties in litigation.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): The formal adversarial relationship in a claim (daʿwā), requiring a direct respondent.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal for courtroom confrontation; metaphorical for any opposing argument.
- Root: ب-ت-ت (b-t-t)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Cutting decisively; finality, certainty.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): The oath of definitive knowledge (ʿalā al-batt) vs. oath of negating knowledge (ʿalā nafy al-ʿilm).
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal for categorical affirmation; metaphorical for absolute legal finality.
- Sībawayh Rule: Conditional Clause Ellipsis (Ḥadhf al-Jawāʾ) — The protasis "if he claims ten" governs an implied apodosis, requiring the response to negate the entirety, not merely the aggregate.
chapters.translation:
I say: If the defendant persists in silence, refusing to answer the claim, he is treated as a denier who has declined the oath (nākil). For if the plaintiff claims ten [dirhams] and he says, "The ten are not incumbent upon me," this is insufficient until he adds, "nor any part thereof." Likewise, he must swear [to this full negation]. If he swears only to the negation of the ten and confines himself to that, he is [still] a nākil, so the plaintiff swears to his entitlement to a portion less than ten and takes it.

When the claim concerns property (māl) attributed to a specific cause — such as "I lent you such-and-such" — it suffices for him to answer, "You have no right against me to anything," or for a preemption claim (shufʿa), it suffices to say, "You have no right against me to anything," or "You have no right to receive the share delivered," and he swears according to this response of his. If he answers by denying the mentioned cause, he swears upon that [denial]. And it is said: he may swear an absolute negation.

If property is in his hand as a pledge (marhūn) or leased (mukrā) and its owner claims it, it suffices for him to say, "Delivery of it is not incumbent upon me." But if he acknowledges ownership and claims the pledge or lease, the sounder position (al-ṣaḥīḥ) is that this is not accepted without evidence (bayyina). If he lacks evidence and fears [loss] — either he acknowledges ownership and loses the pledge, or otherwise — his stratagem is to say: "If you claim absolute ownership, delivery is not incumbent upon me; but if you claim it is pledged, then mention that, and I shall answer."

When a specific chattel (ʿayn) is claimed against him and he says, "It is not mine," or "It belongs to a man I do not know," or "to my infant son," or "it is a waqf for the poor," or "for such-and-such mosque" — in the sounder position, the litigation does not turn away from him, nor is it seized from his hand. Rather, the plaintiff swears him that delivery is not incumbent upon him, if there is no evidence. If he acknowledges it for a specific present person who can be sued and sworn, he is asked [to confirm]. If that person affirms him, the litigation shifts to him; if he denies him, it is left in the hands of the acknowledger. It is said: it is handed to the plaintiff. It is said: the judge preserves it until the owner appears. If he acknowledges it for an absent person, the sounder position is that the litigation turns away from him, and the matter is suspended until the absent one arrives. If the plaintiff has evidence, judgment is rendered by it — and this is a judgment against an absent party, so he swears alongside it. It is said: [the oath is] upon the present one. Whatever is accepted from a slave's acknowledgment — such as a penal sanction (ʿuqūba) — the claim is against him and he must answer; but property (māl), such as damages (arsh), is upon the master.

I say: The oath is made solemn (taghlīẓ) for both plaintiff and defendant in matters that are not property and are not intended for property, and in property reaching the zakāt threshold (niṣāb). The solemnity in the mutual curse (liʿān) has been explained previously. He swears with categorical certainty (ʿalā al-batt) regarding his own act, and likewise regarding another's act if it is affirmative (ithbāt). If it is negative (nafy), he swears upon negation of knowledge. If he claims a debt owed to his testator and the defendant says, "He discharged me," he swears upon negation of knowledge of the discharge. If he says, "Your slave inflicted upon me an injury entailing such-and-such," the sounder position is that he swears with categorical certainty.

I say: If he says, "Your beast caused harm," he swears with categorical certainty, absolutely. And Allah knows best. Categorical certainty is permissible based on strong presumption (ẓann muʾakkad), such as relying upon one's own handwriting or one's father's handwriting. The intention of the judge administering the oath is considered. If the swearer equivocates (warā) or interprets (taʾwīl) contrary to it, or makes an exception (istithnāʾ) inaudible to the judge, this does not repel the sin of the perjured oath (yamīn fājira). Whoever is obligated to swear — such that if he confessed to what is demanded, it would bind him — and he denies, must swear. A judge does not swear that he will not commit injustice in his ruling, nor a witness that he has not lied.

If the defendant says, "I am a minor," he does not swear, and the matter is suspended until he reaches maturity. The oath effects the termination of the litigation (qaṭʿ al-khuṣūma) at that moment, not acquittal (barāʾa). Thus, if he swears him and then evidence is produced, judgment is rendered by it. If the defendant says, "He has already sworn me once," he must swear that he did not swear him — this is permitted in the sounder position.

When he declines the oath (nakala), the plaintiff swears and judgment is given for him; judgment is not given merely by the declination itself. The declination (nukūl) is that he says, "I decline," or the judge says to him, "Swear," and he says, "I will not swear." If he remains silent, the judge rules his declination; and his saying to the plaintiff, "Swear," is ruled as his declination. The returned oath (al-yamīn al-mardūda) in his [the defendant's] statement is like evidence (bayyina), and in the more manifest position (al-aẓhar) like an acknowledgment by the defendant. Thus, if the defendant thereafter produces evidence of payment or discharge, it is not heard. If the plaintiff does not swear and offers no excuse, his right to the oath lapses, and he has no further claim against the opponent. If he offers an excuse — such as producing evidence or reviewing accounts — he is granted a three-day respite; it is said: indefinitely. If the defendant requests a delay when the oath is demanded of him to review his accounts, he is not granted it; it is said: three days. If he requests a delay at the outset of his answer, he is granted until the end of the session.

Whoever is demanded for zakāt and claims he paid it to another collector, or that the assessor (khāriṣ) erred, and we oblige him to swear, and he declines, and the return of the oath is impossible — the sounder position is that it is taken from him. If the guardian of an orphan claims a debt owed to him, and the defendant denies and declines, the guardian does not swear; it is said: he swears; it is said: if he claims direct causation of the debt, he swears.
